chapters.title: Chapter 401: First Evolution III
paragraphs: Lian started looking at his panel from the top and decided to check all the changes step by step.
The Class had not changed and was still Monster, his Race was still Human, but all three of his main Talents had changed.
Dormant Monster was no longer there, Heir of Winter had been upgraded, and Mother of Colony had also turned into something different.
He opened the first Talent, which was his most important Talent.
[Fallen Monster]
[Evolutionary Talent.]
[All Normal Monsters are subject to the holder’s racial superiority.]
[Overall combat capability of Normal Monsters is suppressed by up to 20% in the holder’s presence.]
[Suppression ignores level difference.]
Lian raised an eyebrow, this part was very important, if a Normal Monster was ten levels higher than him, it would still be affected.
Twenty levels? The suppression would still work.
As long as it was in the "Normal" tier, the level difference could not remove his racial superiority.
If his guess was correct, true Fallen Monsters should also have this ability, so could this be one of the reasons for their superiority over Normal Monsters?
[Normal Monsters instinctively recognize the holder as a greater existence.]
[Instinctive fear will be induced.]
[Targets will attempt to avoid direct confrontation whenever possible.]
This alone could completely change the way he moved through the Ruined Realm, many weaker Monsters might not even be willing to approach him.
But the explanations were not finished.
[Fallen Monster muscular structure acquired.]
[Muscle density and contraction efficiency greatly increased.]
[Skeletal density increased.]
[Joint and connective tissue durability increased.]
[Monster Core formation unlocked.]
[The holder can observe the level of any Monster regardless of level difference.]
He opened the second Talent.
[Child of Frost has evolved.]
[New Talent: Heir of Winter.]
[Rank: A.]
He looked at the ice on the floor, so the reason for that reaction was clear and it was related to his evolved Talent.
[Frost affinity: +80%.]
[Learning and utilization efficiency of Frost-based elements: +80%.]
[The holder will not perceive natural or supernatural cold below an extremely high threshold.]
[Ice-aligned Monsters are suppressed by up to 30% against the holder.]
[In frozen environments, offensive Frost skills power increases by up to 10%.]
[Mana consumption of all Frost-based abilities reduced by 30%.]

He stared at the messages for several seconds, eighty percent higher Frost affinity, thirty percent lower Mana consumption, thirty percent suppression against Ice Monsters and increased power in cold environments.
This was not just a numerical increase, from now on, every Frost skill he obtained would be much more valuable to him.
One of his main skills, Glacial Reaper Claw, was also a Frost skill and now with the help of his Talent it would become even stronger and more useful than before.
The satisfaction in his eyes was obvious.
Then the third Talent.
[Mother of Colony has evolved.]
[New Talent: Colony Sovereign.]
[Rank: S.]
He read this one more carefully.
[Maximum Colony Members: 100.]
[Maximum Special Members: 5.]
The number one hundred alone was a huge increase but the next part was even more interesting.
[Special Members can temporarily borrow a portion of the Sovereign’s power during emergencies.]
[Maximum borrowed power: 30% of the Sovereign’s current power.]
[Borrowed power is temporary.]
[Transfer requires direct authorization or a preconfigured emergency condition.]
Lian could not help but think of One, if One became a Special Member, in a dangerous situation he could receive thirty percent of Lian’s current power as a temporary boost.
And as Lian continued to grow, this thirty percent would also become greater.
Five Special Members and one hundred Colony Members.
This Talent was no longer simply designed to connect him with a companion creature, it could become the foundation of a real force.
After finishing the Talents, his eyes moved toward the Innate Skills, these were the abilities that formed the main foundation of his power and the main reason for his growth.
[Glutton has evolved.]
[Glutton → Greater Glutton.]
[Activation probability after killing a Monster has increased.]
[Skill extraction remains more likely than Talent extraction.]
[When Skill extraction activates, up to three extractable Skills from the target will be displayed.]
[The holder may choose one Skill.]
[Extraction activation remains probability-based.]
[The holder cannot force activation on every kill.]
The corner of Lian’s mouth rose, this change was really good, before, if Glutton activated, he did not have much choice over what he received.
Now if a Monster had several Skills, the system would give him up to three options and he could choose one himself.
Of course, Glutton still had to activate first and there was no guarantee, and the chance of getting a Talent was still lower than getting a Skill.
Because of this, the ability was still not completely controllable.
But even with this weakness, he was still satisfied.
[Bloodlust has evolved.]
[Bloodlust → Greater Bloodlust.]
[Experience gained from killed Monsters: 150%.]
[If the target is at least 10 levels above the holder: 200% Experience.]
"The more dangerous, the better." Lian whispered with satisfaction, this rule fit perfectly with the way he had grown until now.
He had never gained much from Monsters at his own level or weaker Monsters and had always been forced to go after stronger Monsters.
And now because of his crazy way of doing things, he could get even greater rewards.
Of course, a difference of ten levels or more was still not small.
Then the next notification appeared.
[Butcher has evolved.]
[Butcher → Greater Butcher.]
This time he sat completely straight and paid even more attention, this Innate Skill was his most important source of stat growth and was considered his most important ability until now.
[After killing a Normal Monster, up to 5% of the target’s absorbable Stats can be transferred to the holder.]
For a moment, he only looked at the number.
Five percent!
Before, it had been one percent and now it had become five times higher, with that one percent he had managed to create a huge gap between himself and the Awakened of his age.
And now five percent?
His thoughts returned to the ten thousand stat limit, reaching that number and even going beyond it no longer seemed unreasonable.
However, the System was still not finished.
[Special Rule: Fallen Monsters.]
[When a Fallen Monster is killed completely solo, up to 20% of its absorbable Stats may be transferred.]
[Activation is probability-based.]
[Activation probability rises as the target’s level approaches or exceeds the holder’s level.]
Lian slowly breathed out, he could obtain twenty percent of the Stats of a Fallen Monster but unfortunately it was "probability-based" and required him to kill it alone.
Then the final section appeared.
[Superior Monster Hunt Rule.]
[Unholy.]
[Demon.]
[Supreme.]
[When a target from one of the above tiers is defeated completely solo, up to 100% of its absorbable Stats may be transferred.]
[Requirement: No other entity may directly contribute to defeating the target.]
[All transferred Stats remain subject to the current Evolution Stat Limit.]
He said nothing for several seconds.
One hundred percent.
If he completely defeated an Unholy, Demon or Supreme Monster alone, he could obtain all of its absorbable Stats.

Of course, the final condition prevented the System from becoming completely crazy, the ten thousand limit still existed and he could not suddenly gain hundreds of thousands of points by killing one strange creature.
"Well..." Lian stared at the panel for several seconds and his smile became wider, he was very satisfied with the evolution of Glutton.
[Ice Resistance removed.]
[Ice Control removed.]
[Both abilities have evolved and merged.]
[New Innate Skill acquired.]
[Frost Dominion]
[Extremely high resistance against natural and magical cold.]
[Control over existing ice within a maximum radius of 10 kilometers.]
[Actual control range depends on Spirit, Mana, and power difference.]
[The holder can create ice from nothing by consuming Mana.]
[The holder can alter the shape, density, and structure of controlled ice.]
[Enemy-created ice can be seized if the holder possesses sufficient superiority in Spirit or Strength.]
He calmly looked at the ice on the floor and simply willed it, suddenly a line of ice rose from the ground.
It wrapped around the leg of the chair like a thin snake and then turned into a clear blade.
Lian moved his finger and the blade immediately changed shape and turned into dozens of small needles.
He had not activated any separate Skill to create them.
Just simple control.
"Ten kilometers..."
Of course, the actual range in a fight would probably depend on the situation, but even a small part of ten kilometers was still a huge number.
And more importantly, Skills like Eternal Frozen Apocalypse and Glacial Reaper Claw would now be under a much more powerful Frost Talent.
And another important upgrade was that before, he could not create ice from nothing and had to be in an icy environment, but that weakness no longer existed.
[Hive Link has evolved.]
[New Innate Skill acquired.]
[Hive Dominion]
This time he immediately became serious again, because this Innate Skill was very important and might help him summon One.
[Members within the same world can sense one another within 100 kilometers.]
[Direct Command unlocked.]
[Colony House unlocked.]
[You can place all members of your Colony inside a dimensional space, similar to a Storage Space.]
[You can summon all Colony Members that are inside the Colony House.]
[Special Member Summoning unlocked.]
His eyes stayed on the final line... finally.
[Special Member Summoning can bypass inter-world distance.]
[Summoning cost is calculated based on distance between worlds and destination resistance.]
[Target must be registered as a Special Member.]
He was silent for a few moments, One was alive and now he could bring him back, and he needed to check the cost and conditions.
But the path was open and he no longer needed to worry about the first member of his Colony.
[Natural Colony Hierarchy:]
[Sovereign]
[Queen]
[Commander]
[Worker]
[Authority Classification:]
[Special Member]
[Normal Member]
He quickly understood the difference, the first ranking was based on the natural structure and power of the Colony creatures.
A Queen, Commander or Worker, each of them ranked based on their power.
But the second ranking was something Lian himself decided.
A Colony Member could naturally be a Commander and at the same time be registered as a Normal Member.
Or it could also be only a Worker but be registered as a Special Member and receive the benefits of being a Special Member.
Then his eyes fell on the final Innate Skill.
[True Sequence]
Its name had not changed and at first he thought that maybe it had not evolved at all.
But then he opened the explanation and realized that he was wrong.

chapters.title: Chapter 402: First Evolution IV
paragraphs: [True Sequence]
[The complete structure of an observed Skill can now be analyzed.]
[Mana route, activation pattern, initiation point, peak point, and structural instability can be identified.]
[Existing structural weaknesses will be displayed to the holder.]
[Possible methods of interruption, redirection, neutralization, and counteraction will be calculated.]
[Analysis time depends on Skill complexity and rank.]
[ increases spiritual defense and sense of identity by 150%, and enhances resistance against attacks that target the user’s identity and existence ]
[ All mental attacks below the third evolution are reduced by 50% ]
This was a major change.
True Sequence no longer only learned movements and patterns, it could dissect a Skill.
If a magic skill needed Mana to pass through three points to activate, it could find the weakest point.
If a Skill became unstable for a short moment before being released, the Skill would show it.
If there was a way to redirect it, its method would be suggested.
"This is better than I thought." He said with serious satisfaction.
Among all his innate skills, it had been the least useful and least valuable one before the evolution, but now, with the changes it had gone through, this might change.
"I guess I have seen all the changes." He thought for a moment, he had checked everything that had evolved.
And now it was time to check the new parts of the system.
[Traits]
Lian focused on it, as far as he knew about this new section, they were a type of secondary booster, traits that affected his main abilities.
And five names appeared.
[Skill Overdrive]
[Level: 0/10]
[Level 1 Effect: Skill power increased by 10% for 10 seconds.]
[Each additional level adds +10% Skill power and +10 seconds duration.]
Level ten would increase Skill power by one hundred percent for one hundred seconds, almost one minute and forty seconds.
For Divine-level Skills, it was terrifying and could make a very big difference.
He opened the next one.
[Quick Mana]
[Level: 0/10]
[Each level increases Mana recovery speed by 10%.]

Level ten would basically make his normal Mana recovery speed twice as fast, simple but very useful, especially for him because there had been many times when he had run out of Mana in the middle of a battle.
[Lifesteal]
[Level: 0/10]
[Level 1: 1% activation chance per successful hit.]
[On activation, the holder restores an amount equal to 2% of damage inflicted.]
[Each level adds +1% activation chance and +2% restoration value.]
Lian calculated it for a few seconds.

Level ten had a ten percent activation chance and would restore twenty percent of the damage dealt as body recovery, in a long battle, especially against a Monster with a huge body, it could be the difference between surviving and dying.
Simply put, this trait helped him randomly recover part of the damage he had received in exchange for some of the attacks he landed.
In long and exhausting battles, it had a lot of use and could also make a very big difference.
[Force Spike]
[Level: 0/10]
[Level 1:]
[1% chance for an attack to gain +10% power.]
[Each level adds +1% activation chance and +10% bonus power.]
Level ten had a ten percent activation chance and one hundred percent more power.
That meant that about one out of every ten attacks could, on average, land with twice the power.
Of course, it was random.

Because of that, he could not build an exact battle plan around it, but if one of his heavy attacks activated it at the same time, the result could have a very major effect on the outcome of the battle.
And the last option.
[Natural Armor]
[Level: 0/10]
[Each level increases the body’s natural defensive power by 50%.]
Level ten would increase the body’s natural defense by five hundred percent.
And because this increase was applied directly to his body, Skills such as Diamond Skin would later work on a much stronger base.
A five hundred percent increase in the body’s defensive power was a very large number.
Lian returned to Skill Overdrive.
He pressed the upgrade button.
[Upgrade Cost — Level 1: 100 Fragments.]
He frowned.
"Only level one costs one hundred?" Lian said with dissatisfaction, this amount was very high, and that was only for one upgrade.
Naturally, every upgrade would cost more than the previous one and God knew how much would be needed to reach level ten.
He calculated it in his mind for a few moments, just bringing one trait to level ten required thousands of Fragments.
If he wanted to max out all five traits, the number would enter the tens of thousands.
This number was crazy, Fragments were not something that dropped from every Monster for sure and the chance of getting them was low.
Quests and powerful enemies were the main sources.
Now he understood why even among powerful Awakened, level ten Traits were considered rare.

It should be remembered that these were secondary boosts, and for the strongest Awakened, where even the smallest difference in power could decide the result of a battle and guarantee their advantage, these boosts were extremely important.
But it did not seem like maxing them would be easy or something that would happen anytime soon.
Of course, he also had one advantage, because of the Wolf Slayer title, he could get Fragments from any wolf-type Monster without exception.
It seemed that from now on, he had no choice but to hunt only wolves.
Then he went to the next section.
[Skill Fusion]
Skill Fusion was one of the most famous parts of the system among Awakened after their second evolution, because they could randomly obtain very powerful Skills from it.
There were even records of some people managing to obtain Skills with Holy potential through this method.
Lian opened it.
[Skill Fusion unlocked.]
[A minimum of 2 and a maximum of 3 Skills can be fused.]
[The resulting Skill will depend on rank, nature, compatibility, and structure of selected Skills.]
[Fusion requires Fragments.]
[Fragment cost varies based on input Skills.]
[Incompatible combinations will be rejected before payment.]
[After successful fusion, the original Skills will be permanently merged into the resulting Skill.]
For a moment, he thought about his list of Skills.
Thunder Step.
Fallen Wolf Speed.
Maybe combining those two completely different movement Skills could create something much more powerful and with greater potential.
Or his Frost Skills, or even combining a defensive Skill with a movement Skill, there were many possibilities but the problem was also obvious.
Fragments.
Everything now required Fragments.
"Looks like I need to take collecting Fragments more seriously from now on." Lian said with a quiet sigh.
Then he saw a section that immediately took all of his attention, this was not a normal section that every Awakened received after evolution.
This was a section that only he had.
[Ruined Heart]
[Available Seats: 5.]
[Completed Seats: 1.]
[Black Silence — Devoured.]
[Power Invocation unlocked.]
His eyes stayed on the last option and he opened it.
[Borrow the power of a devoured Calamity temporarily.]
[Current Invocation Duration: 30 seconds.]
[Available Calamity: Black Silence.]
[After invocation, the corresponding seat requires 24 hours to stabilize.]
Thirty seconds.
Only thirty seconds.
But if the system really meant the "power of Black Silence", even thirty seconds seemed more than enough.
He could borrow the power of a Calamity, the power of an existence that could drive worlds into madness.
Did this mean that he could now do the same...?
But he did not know how it worked or exactly what powers he would gain when he activated it, and he would not know until he actually used it.
But there was no need to rush, just being able to use the power of Black Silence now was already far beyond his expectations.
Then he moved on to the last section.
[Innate Traits Tree.]
[Class: Monster.]
This was also a section that all Awakened gained access to after their first evolution, but it was different from the normal Traits section.
Traits were general and the same for everyone without any difference.
But Innate Traits were different for every Awakened and completely depended on their evolved Class, and the Traits related to their Class were placed inside it.
When he opened it, eight locked branches appeared in front of him.
They all came out from one central point where the name "Monster" was placed.
And to unlock each branch, he needed to pay Fragments as expected... but the required cost was so high that his eyes widened when he saw it.
"You have to be kidding me? Fucking 4,500 Fragments?! for what?"

Simply put, this trait helped him randomly recover part of the damage he had received in exchange for some of the attacks he landed.
In long and exhausting battles, it had a lot of use and could also make a very big difference.
[Force Spike]
[Level: 0/10]
[Level 1:]
[1% chance for an attack to gain +10% power.]
[Each level adds +1% activation chance and +10% bonus power.]
Level ten had a ten percent activation chance and one hundred percent more power.
That meant that about one out of every ten attacks could, on average, land with twice the power.
Of course, it was random.

Because of that, he could not build an exact battle plan around it, but if one of his heavy attacks activated it at the same time, the result could have a very major effect on the outcome of the battle.
And the last option.
[Natural Armor]
[Level: 0/10]
[Each level increases the body’s natural defensive power by 50%.]
Level ten would increase the body’s natural defense by five hundred percent.
And because this increase was applied directly to his body, Skills such as Diamond Skin would later work on a much stronger base.
A five hundred percent increase in the body’s defensive power was a very large number.
Lian returned to Skill Overdrive.
He pressed the upgrade button.
[Upgrade Cost — Level 1: 100 Fragments.]
He frowned.
"Only level one costs one hundred?" Lian said with dissatisfaction, this amount was very high, and that was only for one upgrade.
Naturally, every upgrade would cost more than the previous one and God knew how much would be needed to reach level ten.
He calculated it in his mind for a few moments, just bringing one trait to level ten required thousands of Fragments.
If he wanted to max out all five traits, the number would enter the tens of thousands.
This number was crazy, Fragments were not something that dropped from every Monster for sure and the chance of getting them was low.
Quests and powerful enemies were the main sources.
Now he understood why even among powerful Awakened, level ten Traits were considered rare.

It should be remembered that these were secondary boosts, and for the strongest Awakened, where even the smallest difference in power could decide the result of a battle and guarantee their advantage, these boosts were extremely important.
But it did not seem like maxing them would be easy or something that would happen anytime soon.
Of course, he also had one advantage, because of the Wolf Slayer title, he could get Fragments from any wolf-type Monster without exception.
It seemed that from now on, he had no choice but to hunt only wolves.
Then he went to the next section.
[Skill Fusion]
Skill Fusion was one of the most famous parts of the system among Awakened after their second evolution, because they could randomly obtain very powerful Skills from it.
There were even records of some people managing to obtain Skills with Holy potential through this method.
Lian opened it.
[Skill Fusion unlocked.]
[A minimum of 2 and a maximum of 3 Skills can be fused.]
[The resulting Skill will depend on rank, nature, compatibility, and structure of selected Skills.]
[Fusion requires Fragments.]
[Fragment cost varies based on input Skills.]
[Incompatible combinations will be rejected before payment.]
[After successful fusion, the original Skills will be permanently merged into the resulting Skill.]
For a moment, he thought about his list of Skills.
Thunder Step.
Fallen Wolf Speed.
Maybe combining those two completely different movement Skills could create something much more powerful and with greater potential.
Or his Frost Skills, or even combining a defensive Skill with a movement Skill, there were many possibilities but the problem was also obvious.
Fragments.
Everything now required Fragments.
"Looks like I need to take collecting Fragments more seriously from now on." Lian said with a quiet sigh.
Then he saw a section that immediately took all of his attention, this was not a normal section that every Awakened received after evolution.
This was a section that only he had.
[Ruined Heart]
[Available Seats: 5.]
[Completed Seats: 1.]
[Black Silence — Devoured.]
[Power Invocation unlocked.]
His eyes stayed on the last option and he opened it.
[Borrow the power of a devoured Calamity temporarily.]
[Current Invocation Duration: 30 seconds.]
[Available Calamity: Black Silence.]
[After invocation, the corresponding seat requires 24 hours to stabilize.]
Thirty seconds.
Only thirty seconds.
But if the system really meant the "power of Black Silence", even thirty seconds seemed more than enough.
He could borrow the power of a Calamity, the power of an existence that could drive worlds into madness.
Did this mean that he could now do the same...?
But he did not know how it worked or exactly what powers he would gain when he activated it, and he would not know until he actually used it.
But there was no need to rush, just being able to use the power of Black Silence now was already far beyond his expectations.
Then he moved on to the last section.
[Innate Traits Tree.]
[Class: Monster.]
This was also a section that all Awakened gained access to after their first evolution, but it was different from the normal Traits section.
Traits were general and the same for everyone without any difference.
But Innate Traits were different for every Awakened and completely depended on their evolved Class, and the Traits related to their Class were placed inside it.
When he opened it, eight locked branches appeared in front of him.
They all came out from one central point where the name "Monster" was placed.
And to unlock each branch, he needed to pay Fragments as expected... but the required cost was so high that his eyes widened when he saw it.
"You have to be kidding me?
Fucking 4,500 Fragments?! for what?"

chapters.title: Chapter 403: First Evolution ( Final )
paragraphs: Lian remained completely silent, he did not have access to the Innate Traits and could not even see their descriptions.
However, he could see the cost required to unlock them, although he could only see the cost of the first one and needed to unlock them step by step to see the next ones.
And the first Innate Trait cost 4,500 Fragments!
This was insanely expensive, what the hell was the first Innate Trait to have such a ridiculously high price?
And if this was only the first one, how many Fragments would he need to unlock the rest?
Would he ever be able to collect enough Fragments to unlock all eight of his Innate Traits?
Even he had doubts about it.
This did not mean that Innate Traits were expensive for every Awakened, these Traits were related to each person’s class and because of that, they had different costs depending on their class.
So, an ordinary Awakened might only need to pay around one hundred Fragments for their first Innate Trait.
"Don’t you think they’re a little too cheap?" Lian said to the system with dry sarcasm.
Naturally, there was no answer.
But this tree made one thing completely clear, from this point on, Fragments were almost as important as levels and stats.
Maybe even more.
"I’ve checked everything, it’s as good as I expected." He then took another general look at the panel.
He had checked all the newly added sections and all the changes, and had become completely familiar with his First Evolution.
Some things were within his expectations and some were even beyond them.
The thing that satisfied him the most was the Ruined Heart and the fact that he could now borrow the power of Black Silence.
And the thing that confused him was that his class was still called Monster, his class had not evolved at all and his instincts told him that there was a major reason behind it.
But he did not know exactly why.
Finally, he closed the panel and opened the rewards section.
[Main Quest Rewards delivered.]
[100 Fragments.]
[250 Free Stat Points.]
[Treasure Chest ×1.]
[Highest Contribution Reward.]
[Golden Treasure Chest ×1.]
Lian’s eyes lit up slightly.
A Golden Chest.
Considering what he had done to get it, he expected it to contain something valuable.

Treasure Chests were chests that the system sometimes gave for very special Quests and they could contain almost anything, Artifacts, Skill Books, treasures, weapons, and all kinds of special resources and...
They were divided into four ranks, Normal Treasure Chest, Special Treasure Chest, Purple Treasure Chest, and finally Golden Treasure Chest.

The higher the rank of the Treasure Chest, the more valuable the thing inside would naturally be, but Golden Treasure Chests were extremely rare and were only given as rewards under special conditions.
He put the normal chest aside first and then selected the Golden Chest.
[Open Golden Treasure Chest?]
[Yes / No.]
"Yes." He said without hesitation.
A golden chest appeared in front of him, floating in the air, and then its lock opened by itself.
Golden light came out so strongly that the entire room was completely lit up for a moment.
Lian instinctively narrowed his eyes slightly, the light slowly faded and something appeared in the palm of his hand.
A small fruit, almost the size of a walnut, with a white skin and very thin golden lines moving across its surface.
And Lian only looked at it for a few seconds.
A panel appeared.
[Return Fruit — Mythical]
[Type: Consumable.]
[Upon consumption, the holder gains one Stored Life.]
[Upon death, if the holder’s soul has not been completely destroyed, automatic reconstruction of body and soul will begin.]
[Maximum Stored Lives: 1.]
[The effect becomes permanently bound to the holder after consumption.]
Lian looked at the fruit, this was the same thing he had just consumed or at least something with an almost similar effect but a different structure.
An Extra Life.
The reason he was sitting in this room right now, if he had not had that life, Seris would have pierced his heart and everything would have ended right there.
He was truly surprised, he did not expect to obtain another Extra Life so soon and besides, he could either consume it himself or give it to anyone he wanted.
The corner of his lips slowly rose.
"Well...this one is actually a reward." It was a Mythical-rank Artifact.
The highest rank that existed among Artifacts and treasures, it was so valuable that by selling it he could earn tens of billions of dollars.
But since there was no reason to keep it, he ate it, it did not have any special taste and a moment later, a warm wave passed through the center of his chest.
[Spirit Return Fruit consumed.]
[Extra Life: 1.]
He looked at the message for a few seconds.
Another life, having it felt strange but he could not become careless, death was still painful and if his soul was completely destroyed, even this would not save him.
But having a second chance was not something he could take lightly.
Then another notification appeared.
[Title acquired.]
[Calamity Survivor.]
He opened the information.
[Increases resistance by 50% against overwhelming spiritual pressure generated by vastly superior entities.]
The effect was good, but it was not so strange that Lian stayed on it for more than a few seconds.
This was a Title given to all the Awakened who survived the Special Area and with its help they could resist spiritual attacks to a large degree.
But it did not create complete immunity and only increased spiritual and mental defense by 50%.
Then another panel appeared and this one had a purple and black border.
[You personally devoured a Calamity entity.]
[Unique Title acquired.]
[Calamity Devourer.]
[Calamity Devourer.]
[Unique Growth Title.]
[Innate racial fear and suppression generated by Calamity-class entities will not affect the holder.]
[Resistance to Calamity corruption, possession, spiritual erosion, and identity erasure: +25%.]
[Damage against Calamities, Anchors, Vessels, and direct Calamity-born entities: +10%.]
[The holder can perceive exposed Calamity presences and active vessels and anchors from greatly increased distances.]
[This Title can evolve.]
[Calamities Devoured: 1/5.]
[Each additional Calamity devoured will strengthen this Title.]
Lian remained completely silent for a few seconds.
One out of five, again five, the Ruined Heart had five seats, the Evolution Quest had talked about five Calamities and now even the new Title was following the same number.
This could no longer be a coincidence, the system or the Ruined Heart or both of them expected him to find and devour the rest of them as well.
For a moment, Lian remembered the image of the "Father" from Black Silence’s memories.
Five Calamities that were the children of that Father...would he eventually be forced to face that existence as well?
His expression became slightly more serious.
At least he was not going to look for it now, one of them had almost destroyed an entire world and had killed him once as well.
He still had a lot of work to do but now he knew what would be waiting for him in the future.
"In any case, this Title will make my job easier, I can find the Vessels and Anchors this way." He thought for a moment.

He knew that there was a very high chance that what had happened to their world was also related to one of the five Calamities and if that was true, then there should be both a Vessel and an Anchor in their world as well.
He planned to find both of them but he had no idea how, but now with the help of this Title he could find them.
In the end, he closed the system completely and put it aside and looked around.
Some time had passed since the Evolution ended, but the ice was still covering the floor of the room.
With a short thought, the ice collapsed, turned into very small particles and then slowly disappeared.
His control was much more natural than before even without any special training.
His mind returned to his giant ant, One was still in another world and he had to try to find a way to summon him as soon as possible.
He did not know One’s exact condition and only knew that he was still alive, but that did not make him feel relieved at all.
The situation in that graveyard was so chaotic that something could happen to his ant at any moment.
And the time for his summon was now...

chapters.title: Chapter 404: Welcome Back
paragraphs: Before doing anything else, Lian opened the system panel.
The blue light slowly appeared in front of his eyes and his gaze immediately stopped on one specific section.
[Hive Dominion]
One.
His most important goal right now was to summon the giant ant.
Of course, before summoning him, he had made some short preparations.
The last time he had seen One, the giant ant could not even stand, one of his legs was broken, the armor on his chest was crushed inward and part of one of his antennae was also gone.
If the summoning did not restore the target’s physical condition and One returned with exactly the same injuries, Lian preferred to be prepared beforehand.
So after washing his face and putting on his clothes, he left the inn.
Base #9 was crowded even in the early hours of the morning. Hunting groups were leaving one after another and stores made for Awakened had started working much earlier than normal stores.
He only spent a few minutes.
He bought several healing potions, bone-repair potions, and recovery potions from a trusted store and put all of them into his Storage Space.
Then he went directly to the area for mounts.
This part of the inn area was completely different from what he had seen nine months ago.
A large area had been built behind the main buildings, with several separate sections, large stables for ground creatures and high platforms for birds and flying monsters.
There were open cages with reinforced walls for more aggressive creatures.
There were even several small training fields where Awakened could train with their companions without disturbing normal people.
As Lian passed by, he saw a wolf almost three meters tall sleeping beside its owner.
Several meters away, a reptile covered in red scales was being kept inside a heated area and on one of the high platforms, a black bird with wings almost ten meters wide was sitting.
In a place like this, the appearance of a giant ant would probably only surprise a few people, rather than putting the entire base on alert.
He rented a private area at the farthest part.
It had tall stone walls and enough space even for a creature much larger than One.
Now he could begin.
[Hive Dominion]
[Eligible Special Member detected.]
[One]
[Register One as a Special Member?]
[Yes / No]
"Yes." He said without hesitation.
[Special Members: 1/5]
For a moment, something changed through the Link.
The same very weak connection that had been almost useless until now became a little clearer.
[Inter-world Summoning available.]
[Matter Origin: Unknown World — Graveyard of Giants]
[Destination: Tenth Ruined Realm]
[Summoning Cost: 300 Fragments]
He looked at the number for a few seconds.
Three hundred.
Then his own amount appeared below it.
[Available Fragments: 307]
[Fragments after Summoning: 7]
These were all the Fragments he had collected during almost his entire time in the Special Area and after killing all those monsters.
His face remained completely expressionless for a moment, he had only just realized how valuable Fragments had become from this stage onward.
Traits needed Fragments.
Skill Fusion needed Fragments.
His class’s Innate Traits Tree also required thousands of Fragments for even the simplest options.
Three hundred Fragments was almost everything he had right now.
"Seven?" Lian looked at the final number with a slight frown.
It hurt a lot but the image of One among the ruins of the graveyard appeared in his mind.
A creature that had refused to leave him even when his master’s body was being controlled by a Calamity.
He had almost gotten himself killed three times because of him.
Lian focused on the confirmation option.
"He’s worth it." Paying all three hundred Fragments was completely worth it for a creature like him.
[Confirm Inter-world Summoning?]
[Yes.]
[300 Fragments consumed.]
[Available Fragments: 7]
[Special Member Summoning has begun.]
[Stabilizing inter-world path...]
Nothing happened for a few seconds.
Lian simply stood there.
Then suddenly, the space in the center of the area bent for a moment, not like the huge rifts humans used to travel between worlds.
It was much smaller and darker, as if someone had grabbed part of the air and slowly twisted it.
A black circle the size of a fist appeared, then expanded.
One meter.
Two meters.
Three meters.
At that moment, Hive Dominion reacted.
He suddenly felt something, he felt the presence of a living creature far away!
A creature that was in pain and its pain was heavy and unclear, then came confusion and exhaustion, hopelessness and the fear that his master had abandoned him.
And exactly when the connection was completed, an emotion so clear passed through the Link that Lian became completely silent for a moment.
Master.
The rift opened and something huge fell out from the darkness.
Boom!
The ground shook under its weight and One’s huge body fell onto the ground.
As Lian expected, the summoning had not healed any of his injuries, one of his legs was still in a strange position.
The natural armor on his chest was crushed and the middle part had caved in, one of his antennae was cut in half and there were many cracks across his body shell.
But he was alive.
The rift behind him immediately closed and Lian once again had One in front of him.
One did not move for a few seconds, he probably did not even understand what had happened.
The last thing he remembered was the Graveyard of Giants.
The death of the Titan.
The battle.
The huge presence of the Calamity.
Then the humans had disappeared, his master had also left, he thought he had been abandoned...he thought that because he had been useless, he had been thrown away...
And now he was lying in a completely unknown place, his huge head slowly moved and his eyes first checked the surroundings.
Stone walls, an open ceiling, different air and then they stopped on Lian.
For a moment, no feeling came through the Link, there was complete silence as if he could not believe what he was seeing.
But then came disbelief.
The young Vorhelm felt it much more clearly than before, Hive Dominion was not just a simple connection.
One’s emotions were now almost reaching his mind like a direct wave, the disbelief lasted for one second and then turned into recognition.
And recognition turned into a wave of happiness so strong that Lian blinked without thinking.
Master.
This time it was not a weak feeling but almost a wordless scream.
And for several seconds he said nothing, to most people, One was just a strange monster.
A giant ant, a creature that could perhaps be used as a mount or a weapon.
But Lian had seen something else.
When Black Silence had taken control of his body, everyone else had at least been forced to wonder for a moment whether anything of him was still left inside that body.
One had never doubted it, he had crawled and used his half-dead body to reach that creature.
He had tried to contact him through the Hive Link and when he received no answer, he still did not back away.
He had remained loyal to him always and under every condition.
Lian walked forward and stood beside One’s huge head, then placed his hand on the healthy part of his head armor.
"Yeah, it’s me." And he said it in a calmer voice than usual.
One immediately tried to stand up, his healthy legs pushed against the ground, his body rose several centimeters but the broken leg could not support him and his body fell down again.
"Don’t move, idiot." Lian said with a slight frown and pressed his hand harder against One’s head.
A weak feeling of protest came back through the Link but his master looked at him for a few seconds.
"No." But his answer did not change, although the ant still wanted to stand up so he could lick his master and show his affection.
Lian opened his Storage Space and took out three strong healing potions.
One was more than enough for a normal human body, but One was several times larger than a human.
He opened the first bottle and poured some of it into One’s mouth and spread the rest over the broken part of his chest armor.
The green liquid immediately began to enter his body after touching it, then the second bottle was used for the broken leg and the third for the internal injuries.
[Healing effect detected.]
[Condition: Critical → Severe]
[Regeneration process initiated.]
He let out a quiet sigh of relief, at least he was no longer on the verge of death.
One slowly raised his head, this time he did not try to stand and only moved the side of his head closer to Lian’s hand.
The movement looked a little funny because of the size of his body but its meaning was completely clear.
Lian kept his hand there.
"Next time I tell you to run, you have to run, understand?" He added seriously.
The Link immediately reacted, loyalty, stubbornness and something close to completely rejecting that order, the giant ant refused to accept it, he would not run when his master was in danger!
The young Vorhelm became silent and looked at One for a few seconds, then sighed.
"...Forget it, I know you won’t listen."
One became calmer.
"Welcome back, One."
The giant ant could not be fully healed in a few minutes.
Some fractures and deep injuries needed at least several days, even with good potions.
Lian rented the area for a few more days.
The person in charge of the area stared at One’s huge body for a few seconds when he first saw him, but he quickly returned to his professional behavior.
At Base #9, a several-meter-tall ant might be strange, but it was no longer unbelievable.
Lian paid for the food, care, and daily checkups.
Before leaving, he sent a clear command through Hive Dominion.
[Rest.]
[Do not engage in combat unless directly threatened.]
Then he left the area.
His next destination was the medical center, it was time to meet the head of the student council of their academy.

Hunting groups were leaving one after another and stores made for Awakened had started working much earlier than normal stores.
He only spent a few minutes.
He bought several healing potions, bone-repair potions, and recovery potions from a trusted store and put all of them into his Storage Space.
Then he went directly to the area for mounts.
This part of the inn area was completely different from what he had seen nine months ago.
A large area had been built behind the main buildings, with several separate sections, large stables for ground creatures and high platforms for birds and flying monsters.
There were open cages with reinforced walls for more aggressive creatures.
There were even several small training fields where Awakened could train with their companions without disturbing normal people.
As Lian passed by, he saw a wolf almost three meters tall sleeping beside its owner.
Several meters away, a reptile covered in red scales was being kept inside a heated area and on one of the high platforms, a black bird with wings almost ten meters wide was sitting.
In a place like this, the appearance of a giant ant would probably only surprise a few people, rather than putting the entire base on alert.
He rented a private area at the farthest part.
It had tall stone walls and enough space even for a creature much larger than One.
Now he could begin.
[Hive Dominion]
[Eligible Special Member detected.]
[One]
[Register One as a Special Member?]
[Yes / No]
"Yes." He said without hesitation.
[Special Members: 1/5]
For a moment, something changed through the Link.
The same very weak connection that had been almost useless until now became a little clearer.
[Inter-world Summoning available.]
[Matter Origin: Unknown World — Graveyard of Giants]
[Destination: Tenth Ruined Realm]
[Summoning Cost: 300 Fragments]
He looked at the number for a few seconds.
Three hundred.
Then his own amount appeared below it.
[Available Fragments: 307]
[Fragments after Summoning: 7]
These were all the Fragments he had collected during almost his entire time in the Special Area and after killing all those monsters.
His face remained completely expressionless for a moment, he had only just realized how valuable Fragments had become from this stage onward.
Traits needed Fragments.
Skill Fusion needed Fragments.
His class’s Innate Traits Tree also required thousands of Fragments for even the simplest options.
Three hundred Fragments was almost everything he had right now.
"Seven?" Lian looked at the final number with a slight frown.
It hurt a lot but the image of One among the ruins of the graveyard appeared in his mind.
A creature that had refused to leave him even when his master’s body was being controlled by a Calamity.
He had almost gotten himself killed three times because of him.
Lian focused on the confirmation option.
"He’s worth it." Paying all three hundred Fragments was completely worth it for a creature like him.
[Confirm Inter-world Summoning?]
[Yes.]
[300 Fragments consumed.]
[Available Fragments: 7]
[Special Member Summoning has begun.]
[Stabilizing inter-world path...]
Nothing happened for a few seconds.
Lian simply stood there.
Then suddenly, the space in the center of the area bent for a moment, not like the huge rifts humans used to travel between worlds.
It was much smaller and darker, as if someone had grabbed part of the air and slowly twisted it.
A black circle the size of a fist appeared, then expanded.
One meter.
Two meters.
Three meters.
At that moment, Hive Dominion reacted.
He suddenly felt something, he felt the presence of a living creature far away!
A creature that was in pain and its pain was heavy and unclear, then came confusion and exhaustion, hopelessness and the fear that his master had abandoned him.
And exactly when the connection was completed, an emotion so clear passed through the Link that Lian became completely silent for a moment.
Master.
The rift opened and something huge fell out from the darkness.
Boom!
The ground shook under its weight and One’s huge body fell onto the ground.
As Lian expected, the summoning had not healed any of his injuries, one of his legs was still in a strange position.
The natural armor on his chest was crushed and the middle part had caved in, one of his antennae was cut in half and there were many cracks across his body shell.
But he was alive.
The rift behind him immediately closed and Lian once again had One in front of him.
One did not move for a few seconds, he probably did not even understand what had happened.
The last thing he remembered was the Graveyard of Giants.
The death of the Titan.
The battle.
The huge presence of the Calamity.
Then the humans had disappeared, his master had also left, he thought he had been abandoned...he thought that because he had been useless, he had been thrown away...
And now he was lying in a completely unknown place, his huge head slowly moved and his eyes first checked the surroundings.
Stone walls, an open ceiling, different air and then they stopped on Lian.
For a moment, no feeling came through the Link, there was complete silence as if he could not believe what he was seeing.
But then came disbelief.
The young Vorhelm felt it much more clearly than before, Hive Dominion was not just a simple connection.
One’s emotions were now almost reaching his mind like a direct wave, the disbelief lasted for one second and then turned into recognition.
And recognition turned into a wave of happiness so strong that Lian blinked without thinking.
Master.
This time it was not a weak feeling but almost a wordless scream.
And for several seconds he said nothing, to most people, One was just a strange monster.
A giant ant, a creature that could perhaps be used as a mount or a weapon.
But Lian had seen something else.
When Black Silence had taken control of his body, everyone else had at least been forced to wonder for a moment whether anything of him was still left inside that body.
One had never doubted it, he had crawled and used his half-dead body to reach that creature.
He had tried to contact him through the Hive Link and when he received no answer, he still did not back away.
He had remained loyal to him always and under every condition.
Lian walked forward and stood beside One’s huge head, then placed his hand on the healthy part of his head armor.
"Yeah, it’s me." And he said it in a calmer voice than usual.
One immediately tried to stand up, his healthy legs pushed against the ground, his body rose several centimeters but the broken leg could not support him and his body fell down again.
"Don’t move, idiot." Lian said with a slight frown and pressed his hand harder against One’s head.
A weak feeling of protest came back through the Link but his master looked at him for a few seconds.
"No." But his answer did not change, although the ant still wanted to stand up so he could lick his master and show his affection.
Lian opened his Storage Space and took out three strong healing potions.
One was more than enough for a normal human body, but One was several times larger than a human.
He opened the first bottle and poured some of it into One’s mouth and spread the rest over the broken part of his chest armor.
The green liquid immediately began to enter his body after touching it, then the second bottle was used for the broken leg and the third for the internal injuries.
[Healing effect detected.]
[Condition: Critical → Severe]
[Regeneration process initiated.]
He let out a quiet sigh of relief, at least he was no longer on the verge of death.
One slowly raised his head, this time he did not try to stand and only moved the side of his head closer to Lian’s hand.
The movement looked a little funny because of the size of his body but its meaning was completely clear.
Lian kept his hand there.
"Next time I tell you to run, you have to run, understand?" He added seriously.
The Link immediately reacted, loyalty, stubbornness and something close to completely rejecting that order, the giant ant refused to accept it, he would not run when his master was in danger!
The young Vorhelm became silent and looked at One for a few seconds, then sighed.
"...Forget it, I know you won’t listen."
One became calmer.
"Welcome back, One."
The giant ant could not be fully healed in a few minutes.
Some fractures and deep injuries needed at least several days, even with good potions.
Lian rented the area for a few more days.
The person in charge of the area stared at One’s huge body for a few seconds when he first saw him, but he quickly returned to his professional behavior.
At Base #9, a several-meter-tall ant might be strange, but it was no longer unbelievable.
Lian paid for the food, care, and daily checkups.
Before leaving, he sent a clear command through Hive Dominion.
[Rest.]
[Do not engage in combat unless directly threatened.]
Then he left the area.
His next destination was the medical center, it was time to meet the head of the student council of their academy.

chapters.title: Chapter 405: How Are You Alive!?
paragraphs: Rindo had regained consciousness the day before.
Lian got the room number from the reception and stood in front of the door a few minutes later.
He knocked twice and a tired voice came from inside.
"Come in."
He opened the door and the patient was half-sitting on the bed.
His left arm was completely wrapped in bandages and hanging from his shoulder.
There were several healed wounds on his face and part of his side was also covered with bandages.
But he was conscious and as soon as Lian entered, he only looked at him for several seconds.
From head to toe, clean clothes, a healthy body, completely normal movement and then back to his face.
"Every time I think nothing can surprise me anymore, you show up." For a moment, he even rubbed his eyes.
He tried to consider the possibility that he was seeing an illusion, but he was not in such bad condition that he would see an illusion like this.
To the point that a dead man appeared in front of him.
So there was only one possibility, that dead man was not actually dead.
"I’ll take that as a compliment." Lian closed the door. He answered calmly.
"It wasn’t a compliment."
"This is also one of those indirect compliments."
Rindo stared for several seconds and then only sighed, this was something he had to accept.
"How? How are you still alive? We were all sure you were dead! We even saw your death with our own eyes."
"Did you know the system sometimes gives something called an Extra Life as a Quest reward?" Lian answered with a smile.

The head of the Student Council did not answer immediately, of course he knew what an Extra Life was, it was not an unknown reward, but it was rare and it was not something an Awakened who had not even gone through his First Evolution could obtain.
So it was natural that he had not expected this boy to be hiding something like that.
"So you were playing with all of us from the beginning, huh?" And he let out a deeper sigh.
"I don’t call it playing, I wasn’t even sure if the Extra Life would work in that situation or not."

Rindo nodded, it was a good point, after all, it was a strange situation and there was no way to know if the Extra Life would actually work or not, but it still would have been better if he had at least told them that he had one so they would worry less about him and hesitate less to kill him.
The conversation became quiet for a few moments.
"The others?" Lian asked, he had come directly to check this boy’s condition because from the first day they returned, he had seen that he was one of those in the best condition.
So he guessed that he would wake up earlier than the others.
"Cassian seems to have just woken up, I think he will be allowed to leave the medical center from today, Selina is better, her main problems were Mana exhaustion and burns."
"Liana woke up this morning but Seraphina is still under treatment, but she is not in danger of dying."
Lian became a little calmer for a moment, fortunately, all the members of the group seemed to be safe, Marcus and Ethan were also in completely healthy condition.
However, the next words made him frown again.
"Seris still hasn’t woken up."
That girl had burned everything she had, half of her permanent Stats, her life force, her body and in the end she had been seriously injured, more than all of them.
But she should not be in a life-threatening condition and she would probably wake up sooner or later as well.
Lian himself had forced her to drive the sword through his heart and when she woke up, they would probably have an interesting conversation waiting for them.
"Darian?" Then he asked after thinking for a moment.

"I don’t know, I heard he was discharged earlier than everyone else, I don’t even know if he is in the base or not, and thats your brother, shouldn’t you know better?" Rindo did not show any special reaction to the change of subject.
Lian smirked, that bastard would probably leave the base soon, he might have already left the base and be on his way to report the failure of his mission to kill him.
"What about Aren? Do you have any new information about him?" The last information he had was that the man was also under treatment and after that he would be taken for interrogation.
This time Rindo became a little more serious.
"I don’t know exactly either, but I heard some things from some of the officers who came to interrogate me and you could say it’s complicated."

"He was in the medical center until a few hours ago but suddenly the officers took him away, I don’t know where they took him but it seems they took him to the same place where they took that other native of the Ruined Realm."
Lian said nothing, the image of Aren without both hands, standing beside the Forgotten Tree and all the help he had given to him and the others came to his mind.
If he had not been there, several of those who had returned would be dead now.

Rindo nodded, he was also aware of this, but there was nothing they could do, the other native of the Ruined Realm who had been captured by Lian had been taken by the Federation and Aren was the same.
This was not something they would easily let go when they could get a lot of information from him.
"I have a meeting with the base officials today, I’ll try to talk to them about this." The young Vorhelm said at the end.
Rindo looked at him for a few moments and then pointed at the table beside the bed where several reports were placed.
"I’ll write it in my report too."
Lian nodded, this way they might at least make sure that the Federation would not torture or violently interrogate Aren.
Both of them remained silent for a few moments and then the head of the Student Council suddenly said.
"By the way, I hope you haven’t forgotten that after all this chaos, we’re still students."
Lian paused, the Academy, he had almost forgotten that there had been a life before the Special Area, so many things had happened to them at the same time that they had put this matter aside.
Rindo laughed when he saw his expression.
"I thought after saving a world they would at least give us a few days off." The young Vorhelm said dryly, he was not wrong either, by killing the Calamity they had practically saved the world.
"I thought the same, but we were wrong." Rindo replied.

"Our return has to be officially registered, we have to write a report and we will probably have a meeting with Professor Aldric, this is the normal procedure, but considering the situation it might be a little more complicated this time."
"Fortunately, everyone from our Academy is alive, I can imagine the families of the other Awakened are probably going crazy considering that the news has spread."
"A very large majority of the Awakened who entered have died."
"That’s normal." Lian also nodded.
One-third.
Only about one-third had returned and for most families, that opening had not brought anyone back.
"As soon as the doctors allow it, we have to return to the Academy and we also have to return to Base #3." Rindo let out a breath.
"There is no need to hurry, when everyone wakes up we can talk about these matters." The young Vorhelm said calmly.
They had almost nothing to do at Base #9 and it was logical to prepare to return to their country’s Base, Base #3, but he wanted to at least look around a little before leaving this place.
Maybe he could even find some valuable things with the help of the Celestial Book Of Treasure.
They talked a little more and after that Lian said goodbye, his main reason for coming was to check Rindo’s condition and he was safe.
Besides, it was time for him to go and meet the base officials.
Of course, he still had to wait until they informed him, so he returned to the inn to check on One.
But at that moment, the inn employee told him that the base guards had said to inform him to go to the command building to speak with the base officials.
Considering that they knew which inn he was staying at, there was a good chance that he had been under close watch during this time.
He had expected it and it was also considered a normal procedure.
Less than an hour later, he entered the command building and asked the employees and officers there, and it was clear that the meeting was being held on the third floor.
A formal and fairly simple room, a large rectangular table, six chairs, several floating screens and four people who had been sitting there before he entered.
Two middle-aged men, one woman and an older man sitting at the end of the table, none of them were wearing the official military uniforms of the base.
Their clothes were simple and dark, there was no obvious Federation symbol on their chests either.
But as soon as Lian entered, he understood, these people were different from the officers he had seen in the medical center.
The man on the right had almost no noticeable presence, not because he was weak but the opposite, his presence was too controlled.
The woman across from him also looked completely normal, but the way her eyes moved over him looked more like she was evaluating a target than looking at someone in an administrative position.
The older man? He was just sitting there but Lian’s instincts told him without any clear reason that getting close to him carelessly was not a good idea.
These people did not seem like simple "base officials" at all...

chapters.title: Chapter 406: The Federation Knows
paragraphs: Lian sat down on the empty chair and looked at all three of them, both sides were examining each other until the silence was finally broken.
"This meeting is part of the final evaluation of the Special Area report, and this conversation will be recorded." The middle-aged man said calmly.
"No problem."
"Before we start, you should know that some of the topics discussed here are classified."
"Then you are not the base officials." Lian looked at all four of them for a moment.
A short silence appeared, and the woman slightly raised the corner of her lips.
"Why do you think that?" She then asked with curiosity.
"You are too strong, most base officials are between level 30 and 40, but your presence is much stronger, almost at the level of the strongest professors in our academy."
The presence and aura of these people were equal to Professor Aldric, and that man was someone who had gone through three Evolutions.
Of course, there was another reason, the classified information, base officials were not influential people, at best they were only low-ranking Federation field officers.
The reason he pointed out that he knew they were not base officials was because he wanted them to know that they could not treat him like a toy.
And he was not worried that these people would try to silence him or something like that, he was a Vorhelm and even the Federation did not dare to do anything against this family.
"That was a good observation, but our identities are not important." The woman said calmly.
No one explained anything more and Lian did not insist either, there was no need, in fact he could guess that they were probably from a special unit of the Federation and high-level inspectors.
Then they started asking questions and the first questions were about the route again.
Vhalaris, the Cindari, the Forgotten Tree, the Corrupted Titan.
From the questions they asked, it was clear that they had spoken with all the Awakened they had access to during these three days.
And some information that only Lian and his friends knew had also been shared by Rindo.
Very soon the topic reached something that really mattered to them and the woman changed the page in front of her.
"When did you first hear the word ’Calamity’?"
"The system." Lian leaned back slightly, he did not know why this was important but he answered.
"Did the natives not use this classification?" The woman raised her eyes.
"Not in the same way."
"Did the system directly register the creature as a Calamity?" The man beside her immediately asked.
"Yes."
The man wrote something down and Lian paid attention to their reactions.
The next question was even more interesting.
"What exactly was Black Silence, a creature? A corruption? Some kind of energy?"
"All three, it was an independent entity itself but it could spread like a corruption, it could affect living creatures, minds, and even the environment."
"Could it exist without a vessel?" The older man finally moved his eyes for the first time and asked calmly.
"Yes and no, it exists without a vessel but according to what we understood at least, it needs a vessel to gain freedom of action." Lian paused slightly.
All his answers were within the level of information that the other members of his group also knew.
He still did not know which of the five Calamities their world had faced and who the anchor of that Calamity in their world was, but whoever it was, they might have reached the same level as Cindar.
For that reason, he did not want to expose himself to that person for now by showing too much information.
Of course, if that person really was one of the strongest people in their world, their attention had probably already been drawn to them.

"According to what your friends said, a person named Cindar Vail played a major role in that Calamity appearing in that world, but they did not know exactly what his role was, do you possibly have more information about this?"
This time Lian thought for longer, his friends, just like him, did not know the difference between an anchor and a vessel, they probably did not know that a Calamity needed both to enter a world.
The system had given some clues and hints but for someone who had not seen the Calamity’s memories, putting them together and understanding the truth was difficult.
They probably only understood that Cindar was the main reason the Calamity was able to enter that world, but they did not know what the mechanism behind it was.
"I only know as much as my friends, I do not know why you think I might know more." He then answered with a smile.
"That is because the Calamity was inside your body, it seems likely that you would know more than the others." The female interrogator also answered with a smile.
"It is true that it was inside my body but during the whole time I had almost no control or awareness."
All three of them gave him a heavy look, as if they were trying to understand whether he was telling the truth or there was a lie in his words.
"And how did you survive?" The middle-aged man finally asked.
There was no need to lie about this one, at least not completely.
"I was lucky enough to receive an Extra Life as a Quest reward, after my body was destroyed by my friend, the Extra Life activated and I came back to life." Lian said calmly.
The three of them looked at each other again, and then continued asking questions.

The questions became more numerous, he gave some answers completely, some incompletely and for some he only said that he did not know, he tried to answer within the level of knowledge his other friends had.
During this interrogation, he also realized something, his first guess that the Federation knew nothing about the Calamities turned out to be wrong.
In fact, it was completely the opposite, it was very clear that the Federation had information about the Calamities.
But this information seemed scattered and incomplete, if he had to guess, it seemed that they had obtained this information from previous Ruined Realms.
The information they had obtained during these 250 years had made them familiar with the Calamities, but they still did not know what they were or what the mechanism behind them was.
Of course, it was possible that the highest officials of the Federation and the World Union had more hidden information that even these three people did not know about.
The main information was probably in the hands of level 100 Awakened who had gone through five Evolutions and had seen things in the Ruined Realm that others were not even allowed to hear about.
But this showed that at least they were aware of the Calamities.
Although this did not make Lian feel relieved at all, on the contrary, it made the situation even more complicated.

Because if his guess about the anchor of their own world was correct, then the person who was the anchor might have been working against the Federation and the World Union all this time, trying to stop them from fighting the Calamity.
Another question they asked was whether he had any idea how the Calamity wanted to enter their world and what its inter-world travel mechanism was.

"I am not sure but it seemed very important to it that its vessel was from our world, so it is possible that it needs a body from our world to enter our world? Of course, it seemed that it needed something else besides the vessel, but I do not know what it is." Lian took a thoughtful expression and answered.
Unlike his previous answers, this time he shared more information, now that he knew the Federation knew about the Calamities, he wanted to help them a little.
This way he could also cause some trouble for that anchor and make the Federation search for the vessel of the Calamity that had attacked their world.
But he made sure to answer in a way that was not too far beyond the knowledge of his other friends and spoke as if this was information he had gained from his own observations.
The woman immediately started writing and the man on the right opened several more lines on his screen.
Lian watched their reactions and gave a small smirk.
Little by little, they reached the final part of the meeting and then Aren became the main topic, in fact, it was Lian’s request that they talk about him.
And he made sure they understood that even though that man was a native of the Ruined Realm, he had helped them a lot in the Special Area and during the Quest.
And without him, many more Awakened might have been killed.
And the answer he received was both hopeful and worrying.
"Several of your other friends also asked us to release him, but he is a native of the Ruined Realm, you were not here for nine months and many things happened during this time."
"The conflicts with the seven regions have spread more than you think and they are still causing a lack of safety for Awakened outside the bases."
"Several of our bases were attacked and occupied by them, and freeing them cost us a lot."
"We can treat Aren better, but releasing him is not possible for now." It was the old man who finished explaining everything to him.
Lian immediately said nothing, he did not think their situation with the natives of this world had become so complicated and reached the point of pure hostility.
He only nodded in the end, at least for now, simply making sure Aren was treated better was enough.
The meeting lasted for almost an hour and a half.
When he finally left the command building, the sun was higher and the central area of the base had become its busiest.
He walked a few steps down the stairs when the face of a girl appeared in his mind.
"She might have awakened by now." He then walked toward the medical center.
A few minutes later, he stood in front of Seris’s room, the door was closed and there was no sound coming from inside.
He knocked softly twice but there was no answer, so he lowered the handle and the door opened.
Aurelia had left the room only a few moments ago and Seris was sitting alone on the bed.
Her body was bandaged in several places but other than that she did not seem to have any problems.
Lian entered and closed the door behind him, the girl turned her head.
And became completely still, the man standing in front of her really did not have any injuries, he was not pale and he did not even look weak.
Instead, he was wearing clean clothes and his body was completely healthy, he only seemed a little taller than before.
But it was the same man...the same man she was sure she had pierced through the heart with her sword!
For several seconds Seris only stared, Lian also said nothing.
One second.
Two seconds.
Three.
"Hello." He finally raised his hand slightly and said completely normally.
Seris’s eyes slowly narrowed, the shock on her face was slowly replaced by something else.
Anger.
Her lips pressed together, her jaw tightened and her hand slowly moved behind her head.
"What—" Lian raised an eyebrow.
The girl grabbed the pillow and threw it with all the strength her body allowed.
"You bastard!" She then shouted with real anger.

"Then you are not the base officials." Lian looked at all four of them for a moment.

"Why do you think that?" She then asked with curiosity.
"You are too strong, most base officials are between level 30 and 40, but your presence is much stronger, almost at the level of the strongest professors in our academy."
The presence and aura of these people were equal to Professor Aldric, and that man was someone who had gone through three Evolutions.
Of course, there was another reason, the classified information, base officials were not influential people, at best they were only low-ranking Federation field officers.

Vhalaris, the Cindari, the Forgotten Tree, the Corrupted Titan.

"Yes."

A corruption?
Some kind of energy?"
"All three, it was an independent entity itself but it could spread like a corruption, it could affect living creatures, minds, and even the environment."
