chapters.title: Chapter 407: The Truth She Wanted
paragraphs: The pillow hit the door with a muffled sound and fell to the floor.
Lian only looked at it for a few seconds, then raised his head and his eyes settled on Seris again.
The girl was half-sitting on the bed and staring at him as if she was seriously considering more dangerous options instead of the pillow.
Her face was almost the same as always, cold and controlled, but there was something else under it too, anger.
He had known Seris well enough to understand the difference, this was not one of those short moments of anger that ended with a cold look, a few sarcastic words, and then indifference.
This time it was personal and if he judged fairly, the girl had some right to be angry.
He opened his mouth to say something, but finally gave up, his instinct told him that making a joke would not make the situation better.
Maybe the second pillow would not be a pillow either.
The Young Pendragon took a few slow breaths.
Her chest moved slightly up and down with each breath, the clear anger that had escaped her control for a few moments slowly went away and the familiar cold wall returned to her face.
A few seconds later, it was as if she was not even the same person who had thrown a pillow at him moments ago.
"How are you?" she then asked in a calm and cold voice.
But Lian knew exactly what she meant.
How could a man whose heart she had pierced with her sword be standing in front of her three days later without even a single wound?
"I had gotten an extra life from a mission before, when I died, it activated by itself and rebuilt my body." He did not try to hide the truth and spoke directly.
Seris stared at him for a few seconds, but she was not surprised.
The System had proven many times that abilities, titles, and rewards far stranger than the normal rules of the world existed.
An extra life was rare and unbelievable, but it was not something she could deny existed.
However, her problem was something else.
"Wouldn’t it have been better if you had told me this small detail before you forced me to pierce your heart?" she asked with the same cold face.
Her tone was calm, and that calmness made the sentence even worse.
She had never, ever in her life felt regret or felt as if her heart would break from pain because she killed someone or something.
But thanks to a Vorhelm, one of the greatest enemies of her family, she had experienced something this stupid too.
"Becoming the vessel of Black Silence was not exactly part of my plan." Lian answered in a realistic tone.
Seris said nothing and waited for an explanation.
"I didn’t know I was going to need an extra life before that, and after it took my body, I didn’t exactly have a chance to sit down and talk to you about the plan."
His explanation was so stupidly logical that she could not find any reason to stay angry and her face became calmer.
"So you were there the whole time? Inside your body and alive?"
"Almost." Lian did not answer immediately and thought for a moment, although he finally spoke.
Seris waited for more explanation.

"Everything wasn’t clear, the sounds, the feelings, the movements... most of it was unclear and scattered, and sometimes I understood things with a delay." He was trying to explain the truth in a twisted way so that this girl would calm down.
Normally, he did not care about other people’s anger toward him, they could feel anything they wanted about him.
He did not think he needed to explain his actions to other people.
But this girl had helped him too much, in fact, he had even used her feelings.
At least giving her an explanation was the least he could do for her.
"But you could understand what was happening outside." Seris concluded.
"Almost, yes."
A short silence appeared.
"Could you hear everything?"
This time Lian knew exactly what she was referring to, he really had heard everything.
One.
The screams.
And even those two words, "Help me, damn it." that had come from the Young Pendragon’s mouth and all the moments when she thought he no longer existed.
He had seen and heard everything.
"Enough." He finally answered honestly but vaguely.
Seris’s face remained cold.
But her fingers slightly tightened on the bedsheet for a moment.
"But you didn’t answer any of them, even when I needed to know you were alive more than ever." Seris said in an emotionless tone.
This time it was not a question, it was a fact.
Lian was a little stunned, he did not know why he felt like a man whose wife had caught him cheating and he was making excuses to clear himself.
"I couldn’t, I interfered twice, once near the tree, when it was going after One." He paused and then added.
"And once for you."
For the first time, something changed in Seris’s eyes, the memory returned very quickly.
Two strange pauses.
Two moments when Black Silence had stopped for a fraction of a second, as if something inside its own body had fought against it.
"So those two times..." she said quietly.
"That was me, but then I realized that if I interfered again, it would notice that I had not completely disappeared yet." he confirmed and his voice became a little more serious.
"If it realized that, it would probably find the remaining part of my identity.
Seris lowered her eyes.
"So when I called your name too..." Seris left the sentence unfinished.
"I heard you, but I had to stay silent." Lian answered without trying to avoid the question.
The Young Pendragon asked nothing else, she really did not need to, she had understood everything she wanted to know.
Lian had been inside the body, he had been alive, he had heard and seen everything, but his silence had not been because he did not care.

Knowing these things did not completely erase all the feelings of the past few days, but it definitely helped her feel better, the anger she felt, as if she had been tricked, had completely disappeared.
Lian only looked at Seris for a few seconds, the girl’s face was completely cold again, it was impossible to tell if she was still angry or not.
She probably was, but not as much as before and she simply was not showing it anymore.
To most people, Seris the Pendragon was always like this, a sword genius, the heir of one of the greatest families in the world.
Cold, proud, someone who seemed to feel no difference between the presence or absence of other people.
But he knew better now, Seris might never say it out loud, but she had accepted him as a friend.
And knowing her personality, this probably meant much more to Seris than it would to a normal person.
Because a girl like her probably never had many friends.
Maybe she had never let anyone get close enough that she would truly feel pain from losing them.
And he had created almost all of the worst possible situations for her one after another in just a few days.
First, her body had been taken by a Calamity, then he had almost killed Seris several times and Seris had also been forced to kill him several times.
He had not answered any of her calls the entire time and in the end, he had forced her to pierce his heart with her own hands.
That word, "do it." that he had said in his final moments might have been only a few words to him, but it had affected this girl much more than he had expected.
Even if the plan had succeeded, this was not something that a few simple explanations could erase.
Lian let out a short sigh, he was not going to expect Seris to smile right now and forget everything.
"I only came to make sure you’re okay." He finally said simply.
"I don’t die that easily." Seris said in her usual cold tone.
A small smile appeared on the Young Vorhelm’s face, at least this part of her personality was completely fine.
"I understand."
A few seconds of silence passed and she looked toward the window for a moment, then as if she had remembered something, she looked back at him.
"One more thing...be careful of your brother, I don’t know if you will believe me or not, but he does not have good intentions."

chapters.title: Chapter 408: Unexpected Meeting I
paragraphs: "Darian? I heard what he said, I know he doesn’t have good intentions." The smile on Lian’s face slowly disappeared.
"A person who stands over his brother’s corpse and talks about how much easier his work will be because you died usually doesn’t have good intentions." Seris said without the slightest joke.
She didn’t know what the relationship between these two brothers was like and didn’t want to speak in a way that made it seem like she was trying to ruin the relationship between the two brothers.
But she still thought it was necessary to warn him, she had felt something was wrong about Darian from the very beginning.
"I’ll be careful." He looked at her for a few seconds, there was no reason to pretend he didn’t know anything.
He could already guess the reason behind his brother’s intentions, but since it seemed that he might have already left the base or even the Ruined Realm, he couldn’t go after him directly.
But that wasn’t a problem, he could find him later and his instincts told him that sooner or later, they would meet again.
On the other hand, this answer was enough for her, she didn’t ask what he planned to do and she wasn’t curious about Darian’s motives.
If Lian said he would be careful, that was enough for now.
"When are you getting discharged?" Lian changed the subject after a short pause.
"In a few hours, the main treatment is finished and the rest only needs some rest, I don’t need to stay here just to rest." Seris answered calmly.
He looked at her condition, the bandages still covered a large part of her body, but she didn’t seem to have any other problems and most of her injuries had already been treated.
It didn’t seem like this girl had any interest in staying in the treatment center for more days either.
"Are you going back to the Pendragon Family?"
"I’ve been away from home for a long time, I need to go back." She had duties that she had to do and couldn’t ignore.
And the amount of time she had been away was long enough that many changes might have happened.

There were no succession conflicts in their family like there were among the Vorhelms, it was almost certain that she would become the heir of the family, although it had not been officially confirmed.
Because of that, she wasn’t worried about her position, even if she didn’t become the heir, she wouldn’t care, that position had no value to her.
What she was worried about was her mother.
"What about you?"
"I’m going back to the Academy." Lian answered without needing to think.
Nine months had passed, the Academy must have changed.
There were students, rankings, powers, and people that he really wanted to know what they had done during this time.
Of course, there was another reason, the Academy had its own exams and he couldn’t ignore them, he had to take the exams.
He and the rest of the group had missed the midterm exams, but they had an excuse for that, even though they couldn’t ignore the final exams.
"Nine months have passed, there are a few people I want to see and find out what they’ve done during this time."
"We’re probably behind most of them." Seris said without emotion.
But the sentence had another weight for her, she had lost nine months of growth.
People her age had hunted, gained levels, evolved, and even learned new skills.
But her?
She hadn’t just lost time, she had burned a thousand points from her permanent stats and had fallen from two thousand to one thousand stats.
The mission reward had only given her two hundred and fifty free stat points.
Even if she used all of them immediately, she would only reach one thousand two hundred and fifty.
She was still seven hundred and fifty points weaker than the power she had before the battle.
While everyone else had moved forward.
For someone like Seris, becoming weaker was scary, she wasn’t afraid of losing, although she didn’t like it, but that wasn’t her fear.
She was afraid of falling behind and staying weak and it was one of her biggest fears.
But that didn’t mean she was worried, she trusted herself enough to know that she could return to the top in a short time and even go beyond it.
Lian looked at her face for a few seconds.
"That’s true but but catching up to them won’t be hard for us." Lian said without trying to deny it for no reason.
He wasn’t saying this just to make her feel better, especially since she didn’t seem to care much, he was only telling the truth.
He was an anomaly, he knew that himself.
But Seris wasn’t normal either, among all the people he had seen until now, he didn’t know anyone with better combat talent than her.
It wasn’t an exaggerated compliment, it was the truth, this girl was a genius, in fact, she was the real definition of a genius.
A few moments later, Seris’s eyes moved over Lian’s body again.
He had grown a little taller, his shoulders were wider and even the way he stood was a little different, not only because of his confidence, but because of a real change in his body’s structure.
And all of this had one meaning.
"Did you complete your first evolution?"
He nodded to show yes.
"Did it take long?"
"The evolution itself? Not really." Lian answered and then sighed.
"It was easy, what opened after that wasn’t."
"What opened?" Seris became a little more curious.
"Traits, Skill Fusion and the Innate Traits tree."
She didn’t notice anything strange about this, all of these were common knowledge about the first evolution that almost every awakened, including her, knew about.
"The main problem is that all of them need Fragments too." Lian added with a tired tone.
"That’s normal." Seris answered.
"You don’t understand, some Traits for the first level need hundreds of Fragments and just the first branch of my Innate Traits tree needs more than 4000 Fragments just to unlock.
"Several thousand?" This time the Young Pendragon really turned her head slightly toward him and asked with a small frown.
"More than four thousand."
Silence filled the room for a few seconds, this amount was terrifying, especially when it was only for the first Innate Trait.
Seris had heard about the value of Fragments after evolution since childhood.
The elders of the family always said that awakened didn’t understand their true value before their first evolution.
But more than four thousand just to unlock one branch? This number was not the same for everyone and each person’s Innate Traits tree was different.
But considering Seris’s talent and class, the amount she needed would probably be around the same.
"The family always said that after the first evolution, Fragments become more important than stats, I thought they were exaggerating." She finally said calmly.
"They’re even more important than money." Lian also emphasized and added another point.
"With money you can buy equipment, buy potions, get services, but right now almost every part of the system can only be unlocked with Fragments."
Seris nodded.
A wealthy awakened could buy the best armor.
But they couldn’t create thousands of Fragments out of nothing.
In the end, they had to hunt or do Quests, getting Fragments from the first method was completely based on luck and getting Quests from the system wasn’t easy either.
"How many do you have?" she then asked curiously.
"Seven."
"What? Didn’t you get a hundred from the mission?" Seris’s eyes widened slightly.
"I did."
"Then what happened to the rest?"
"I spent three hundred to bring One back."
"One is back?" The Young Pendragon immediately asked.
"I summoned him this morning."
"Is he alive?"
"Yeah, his injuries haven’t fully healed yet, but he’s out of danger." Lian also answered calmly and realized that the ant seemed to have become important to this girl too.
"Good." Seris stayed silent for a few seconds and finally said with a kind of hidden relief under her coldness.
At that moment, the door opened.
"The discharge—" Aurelia entered, although her sentence stopped halfway when her eyes fell on Lian.
She stayed silent for a second and then an amused smile appeared on her face.
"Oh, oh... the handsome Vorhelm is here too." She finally said playfully.

I heard what he said, I know he doesn’t have good intentions." The smile on Lian’s face slowly disappeared.
"A person who stands over his brother’s corpse and talks about how much easier his work will be because you died usually doesn’t have good intentions." Seris said without the slightest joke.
She didn’t know what the relationship between these two brothers was like and didn’t want to speak in a way that made it seem like she was trying to ruin the relationship between the two brothers.

chapters.title: Chapter 409: Unexpected Meeting II
paragraphs: "Lady Pendragon, I’m glad to see you again." Lian stood up from the chair.
Aurelia walked forward, her eyes moved from his head to his feet.
A few centimeters of height change, a slightly different body structure and no sign of the man whose heart had stopped working three days ago, she noticed every small and big detail.
"Same here, especially considering that I heard you were dead three days ago."
"Looks like you fooled half the people in that world by faking your death." She said as if she was telling an interesting story.
Lian thought about the sentence for a few seconds, he didn’t know why but "faking your death" sounded like something taken from a cheap show.
The main character fakes his death, comes back a few years later and everyone is shocked.
"I had to do it to trick our enemy and defeat him." But he only said dryly.
Aurelia looked at his serious face for a few seconds and then laughed.
"You’re right."
At that moment, a cold voice came from beside them.
"What he did allowed us to win in the end." It was Seris, who added in a cold voice.
Lady Pendragon was slightly stunned, this girl had almost exploded from anger and from feeling that she had been used because of this only a few hours ago.
But now she was even defending him? Her eyes moved briefly between the two, she said nothing but her smile became slightly more suspicious.
Then she put the folder on the table beside the bed.
"Anyway, your discharge is finished, we can go now."
The Young Pendragon nodded.
And Lian also felt that it was better not to bother them anymore, he also had many things waiting for him.
"Anyway, I should go too." He said and moved away from the chair, then turned toward Aurelia.
"I’m glad to see you again."
"Same here." The woman answered with a smile.
The Young Vorhelm then looked at Seris, for a moment he didn’t know if he should say anything more or not.
"Take care of yourself." He finally said simply.
Seris said nothing.
Lian turned to leave.
One step.
Two steps.
His hand reached the door handle.
"Wait." The girl suddenly said in a calm voice.
Lian stopped and Aurelia also raised an eyebrow at the same moment.
Seris didn’t speak for a few seconds, this pause made the other woman’s gaze become more curious.
"Next month, the Dragon Mark Ceremony will be held."
The Young Vorhelm knew the name, almost everyone who had basic information about the great families had heard of it.
The Dragon Mark Ceremony, one of the oldest traditions of the Pendragon Family.
This ceremony was usually held a few months after a new Ruined Realm was opened and despite how it looked, it was not just a family celebration.
The current generation of the family was introduced there, and people who had made important achievements in exploring the new realm were honored.
Allied families and unions were invited, political and business deals were made behind closed doors.
And the important members of the new generation swore the traditional family oath in front of the First Dragon Mark.
Of course, the most important part of it was announcing the heir who would lead the Pendragon Family for the next 25 years and until that realm was cleared.
For people outside the family, being invited to such a ceremony was not a small thing.
"Since nine months have passed, it should be held next month, you can come." Seris continued.
Lian really paused for a moment, he didn’t expect to be invited so suddenly.
But Aurelia’s reaction was more interesting, the woman’s face became completely blank for a fraction of a second and her head slowly turned toward her.
She had heard something she did not expect.
Seris... had personally invited someone?
The same girl who didn’t even attend family ceremonies most of the time?
"Is this an invitation from Seris Pendragon or from the Pendragon Family?" Lian asked curiously.
"If it was an invitation from my family, the family itself would send you an invitation." The Young Pendragon answered dryly.
So yes, it was personal.
And his mind quickly checked the next month.
Returning to the Academy, meeting Kain, getting the ancient armor, selling the bodies of the monsters he had collected and probably the Academy exams.
These were all the things he could think about for now and it was not clear what would happen by then.
But if he was free, going to the Pendragon Family ceremony would not be a bad thing, in fact, it was a good opportunity.
Many of the most important people of the new generation, great families and unions would probably be there.
"If I can, I’ll definitely come."
"Okay." Seris only gave one answer and her facial expression remained cold as if she had just done something completely normal a few seconds ago.
Only Aurelia was standing beside the bed and looking at her strangely.
This time Lian opened the door and left the room, the door slowly closed behind him.
And with him gone, silence filled the room for a few seconds.
Seris opened her panel again to check the information about her evolution, as if nothing special had happened.
Aurelia was still standing in her place, her eyes were on her, she wasn’t speaking or moving but only staring.
The Young Pendragon tried to ignore her for a few seconds.
Five seconds.
Ten seconds.
Finally, she lowered the panel.
"Why are you looking at me like that? It’s annoying." She asked with a small frown.
Aurelia looked very serious, so serious that for a moment Seris even thought she wanted to talk about something important regarding the family.
"Now I’m sure." She said in a completely serious tone.
"About what?"
"You’re really in love." Aurelia answered without the slightest pause.
"No." Seris’s face immediately became colder and she said without hesitation.
"You invited someone to a ceremony!"
"So what? It’s just a simple invitation."
Aurelia really couldn’t believe that Seris was seriously asking that question for a moment, she raised her hand and pointed directly at her with her index finger.
"You, Seris Pendragon!" She said with emphasis and wanted to continue, but the girl snorted.
"I know my name."
"The person who didn’t even attend her own birthday two years ago and said that inviting guests was something idiots did, you invited someone to a ceremony!" Aurelia continued in disbelief.
"It has nothing to do with it." Seris answered completely without emotion.
She only looked at her for a few seconds, it had nothing to do with it? Of course, completely unrelated, ridiculously so!
The girl who probably wouldn’t even notice if this ceremony was canceled had now invited a man herself to attend it.
And not just any man, Lian Vorhelm, the son of the patriarch of their biggest rival family.
Her gaze slowly changed, an old thought, almost forgotten, came back from the corner of her mind.
The Pendragon Family.
The Vorhelm Family.
Two young generations.
Two geniuses.
A family marriage.
And a plan that she had once made in her mind mostly as a joke and a fantasy.
Aurelia’s eyes narrowed slightly, maybe... just maybe, that plan was not so unrealistic anymore.
A calm smile appeared on her face, but this smile was different from her previous smiles, it was too calculated.
"I don’t like that look of yours." Seris noticed it almost immediately and said coldly.
"Why me? I didn’t do anything." Aurelia asked with completely fake innocence.
The Young Pendragon stared at her for a few seconds and this time the woman couldn’t stop herself from laughing.
And at that exact moment, Seris became sure that inviting Lian had probably been a much bigger mistake than she had thought.

chapters.title: Chapter 410: Colony House
paragraphs: After leaving Seris’s room, Lian still had a few small things to do in Base #9.
None of them were supposed to take long.
Most of them were simply visiting people who, a few days ago, had stood together in a place where almost no one expected them to come out alive.
First, he went to see Seraphina.
The girl was still in the medical center, although her condition had changed a lot compared to the day they returned.
The severe shaking in her sword hand had almost disappeared, and the color had completely returned to her face.
When Lian entered the room, Seraphina looked at him from head to toe for a few seconds without saying anything.
A man who should have been dead had suddenly appeared in front of her without any wound or bandage, and there was not even a sign that his heart had been pierced by a sword.
"I don’t even know how I’m supposed to react to this, I’m just glad you’re alive." Seraphina said with a tired look that showed her relief.
"Everything happened so fast that I couldn’t tell you I had a backup plan." Lian calmly replied.
"That answer was not reassuring at all, I just hope you know that there are people like me who can’t easily watch you die." The girl said dryly.
After her, the visits with the others were even shorter.
Liana could now walk without help, although the deep wounds on her body had not completely closed yet and she had lost both of her summons.
Now she was a summoner without any summons and had to find a way to solve this problem as soon as possible, otherwise her career as an Awakened would completely fail.
Selina also looked more tired than injured and a large part of her problems had already been solved.
Cassian was also in fairly good condition and as usual, the first thing he did when he saw Lian was stare at his completely healthy chest for a few seconds and let out a sigh of relief.

Among all the members of the group, it could be said that this boy had the strongest sense of responsibility and he still could not forgive himself for losing one of their teammates in the Fallen Border City.
And the fact that he thought Lian had died and that once again he had failed to stop the death of his teammates had made him seriously think that maybe he should quit being an Awakened.
But now that he saw that Lian was fine, it seemed his opinion had changed again.
The visits were short.
But it was strange, none of them were exactly the same people who had entered the Special Area.
Something in their eyes had changed, after all, a large number of their companions had not returned.
The experiences they had gained during this time could have been the experience of an entire lifetime, they had been accused and sentenced, imprisoned, and then fought and taken over a city.
They had been surrounded by a civilization and then fought against an entire civilization that had dozens of times more forces than them, and had gone to the edge of complete extinction.
In the end, they had been forced to face an existence that could shake the foundations of worlds.
Even when they laughed, the weight of those nine months was still somewhere behind their eyes.
Rindo and the others decided to stay at the base for one more day until their conditions became completely stable and they handed in their reports, then they would return to the academy.
Aren was still under the Federation’s supervision.
And Darian? Lian still did not know exactly what his older brother was planning, but for now, it did not matter.
Before leaving the Ruined Realm, there was one more person left.
One.
When he entered the mount maintenance area, the first thing he felt was the familiar connection of Hive Dominion.
A moment later, a calm wave of happiness reached his mind through the connection.
"Did you miss me this soon?" Lian raised the corner of his lips slightly.
He opened the private area and One almost immediately raised his huge head.
His condition was very different from the morning.
His injured leg had still not completely healed, but it was no longer in that terrible position.
The broken bones had been stabilized with the help of the potions and the natural healing ability of his body.
The large crack on his chest armor was also slowly closing.
Parts of his natural armor were still cracked and his damaged antenna had not regenerated yet, but One no longer looked like a creature that could die at any moment.
He should be able to completely return to his peak within the next one or two days.
His master walked over to him and placed his hand on his head.
"You’re much better now."
The giant ant slightly pressed his head against his hand, and satisfaction, calmness, and a little pride could be seen in his eyes.
"Do you still think what you did that day was right? You could have died." Lian gave a smirk.
An answer came through the connection.
Firm and without the slightest hesitation, yes, and he would do the same thing again.
Young Vorhelm stayed silent for a few seconds, he did not know whether this was the ability of his innate talent or whether this ant was simply this loyal by nature.
If it was the second one, then fine, but if it was the first one, the ability of his innate talent was more frightening than it seemed at first glance.
He probably needed to find another member for his colony to get the answer.
Then he opened his evolved innate talent panel.
After the first evolution of his innate talent, not only had the capacity of the colony changed, several secondary abilities had also been unlocked with it.
One of them had not been used until now.
Colony House
Lian kept his eyes on the name and the information appeared.
[Colony House]
[A special living space connected to the owner of the colony.]
[Registered colony members can enter.]
[Members inside the colony space will enter a resting state.]
[The need for food and water is greatly reduced.]
[Natural recovery speed is increased.]
[Special members can be transferred almost immediately.]
He read the text several times.

The space was not actually inside his real body, in fact, it was similar to a separate space that was connected to his existence through the colony talent, but from the outside, it seemed like the creature entered his body.
It looked somewhat similar to the ability of some summoners.
Then he looked away from the panel and looked at One.
"How about seeing your new home?" he asked him with a smile.
[Colony House]
[Special Member detected: One.]
[Current Condition: Injured.]
[Transfer available.]
[Transfer One to Colony House?]
[Yes / No]
He clicked the confirmation option.
[Yes.]
Lian expected a spatial crack to open or something like a gate, but suddenly a weak light appeared under One’s body.
The light moved up from the giant ant’s legs and the black shell of his body began to shine, then glowing particles separated from his legs.
"Hmm?" Young Vorhelm unconsciously took one step back.
The light moved faster.
Legs.
Abdomen.
Chest armor.
Head.
One’s entire huge body turned into thousands of tiny particles of light in less than a few seconds, he did not even have time to react.
The particles moved toward Lian, directly toward his chest, and disappeared.
The area that had contained a several-meter-long ant only moments ago was now completely empty.
He stood there for a few seconds and then slowly lowered his head and looked at his own body.
"...What?" he said with a truly confused expression.
After Black Silence, the Ruined Heart, and almost having his soul devoured by a Calamity, he thought his threshold for things that could surprise him had become very high.
But seeing a several-ton ant turn into light and disappear directly inside his body was still a little strange.
The panel immediately appeared.
[Colony House]
[Residents: 1]
[One — Special Member]
[Status: Resting.]
[Recovery Efficiency: +20%]
Lian narrowed his eyes slightly, he could still feel One through Hive Dominion.
But the feeling was different, One’s presence was no longer coming from a specific direction.
It was as if he was somewhere exactly beside his own existence, but at the same time, he was at a distance that could not be measured by the normal concept of space.
He focused on One’s name.
[Release Special Member?]
"Yes."
Glowing particles appeared in front of him and joined together in less than two seconds, One’s huge body formed again.

The ant moved his head in confusion for a moment, as if he could not understand what had happened, he had suddenly entered a place that truly felt like a home to him and then suddenly came back outside?
Lian looked at him and then again said...
"Inside."
The giant ant turned into light again and entered his master’s chest.
"Outside." Young Vorhelm waited for a few seconds.
The light gathered again and turned into a giant ant.
One appeared and this time, a clear wave of displeasure reached Lian’s mind through the connection.
Lian looked at him for a moment and the ant was also looking at him and if the face of a giant ant had the ability to show annoyance, it was probably this.
"Okay, okay, the test is over." he raised his hand and said in a surrendering tone.

chapters.title: Chapter 411: Noticeable Changes In Academy
paragraphs: "Okay, okay, the test is over." Lian raised his hand and said in a surrendered tone.
One looked at him for a few more seconds and finally his master activated the Colony House again.
[One — Resting.]
[Recovery Efficiency: +20%]
Lian closed the panel, it seemed like a simple ability, but its use was not simple at all, he no longer needed to find a way to move One around.

He could take him to cities, pass through gates, enter buildings and in the future if his colony became larger, not only One, but also other commanders and powerful members could always be carried with him.
An army that no one could see was always with him.
It was an interesting thought but for later, for now, it was time to go to the Academy.
He left the mount section and went directly toward the transfer gate area.
Nine months ago, to get from his own country to Base #9, they had first needed to use the Base #3 and then travel through the Ruined Realm for the rest of the way.
At that time, there had been no direct route.
But during the past three days, he had heard several Awakened people say that the transfer network of Base #9 had expanded greatly.
With more than several thousand kilometers of the surrounding areas stabilized, many new portals had also been created.
Maybe one of them was directly connected to his own country.
He spent a few minutes searching among the large boards in the transfer center and finally asked one of the workers about the route to the capital.
The answer was better than he expected, there was a direct route.
Base #9 — Capital Transfer Center of His Country
Lian looked at the name of the route for a few seconds, nine months ago, something like this had not existed.
Now traveling between their world and one of the farthest bases of the Ruined Realm had almost become as simple as buying a normal ticket.
The transfer cost was not cheap, but it was not something he cared much about, so he paid.
A few minutes later, he was standing in front of one of the large portals, its surface was shaking like a wall of blue light.
Lian looked at Base #9 one last time and then entered the portal.
The sounds disappeared and the world became dark, for a moment there was nothing.
He could not feel his senses or his weight, it was almost as if his body no longer existed and then the light returned.
He heard the sound of many people talking.
He blinked and found smooth stone under his feet, several large portals were around the hall and hundreds of people were moving through marked lines.
Agents, Awakened people, families and workers were moving around and route signs and shops came into his view.
Lian stood there for a few seconds, there was no smell of blood, no burnt ground and no Calamity feeding on corpses.
There was no strange sky above him and more importantly, he could not feel any danger.
He took a deep breath.
In the Ruined Realm, it was impossible to truly feel calm and at any moment something dangerous could happen that no one expected.
And the color of the sky in the Ruined Realm was depressing and suffocating.

But now he had finally returned to his own world, the same beautiful, calm, clear blue sky that did not have that constant heaviness that had unconsciously become part of his life in the Ruined Realm.
He had just realized how much he had gotten used to the constant presence of danger.
"I’m back." The corner of his lips rose slightly and he whispered very quietly.
Maybe this city was not his birthplace but this world was his world.
Lian left the transfer center, took a taxi and went directly to the Academy, during the entire trip he only hoped that Kain was at the Academy.
After all, there was a very high chance that his childhood friend was currently in the Ruined Realm, hunting and advancing.
There was only a small chance that he would be at the Academy at such a random time.
Almost half an hour later, the Academy gates appeared through the car window.
He unconsciously leaned forward a little and looked at the same walls, the same large Academy symbol and the same buildings that he had seen on his first day when he entered.
For a few seconds, memories that now seemed very old returned to his mind.
On the first day he came here, he was a boy who did not even have a successful Awakening.
Someone who had only managed to enter the Academy because of his analytical ability.
A student whose presence here was considered a mistake by many people and some had even openly made fun of him.
And now Lian leaned back against the seat, one of his classes was unknown and abnormal, a class that challenged all known limits.
He had completed his first evolution.
He had devoured a Calamity.
And a giant ant was also sleeping inside a space connected to his existence.
It had really been a strange nine months, although he had only felt and truly experienced around thirty days of it, and even a little less.
The car stopped in front of the entrance and he paid the cost and got out, he looked at the entrance gate for a few moments and then entered.
And almost at the same moment, he felt something strange.
At first glance, nothing had changed much, the educational buildings were the same and the stone paths were still there.
The old trees were still on both sides of the path, even the voices of the students moving between the classes and dormitories were familiar.
But the atmosphere was different.
Lian slowed his steps a little, his eyes moved among the students.
First, he noticed the groups, it was not that there had not been groups before, it was natural for students to move with their friends and teammates.
But now their structure was much clearer.
Some students had small symbols on their clothes, several large groups almost always moved away from the others.
And every time one of those groups passed through the path, the weaker students unconsciously moved aside.
No one gave an order and there was no clear threat but the people’s behavior showed everything by itself.
Hierarchy.
During the first nine months of the school year, the positions had become fixed.
The strong people were known, the influential people were known and there were also people that others preferred not to bother.
Lian could see it in their eyes, in their movements and in the short silences that appeared when some groups passed by.
But this was exactly what bothered him, something here was out of its natural balance.
Although hierarchy always existed everywhere, now it was too obvious, as if someone had forced the law of the jungle to be followed in the Academy.
"It could also be because of the students’ competitive nature." He whispered to himself, after all, the students were still young and the feeling of competition among them was strong.
But he did not know why, but he felt that this obvious change had another reason, a reason that he definitely would not like.
In the end, at least for now, he ignored it, he could ask his friend about the details later.
His first target was the dormitory, if Kain was at the Academy, the dormitory was the best place to find a sign of him.
But the second reason was even more important.
His phone.
Before entering the Special Area, he had left it in the locker of his room, probably hundreds of messages and calls were waiting for him...or maybe not.
But there was one message he was really waiting for.
The blacksmith.
The Ancient Rank armor was supposed to be ready much earlier and after nine months it was almost impossible that it was still unfinished.
Just imagining seeing the final result made a small feeling of real excitement appear inside him.
An Ancient Rank armor, with such armor he no longer needed to worry about defense, at least not until his enemies became terribly powerful.
But before he had even covered half of the distance, two people stood in front of him.
At first, he did not pay much attention, he thought they were just students coming from the opposite direction.
But they did not move aside and Lian raised his head slightly and recognized one of the faces almost immediately.
Darren.
His classmate in the Elite Class, a man who called himself Rodrick’s best friend, although he was only one of his dogs and nothing more.
And more importantly, someone Lian had given a rather unforgettable lesson to on his second day at the Academy.
His eyes then moved to the person beside him, at first he could not recognize him, but his face looked familiar, as if he had seen him somewhere before but only vaguely.
After thinking for a moment and using his brain more, he remembered him too.
The same man who had tried to make fun of him from among the crowd on the first day of the Academy, during Professor Aldric’s test.
His name was not important, but his face was familiar to him.

And by looking at them, he noticed something, something about both of them had changed, not only their appearance, although their equipment was much better, the flow of mana around their bodies was more organized.
And Lian was almost sure that both of them had completed their first evolution.
But what attracted more attention was their behavior.
Their shoulders were pulled back, their chins were raised and the way they looked at the students around them, they did not only have confidence ...
They acted as if they owned this place.

chapters.title: Chapter 412: The Power Gap Just Gotten bigger
paragraphs: Darren also stared at him for a few moments, then a mocking smile appeared on his face.
"Ha, look who finally came back." Then he said in a voice louder than necessary.
A few students nearby turned their heads, and the man beside him also laughed.
"I thought you died in that area." He said in a mocking tone.
Darren put his hands into his pockets.
"He disappeared for nine months, maybe he was hiding somewhere and waiting for the others to do the work."
Lian only looked at them for a few seconds, he never expected good behavior from these two idiots, but he also did not expect to receive such a welcome after coming back after all this time.
Nine months ago, maybe these words would have bothered him a little, and even that was a maybe, and that maybe was a big one.
Now? After facing the Black Silence, the mockery of these two was almost sweet, like hearing threats from two children.
"The academy’s welcome was warmer than I expected, they sent two idiots to make me understand that if I become lazy, my future will look like theirs." Then he answered in a completely dry tone.
"You still have that mouth." Darren said with a frown, and his smile became a little weaker.
"You still have the same face I punched the last time, so it seems neither of us has changed much." Lian also answered calmly.
A few students nearby could not completely hide their reactions, and some short smiles and hidden laughs came from them.
Darren’s face immediately became dark, he could never forget the memory of that damned day.

"You talk too much for someone who is nine months behind the others, if you fight Brother Roderick again, he will smash your face into the ground." The man beside him took one step forward and said proudly.
This time, Lian looked at them more carefully, interesting, they were not bluffing, they really believed they had become stronger than him.
Nine months ago, he had been a problem for them, but now, in their minds, he was a student who had made no progress for nine months, while they had hunted, gained levels, and evolved.
Even so, their confidence was too much, even considering that.
The young Vorhelm looked around briefly, many students were watching what was happening, but no one came closer.
Some of them had even moved farther away on purpose after seeing Darren.
So it was not only personal strength, there was something, or someone, behind these two.
Roderick... huh?
The answer was probably that simple.
"What happened? Did you finally realize how far behind you are?" Darren thought he was afraid when he saw that he did not answer, and his arrogant expression returned.
"No, I was thinking about what made your false confidence become this high and made you start imagining things.
"Maybe because I’m not the same student I was nine months ago." Darren’s smile became a little stiff.
"Unlikely."
"You better understand that things have changed, this place is not like before." Darren came closer, and this time the distance between them was less than one meter.
"Oh? What exactly changed?" Lian looked at him with a mocking expression.
And the man raised his hand, as if he wanted to put it on Lian’s shoulder, but before he could touch him, something changed.
For only a moment, he loosened his control.
He released only a very small part of what had formed inside him during this time.
The presence, killing intent, and monster-like instincts that had formed in his body through battles and coming close to death several times.
Darren’s eyes suddenly became wider, and his hand stopped in the air. The breathing of the man beside him also stopped for a moment.

The surroundings did not change for them, but for a fraction of a second, Lian was no longer just a normal student standing in front of them, and instead, something unclear and instinctive appeared deep inside their minds.
Something huge, hungry, and extremely dangerous, a creature that did not see them as enemies, but as prey.
Darren’s body took half a step back before his brain could even decide to do it.
Cold sweat appeared on the back of his neck, and the man beside him even took a full step back.
The young Vorhelm immediately gathered his presence again, the entire thing had lasted less than a second, but both of their faces had changed, and fear had made their whole bodies tremble.
"Your confidence has become much higher, but it seems your strength has not changed much but the gap of power between us has only gotten bigger " Lian said calmly.
He paused for a moment.
Darren’s jaw tightened, the initial fear was now mixed with anger and humiliation.
Could he retreat in front of everyone? No, his pride would not allow it.
Mana slowly began moving around his body, and the man beside him also prepared himself.
But before anything else could happen, a cold voice came from a few meters away.
"Lian Vorhelm."
The mana almost stopped at the same moment.
Lian turned his head, and Darren and the man beside him did the same.
A tall man was standing at the end of the path, wearing the formal clothes of the academy professors, with the same serious face and the same cold eyes that seemed to always find something to judge.
Professor Aldric.
The two frowned deeply, but they did not dare to continue the fight in front of the professor, and before leaving, they looked at the young Vorhelm one more time.
"Consider yourself lucky."
"If that helps you sleep better at night, sure." Lian answered without the slightest worry.
Darren’s face became dark again, but he said nothing and left with the other man.
He watched them leave for a few seconds, then turned toward the professor.
"Professor, it has been a long time."
Aldric said nothing for a few seconds and only looked at him, a long look that moved from his face, shoulders, and hands to the way he was standing.

"Looks like you were not lazy during these nine months." Of course, news that time in the Special Area moved ten times slower had also spread, and this was why some people thought those who entered that place might have fallen behind.
"If I had been lazy, I would not have had anything to say in front of those two and would have had to keep my head down." Lian gave a small smile.
"Come, we’ll talk in my office."
The office was almost exactly as he remembered it.
Clean and simple, even the way the files were placed on the desk was almost the same, unlike himself, Professor’s office had not changed much during these nine months.
Aldric sat behind the desk, and he also sat on the chair in front of him.

"What really happened there? I heard the rumors, but I would rather hear a better explanation from you, and of course, it is not only an explanation for me, the report you have to give to the academy also counts." Then Professor asked.
"Do you want the short version or the version that takes several hours?"

"Short, enough to give the academy a satisfying report, if you also achieved something useful, do not be shy about mentioning it, it can be recorded as part of your record and earn you student points."
It was predictable, and Lian began.

He talked about the native civilization, the Cindari, their cities, the conflict with them, the Titan, the Graveyard battle and the casualties, and the extremely dangerous creature that had eventually caused almost the entire group to be destroyed.
Aldric listened the entire time without interrupting him, although the more he heard, the more his eyebrows came together.
"That was a pretty busy student trip." He stayed silent for a few seconds, then added

From the first day he met this boy, he had felt that he was a magnet for trouble, when he sent him to the fallen border city, he realized that he was not only a magnet for trouble, but also so brave, or maybe stupid, that he would walk straight into the arms of trouble and danger.
In the entire report he heard, this boy was the one who went toward trouble and extremely dangerous and crazy actions, and doing such things required either endless courage or endless stupidity.

chapters.title: Chapter 413: Kain is isolated
paragraphs: In the entire report he heard, this boy was the one who went toward trouble and extremely dangerous and crazy actions, and doing such things required either endless courage or endless stupidity.
He did not know where this kid had gotten such a personality.
Maybe it was genetic... according to the stories he had heard about the Vorhelm patriarch, that man had the same personality.
"A little." Lian could not stop a short laugh, then added.
"Professor, what about things here? Nine months is not a short time, how was the situation while we were gone?"
"Business as usual." Aldric answered very simply.
"Your definition of normal can be worrying."

"Most students spent a lot of time in Base Number Three, hunting, doing missions, and exploring new areas, and the members of the Elite Class completed their first evolution, a considerable number of them also passed Level 25."
Lian raised an eyebrow, it was not that bad, nine months was a long time for growth.

But his expectations were too high, his own growth speed was terrifyingly explosive, and even though the EXP he needed for each level could be up to five times the amount needed by a five-star class, he still leveled up very quickly.
And this was thanks to one of his innate skills, which allowed him to absorb 100% of the EXP from killing every monster, although it was 150% now.
But other Awakened did not have such an advantage, and four-star classes could only absorb 40% and three-star classes 30%.
Their leveling speed was much slower, and unlike him or Seris, they could not hunt alone, and this reduced their speed and even caused them to kill monsters in groups, which cut the rewards in half.
That was why for two-star, three-star, and four-star classes, reaching the second evolution could take up to two years.
If he had not been trapped inside the Special Area, his level would probably have been much higher than thirty, in fact, he could even have been close to his second evolution.
Of course, level was not everything, everything he had gained in the Special Area was much more valuable and made up for the time he had lost.
Besides being able to become familiar with a hidden part inside his body called the Ruin Heart and learn huge secrets such as the secret of the Calamities.
He had managed to destroy and devour one of those Calamities, gain a very useful S-Rank talent, and obtain a multi-ton ant as a mount.
"So I really fell far behind." Lian said jokingly.
Aldric said nothing and only looked at him for a few seconds, his gaze became calmer and more careful.
The young Vorhelm could almost feel that the professor was examining something inside him.
Humans, unlike monsters, did not have a panel that directly showed the level of other humans.
But the professor had a lot of experience, and that experience was telling him something.
Lian’s presence was huge, but compressed and heavily controlled, like a large river flowing under a completely calm surface.
"I don’t know about Rindo and the others, but I doubt you have fallen behind anyone."
"Can I take that as a compliment from Professor Aldric?"
"Anyway, have you completed your first evolution?" Aldric ignored him and changed the subject.
"Yes, I completed my first evolution." Lian nodded, there was nothing to hide about completing an evolution.

"Didn’t you want to explore around Base Number Nine for a few days before coming back? There are several dungeons in that area, and for someone who has just evolved, it was a good chance to grow, you should understand the value of Fragments now."
"Besides killing monsters and doing Quests, you should also know that clearing some dungeons and doing explorations can give you Fragments."
Lian knew this, when he was first summoned to the Ruined Realm, when he and Seris discovered Frostfallen City, the system had rewarded them with Fragments.
Of course, getting Fragments through these two methods was very difficult and depended on luck, and the system was not always that generous.
Still, if he had nothing else to do, he would probably have done the same.
But—
"I have some things to take care of." He answered, then added.
"I also have an armor waiting for me for nine months, and knowing that blacksmith’s personality, I’m sure he is extremely angry with me, and I also need to see my friend."
"Kain?" Aldric asked immediately.
"Oh, I didn’t expect you to know his name."
"I know the names of my students, and in any case, I am not the only one who knows him these days."
"What do you mean?" Lian became serious this time.
"Your friend is currently one of the main topics of discussion in the capital, and more specifically, he is someone the major guilds are trying to recruit." Professor answered.
"Oh?" The young Vorhelm was a little surprised at first, but then he smiled.
He did not expect this, at least not to the point that even Professor Aldric would speak well of him, he knew that with the legacy that boy had obtained, sooner or later he would attract attention.
And it seemed he had really managed to make a name for himself during this time.
"Before you get too happy, you should know that his situation in the academy is not good." But Aldric continued almost immediately.
"What do you mean?" Lian’s smile slowly disappeared.
"He has become isolated."
"What?" His face became completely serious, how could someone that the biggest guilds were trying to recruit become isolated in the academy?
"You were not here, and many things changed inside the academy during these nine months, and a considerable part of these changes is related to a student named Roderick."
"Roderick." Lian’s eyes became slightly cold.
That name.

The man who, before he entered the Special Area, was more like an annoying mosquito than a real threat, and during this time, he had completely forgotten about him, he had become this worthless in his eyes.
But apparently, nine months had not been wasted for him either.
"I heard you have some history with him." Aldric watched his reaction.
"You could say that."
"Then you should probably ask Kain for the details, as long as the academy rules are not directly broken, I do not get involved in the kids’ conflicts."
Lian thought about the last word for a moment.
kids
Some of those same "kids" could probably destroy a building with their fists now.
But from Aldric’s point of view, they were apparently still children.
"Thanks, I’ll ask him when I see him." In the end, he also nodded.
"He’s here?" He immediately asked another question.
"He should be." Aldric answered.
"You’re not sure?"
"I’m not in charge of attendance at the dormitory."
"That makes sense."
"A general call has been sent for the final exams, all students have to return, even those who spend most of their time in the Ruined Realm."
That was good news, so he was probably here, or at least he would return soon.
And it was not only Kain, almost their entire generation should have returned, rivals, the Elite Class students, and Roderick and Elena.
It seemed he had chosen a good time to return.
The conversation continued for a few more minutes, but nothing else important was brought up.
"If you have nothing else for me, can I go?" He finally stood up from the chair and asked.
"Sure." The professor nodded.
Lian walked toward the door and put his hand on the handle.
Now his first task was clear, he had to find Kain and find out what had happened while he was gone.
But just before he opened the door, Aldric’s voice came from behind him again.
"Wait."
"Yes?" The young Vorhelm kept his hand on the handle and turned halfway around.
"Do you remember Commander Gareth?"
Lian turned completely around, going over the name in his mind for a moment, but only for a moment.
How could he forget? Commander Gareth, the man responsible for dealing with the incident of the fallen border city.
One of the first real and bloody events he had faced after becoming an Awakened.
The same city that had been occupied by monsters, and later it was discovered that the truth behind it was more complicated than they had thought, and unfortunately, the real culprit had escaped.
"Yeah, why?"

chapters.title: Chapter 414: An Old Case
paragraphs: "Yeah, why?" Lian answered calmly.
His hand was still on the door handle, but after hearing Commander Gareth’s name, he was no longer in a hurry to leave.
It had been a considerable amount of time since he had last heard that man’s name, and the fact that the professor suddenly mentioned him meant it had to be something important.
"They caught the person responsible for the border city incident." Aldric said in his usual cold and serious tone.
His hand also stopped on the handle.
There was only one person in the case of that city who could really be considered the main person responsible.
"They caught him?" He then asked with some surprise.
"A few weeks ago." The professor nodded and confirmed.
Lian turned completely toward him, more than ten months had passed since the border city incident.

It was not a short amount of time, but considering that the man had managed to escape from him and the security forces surrounding the area and disappear without leaving any clear trace, finding and arresting him was not a small matter.
Not to mention that this person had escaped many times before and had managed to stay hidden for several years.
It seemed the government and the Awakened Federation had decided to take this matter more seriously, probably because they were truly worried about what he wanted to create.
"Gareth personally told me that if you came back, I should tell you about this, apparently there is something he needs to discuss with you."
"With me?" Lian raised an eyebrow slightly.
"That’s what he said, he also has your number. He sent you a message. Reply to him directly." Aldric added after a short pause.
"Sure." The young Vorhelm thought for a few moments, then nodded.
This time he opened the door and left the office, and the door quietly closed behind him.
He had only walked a few steps away from the office when the memories of the border city returned to his mind.
That man with completely white eyes.

A voice that was sometimes so calm and logical that it was easy to forget its owner was a madman, and the next moment it would shake with so much excitement that it became clear something was very wrong inside that man’s mind.
Among all the people Lian had seen until then, he was one of the strangest.
A man who did not even have killing humans as his main goal, the victims were only raw materials to him, that man wanted to create.

More specifically, a monster from a new species of creatures, something that nature had never created, a creature that according to that madman himself was supposed to be the perfection of all creation.
Of course, he had managed to create something, but in the end, it was fortunately killed by him, and all his achievements were destroyed by him.
And it would not be wrong to say that the white-eyed man absolutely hated him and would probably do anything to kill him and get rid of his hatred.
Lian had managed to face him on the last day he was in that city, but the white-eyed man had eventually escaped.
And now he had finally been caught.
"So they weren’t doing nothing, at least." Apparently Gareth and the security forces had not given up the hunt during these nine months.
But the strange part of the matter still remained, why did that commander want to talk to him?
This should not have anything to do with him anymore, he was only a student who had gone there as part of a mission and had also completed his job.
Lian thought about this question for a few seconds, then shrugged, his phone probably had more information.
The rest of the way to the dormitory passed without any trouble, unlike before.
There was no Darren, and no one came forward to stop him, and a few minutes later, he finally stood in front of the familiar dormitory building.
He looked at it for a moment, then entered.
The hallway still had almost the same old smell.
The voices of students talking came from different rooms, and although many faces were unfamiliar to him, the building itself had almost not changed.
Lian went up the stairs, and a few moments later, he stood in front of the door to his room.
He opened the door and stayed there for a few seconds.
Two beds, two desks and closets, chairs, and even some of the things he had left on the desk nine months ago were still almost in the same place.
It was a small room and there was nothing special about it.
But after sleeping on the ground for a month, inside a tent, or not sleeping at all, and after all those hardships one after another, this room suddenly looked like the best place in the world.
A smile appeared on his face, and then without any ceremony, he threw himself onto the bed.
The mattress sank under his weight and his head rested on the soft pillow, he closed his eyes and silence filled the room.
There was nothing here that could cause him trouble, danger, or disturbance, he could completely relax without any problems and simply enjoy his time as much as possible.

But it also felt a little strange, he had never thought that simply relaxing in this small dormitory would become so enjoyable, it was really impossible to imagine what would happen to you the next day.
For a few minutes he really did nothing and only lay there, his body was no longer tired.
After returning from death and completing his first evolution, even physically, he was probably in the best condition of his entire life.
But his mind needed a few minutes of peace.
After that he turned his head slightly, the bed across from him was empty and Kain was not there, however, his belongings were still in the room.
A few clothes and pieces of equipment, so at least it was clear that he still lived here and should be somewhere nearby.
"Wherever he is, he should come back soon." Lian said quietly, he had probably gone out for some reason and it was not unlikely that he would return within a few hours.
A few more minutes passed.
Then he finally got up from the bed, now he had to check something that had been waiting for him for nine months.
He sat beside the desk and reached into the small cabinet next to it, and after searching for a while, he found his phone.
It was completely turned off, which was natural, the phone had been left without a charge for nine months and it made sense that the battery was completely empty.
He connected it to the charger and waited for a few minutes, when the small power-on symbol finally appeared on the screen, he leaned back a little.
A few seconds later, the screen turned on, the new date, the time, and then the notifications started appearing one after another.
There were many of them, but most of them were not personal, Lian had never had a large social circle.
There were not many people who regularly sent him messages, and after entering the Special Area, this had not changed much either.
All of his friends except Kain had been with him there, and he also had no contact with any of his family members except his uncle.
When he ignored the academy’s automatic notifications, only three names really caught his attention.
Ironsoul the Blacksmith.
Commander Gareth.
And Uncle.
"Uncle?" Lian looked at the third name for a few moments.
The first two were understandable, the blacksmith had made his armor, and it was now clear why Gareth was looking for him.
But his uncle? They did not have a bad relationship, but their relationship was not the kind where they regularly sent messages to each other.
He tapped on the message, and there was only one message, he checked the time it had been sent, nine months ago, and exactly on the same day he had entered the Special Area.
Lian’s eyes narrowed slightly, he also opened the exact time, the message had been sent almost at the same time he entered the Special Area.
The message was even shorter.
"Take care of yourself, the weather isn’t good."
That was it, there was no explanation and no other message, and even this message seemed unclear.
Lian looked at the screen for a few seconds, at first glance, there was probably nothing special about it, a family member could say something like this before a dangerous mission.
The fact that his uncle knew he was entering the Special Area was not strange at all, with that man’s position and power, it was natural that he could find any information about him.

But the tone of the message was strange, his uncle did not send messages like this, maybe now because of what had happened, he was trying to pay more attention to him so he could at least gain his affection.
But the part about "the weather isn’t good" sounded like a warning, this was part of the hidden vocabulary of the Vorhelm family that was used to give warnings.
It meant that things had happened that could put you in danger and that you should be careful.
And he also did not think his uncle would want to use a code to talk to him so that others would not understand, he only wanted Lian to clearly understand how serious the situation was.
"Interesting..." Lian whispered quietly.

chapters.title: Chapter 415: A Reunion After Nine Months I
paragraphs: His finger stayed on the call option for a moment, but in the end, he did not touch it.
If he was going to talk to his uncle about this matter, he preferred to start the conversation when he had more time.
Besides, nine months had already passed since this matter and since this message.
And it was not as if he had no guesses.
"Could it be related to Darian?"
Whatever it was, he could ask about it later, now it was time for Ironsoul the Blacksmith.
The first message had been sent almost two weeks after he entered the Special Area.
"If you have time today, come here, I need to talk to you about a few final details of the armor."
Lian raised an eyebrow slightly, so the old man had reached something during the construction that needed his opinion.
The next message had come almost one month later.
"You didn’t come, I continued according to my own judgment."
Lian could not stop himself from smiling.
The next message came one week after that.
"The armor is ready."
His eyes shone for a moment, so it really was complete, his Ancient-Rank armor was ready to use.
The next message came another seven days later.
"Then why aren’t you coming?"
This time Lian gave a short laugh, he could imagine the old man’s face while writing the message.
A man who had probably spent several weeks working on the armor, and now its owner had not even shown up to see it.
The old man probably did not know that he had gone to the Special Area, and the next message confirmed it.
"I found out today that you were also one of the people in the Special Area, I’ll keep the armor for you for now."
Lian’s smile became a little calmer, then he typed a message.
"I’m back, thanks for keeping the armor for me, when can I come to pick it up?" He then sent it.
He looked at the message for a few seconds, and the corner of his mouth rose.
Finally, the armor he had ordered before entering the Special Area was ready.
After all the changes his body had gone through during his first evolution, he was really curious to see what difference Ancient-Rank equipment would make to his strength.
But there was still one more important message left... Commander Gareth.
Lian opened the conversation, the message had been sent only two weeks ago, so the arrest of the white-eyed man really was a recent event.
"I need to talk to you about the case of the fallen border city, we caught the main person behind the incident."
He continued reading.
"He has almost refused to cooperate since his arrest, but he said he would only agree to talk to you."
The young Vorhelm’s eyes narrowed slightly, and he read the last line.
"If you see this message after returning, let me know."
Lian did not move for a few seconds, the white-eyed man would only agree to talk to him.
That sick excitement in his voice when he talked about creating a new species, and the last moments of their confrontation.
That day the man had escaped, and he was not strong enough to stop him, but he had finally been caught.

Now things were different, he doubted that man could still be a threat to him or that he needed to worry about him, he had not even thought about him during this time and had almost forgotten about him.
"Why me?" He then quietly said.
Why? What did the white-eyed man want? He knew that man hated him in the strongest way possible, and it would not be strange if he wanted to try to kill him.
But why would he want to talk to him? Did he just want to argue with him with that sick mind of his? Did he want to threaten him? Or, like last time, did he want to say some nonsense?
For now, there was no way to know, he also had no interest in seeing that madman again, but since the commander himself had asked him, he had no problem meeting that madman one more time.
"I’m back, I arrived in the capital today."
The message was sent, and then he lowered the phone for a moment.
Until a few minutes ago, he only planned to find Kain and pick up his armor, now three separate matters were waiting for him.
His uncle, Gareth, and Ironsoul the Blacksmith, and this was probably only the beginning of the things that had happened during his nine months away.
Lian raised his phone again, almost none of the remaining notifications were personal, and all of them had been automatically sent by the academy to all students.
Changes to the academic calendar, reports from Base #3, student rankings, mission notifications requested by the academy, and finally, the official call for the final exams.
He opened a few of them, but soon realized that he would need much more time to understand all the changes from the past nine months.
More important than these automatic notifications was reading the news about the country and the situation in the Ruined Realm.
Although he had heard a few things here and there, they were only random pieces of information, and he had no idea how the situation of their world and the Ruined Realm had been during this time.
His finger moved toward the news section to take a look at them, but just before he opened it—
Click.
The sound of the door unlocking came, and he raised his head.
The door slowly opened, and a young man with brown hair entered the room, Lian first saw his face and then noticed the changes.
Kain’s hair was longer.
Not enough to completely change his appearance, but it was no longer as neatly short as before, and part of his hair had fallen over his forehead.
His face also looked more mature, his shoulders were wider and his body was more trained, even the way he stood showed that he had gone through many battles during these nine months.
But his eyes were the same, except that there was a kind of tiredness and pressure deep inside them.
Kain took one step into the room and his eyes fell on his own bed, then he saw his friend, and his foot stopped there.
The young Vorhelm also said nothing for a few seconds.
They had not seen each other for nine months, and for both of them, the other had almost disappeared from their world for part of that time.
They only looked at each other for a few seconds, and then they smiled almost at the same time.
"You finally decided to come back after nine months?!" Kain said with a voice full of laughter, excitement, and a lot of disbelief.
"We got into a little too much trouble in there." Lian answered with a laugh.
"A little? Nine damn months!" The Chosen of Light quickly walked forward.

When he reached him, the first thing he did was punch his friend hard on the shoulder, although compared to the things Lian had recently endured, it was more like a friendly hit, and then they firmly shook hands.
"Bastard, I really thought you were dead." Kain said with a wide smile, but for a moment, a very small amount of moisture could be seen in his eyes.
"Well, you weren’t exactly wrong."
"What? What do you mean?"
"We got trapped there, and you can’t even imagine what we faced." Lian sat on the bed again.
"You also can’t guess what happened here while you were gone." Kain kept the same smile for a moment, then his smile became a little strange.
The young Vorhelm thought about the sentence for a moment, but his friend did not give him more time, he went toward his own bed and sat down directly across from Lian.

For a moment, the scene was almost like nine months ago, two friends and two beds facing each other, and a normal conversation in the dormitory, but the appearance of both of them showed that time had really not stopped.
Kain had changed, and Lian? Probably much more.
"You first, I heard only about one-third came back, is that really true?." The Chosen of Light immediately leaned forward with curiosity.
"Yeah."
"Damn..."

chapters.title: Chapter 416: A Reunion After Nine Months II
paragraphs: The number on paper was one thing, but hearing it from someone who had actually been there was something else, and the deaths of this many Awakened was not a small matter.
"What about Seraphina? Is she okay?" Kain lowered his eyes for a moment, but almost immediately raised his head again.
Lian nodded.
"She’s fine, her injuries are completely healed, and there is no special danger, she should return to the academy with the others tomorrow." Lian added.
"Thank God she’s okay, and what about the rest of your group?"
"Our academy group was lucky, none of us died." The young Vorhelm answered without hesitation, among all the other groups that had been sent there, they could be considered the luckiest.
Not only did none of them die, but they had also somehow taken the lead in the Main Quest and among the other Awakened in the Special Area.
Of course, One himself had died, but he probably did not need to explain that detail right now.
"Good... really good." Kain’s smile returned, then he stayed silent for a few seconds before the familiar curiosity from the past returned to his eyes.
"But one thing, did you really fight an entire civilization?"
"The rumors reached here too? Of course, I shouldn’t expect anything less, I guess the Special Area is the number one trend in the news these days."
"Dude, you came back after nine months and only one-third of you came back, what did you think people would talk about? The weather?"
"Yeah, I can underestand that." Lian gave a short laugh and then started explaining, and he briefly talked about the Cindari.

The civilization that had formed in that world, about their cities, and then about how they occupied the city, and a little about the Giant Forest and especially the nest of that giant bird where he had appeared.
In the end, he explained the part about the Black Silence very briefly, and when he finished his explanation, Kain only looked at him for a few seconds.
"Man... I feel like you guys had a much better time than us."
"That’s an interesting definition of having fun, and do you know how many times each of us came close to death? The fact that I’m still alive is almost a miracle."
"I killed monsters for nine months, and you fought an ancient civilization." Kain shrugged.
"And I almost actually died." Lian added dryly.

"When you put it like that, I feel even happier that I didn’t come, but I still would have preferred to be with you and Seraphina instead of spending these nine months." He sighed, it was clear that he was not talking about having fun at all.
Things had simply happened to him during these nine months that made him wish he had entered the Special Area instead of facing those things.
Lian looked at him, he had really missed this idiot, but he could also see that these nine months had not been easy for him.
A few moments later, Kain looked at Lian more carefully, and his eyes moved over his shoulders and the different structure of his body.
"By the way... did you complete your first evolution?
"One or two days ago." The young Vorhelm answered.
"Just now?"
"You know that less than thirty days have passed for us in there, right? You guys were the ones who had nine months, not us."
"Makes sense, but what level are you?"
