"Finally! At least now you understand how painful it is."
"That’s true, and collecting them won’t be easy either."
"Before the first evolution, everyone thinks a Fragment is just a side reward, then you evolve and suddenly the system needs Fragments even for you to breathe."

"You mean they didn’t clearly explain the importance of Fragments in high school classes? After the first evolution, they explained it very clearly, we just didn’t know that instead of needing a few or a few dozen, we would need several thousand, you were just too lazy and didn’t know this."
Kain became silent after hearing that sentence and preferred not to answer anything about his laziness.
"So you also completed your first evolution." Lian said after seeing that.
His friend’s smile suddenly changed, he realized at that moment that he had made a mistake, that question was exactly the opportunity Kain had been waiting for.
The young man sat straight on the bed, moved his shoulders back, pushed his chest slightly forward, and said with completely fake pride.
"I didn’t just evolve." He deliberately waited for a few seconds, then added with a wide smile.
"I’m Level 34 now, and I’m not far from my second evolution." He then continued proudly.
Level 34, Lian thought about the number, before entering the Special Area— both he and Seraphina were ahead of Kain.
Now? He was Level 23, and he was not sure about that girl, but since she had not completed her evolution, she should still be Level 20.
Kain had gotten almost eleven levels ahead of him, this difference was not small, but it also did not matter, he was happy for his friend that he had managed to progress so quickly.
"Congratulations, now you’re even ahead of me." This sentence was correct in terms of level, but in other areas... not so much.
"Don’t worry, from now on I’ll look after you myself." Kain proudly put his hand on his chest.
"Are you sure?" Lian looked at him for a few seconds, then the corner of his mouth rose slightly, and he asked suspiciously.
"Completely."
"But Professor Aldric said you became isolated in the academy, how are you going to protect me like this?
And Kain’s smile disappeared almost at the same moment, and the pride that had been on his face a few seconds ago disappeared.
His eyes moved away from him for a moment and stopped on the floor, his shoulders, which had been pulled back proudly a few moments ago, dropped slightly.
The change was small, but to Lian it meant more than any explanation, and his eyes narrowed slightly, so Aldric had told the truth, in fact, maybe he had made it sound softer than reality.
"So it’s true."
The boy did not answer and only gave a short sigh.
"And judging by your face, ’isolated’ is the polite version."
"Lian—"
"Tell me what happened." The young Vorhelm said completely seriously this time.

There was no threat in his voice, no pressure, but Kain knew him well enough, and if he did not explain, Lian would find the answer himself, and his way of finding the answer would probably not be much calmer than simply explaining it to him.
He hesitated for a few seconds, then put his hand through his longer hair and pushed it back.
"It’s a long story." He finally opened his mouth.
"I lost nine months, a few more minutes won’t matter." Lian leaned against the wall behind the bed.
Kain looked at him more carefully for a moment, then took a deep breath and looked toward the window for a moment, when he turned back, his expression was serious.
"After you entered the Special Area... the first few weeks were almost completely normal."

"Everyone was talking about your departure, the things you might experience there, and the opportunities you had gotten, I also spent most of my time in the Ruined Realm, hunting and helping expand the territory of the base."
"Academy life continued normally for a while." His eyes became cold, and he paused for a moment.
"And then Roderick came back, and Elena was with him." Kain said.
Roderick.
Elena.
The first was only a hateful and jealous bastard from high school who had bothered him for a long time because of his own complexes after Lian failed the Awakening process.
And the other was a name that had been pushed into a far corner of his mind for almost two years, and during this one year, it had not even crossed his mind.
The same girl who had once been a much closer part of his life.
Kain looked at him, and his expression now had no trace of the jokes from a few minutes ago.
"From that moment... everything in the academy changed." He finally added.

chapters.title: Chapter 417: The New Order In Academy I
paragraphs: "Since then... everything in the academy changed."
Lian was sitting on the bed across from him and said nothing.
The sudden change in Kain’s expression was enough for him to understand that whatever he was about to hear was probably much more than a simple fight between a few students.
Of course, he had expected it and could already guess some things about what had happened.
"How?" he then asked.
His friend stayed silent for a few seconds, as if he was deciding where to start the story.
In the end, he raised his head.
"When Roderick came back, he wasn’t the same Roderick you knew anymore, well, in terms of personality he was still the same trash... but not in terms of power."
"At least one thing stayed the same." Lian could not stop his short smile.

Of course, Roderick had already been a powerful Awakener from the beginning, a four-star class was no joke and combined with an S-Rank talent that was expected to be his, it was a very dangerous combination.
And because of that, he had always been noticed by the big guilds in the country.

"Unfortunately, anyway, when he came back he was level 18, it didn’t take long for him to complete his first evolution and after that he spent almost all his time between Base #3 and different missions."
"His family and the guild behind him also provided him with everything he needed; equipment, resources, artifacts... everything."
This part was not very surprising.
Roderick had already made it clear from the first day that his strength was not only because of his personal talent.
A rich family, connections, talent and then becoming a member of one of the strongest guilds in the country, he basically had everything.
But Kain had not finished yet.
"He also completed several big missions, not those missions where he just uses his sponsors’ names and lets others do the work, he actually fought himself."
Lian had no problem accepting this fact.
If Roderick was going to face him again, he preferred him to actually have become stronger instead of still being the same arrogant boy from nine months ago.
Of course, he still doubted that idiot could be considered "strong" against him.
"At first I thought that was the only problem, I thought he came back, became stronger, became a little more arrogant and would be more annoying than before and that was it."
"But that wasn’t the problem." The young Vorhelm looked at him and could guess the next words.

"No, the problem was that he knew how to gather other people around himself too, although saying that he knows how is wrong, most of them are more afraid of him, he is strong and he also has strong supporters behind him."
Lian quickly understood what Kain meant.
The small group that had surrounded Roderick nine months ago was no longer just a few students who praised him, during this time it had become something much bigger.
It was not something like an official association and not even a registered group with a clear name or symbol but almost everyone in the academy knew it by one simple name.
Roderick’s group.
It was more like a gang of bullies, with the difference that they were not really bullies in normal situations, at least not in the traditional way.
"First, a few people from the elite class joined him, then a few people from rich families, then hunting teams, healers and even a few older students."
"By force?" Lian slowly nodded, gathering this many people around yourself really required talent and ability.
Kain snorted.
"No. This is the part that makes what he is doing worse, he created an exclusive system, he doesn’t force you to join, but if you join, your growth speed becomes much faster.

"You can easily find a hunting team, good missions are introduced to you first, you can get equipment at better prices, resources are traded between the members and you can even get better places for training which are controlled by the guild behind him in the Ruined Realm."

"And he created a kind of unofficial structure where the higher your position in the group is, the more benefits you can use and since then, the people closest to him in the academy have been treated with a lot of respect."
Lian now understood better why the atmosphere of the academy had seemed strange when he entered.
That guy had basically turned the entire academy into his playground and he doubted Rindo would be happy about this when he returned.
Cassian, as the possible next president of the Student Council, and Seraphina, as the vice president of the Student Council, would also be angry about this.
But could they do anything? After all, no law had been broken.
Kain continued.

"In the beginning, if you weren’t part of his group, there was no problem, but recently, because almost a large part of the academy has joined his group, anyone who isn’t in that group is systematically and unwillingly screwed over."

"No one directly comes and says they will make your life miserable, everything just becomes a little harder; you can’t find the right team, some deals don’t reach you, some missions are already full before you even hear about them."
Considering that most Awakeners had two-star and three-star classes, they had no choice but to hunt in groups and basically did not have enough ability to hunt alone.

Because of that, not being able to find a team inside the academy caused them a lot of problems, they were forced to join teams where the age difference was very large and they could not agree with each other on many things at all.
"That’s smart." Lian narrowed his eyes slightly.
"You weren’t supposed to compliment him." Kain stared at him for a moment.
"I didn’t compliment him, I said it was smart."
Those two things were different to him.
Roderick might be someone he did not like, but at least he was apparently not stupid enough to maintain his control by openly beating students.
Real power did not always have to be obvious.
Sometimes it was enough for people to know that standing beside someone would make their lives easier and in the academy it was clear that if they chose him, their lives would become easier.
"Anyway, he didn’t do all of this alone, Elena is also with him and she has changed a lot too, she completed her first evolution and the last time her level became public, it was 31."
"Good." Lian only nodded.
"That’s all?"
"What am I supposed to say?"
"I don’t know, something. After all, you two had a past." Kain shrugged.
"Exactly, the key word is past." Lian said calmly.
Kain studied his face for a few more moments.
Then he gave a small smirk.
"Okay, okay, apparently you really got over her."
The young Vorhelm did not answer, because there was nothing else to say, whatever Elena had done during the past nine months was no longer an important part of his life.
"But you didn’t explain why you became isolated.
Kain stayed silent for a moment and then his expression changed slightly.
"And my story with Roderick started somewhere else."
"At first he didn’t even have a problem with me."
"Really?"
"Yeah, he even asked me to join his group."
"What did he offer?"

"Almost everything, a fixed hunting team, help getting resources that could give me stats, equipment at a discount, a bigger share from group missions and a good position among his people." Kain started counting them.
"That was a tempting offer." Lian laughed loudly.
"Very."
"So why did you refuse?"
"I didn’t like his face. I only follow someone who is more handsome than me." Kain answered without the slightest pause.
"That’s a strong reason." The young Vorhelm stared at him with a completely serious expression for a few seconds and then nodded.
"Thank you." he said with satisfaction and pushed his chest out slightly.
The two stayed silent for a few seconds.
"Enough joking, what was the real reason?"

"Apart from the fact that the bastard had dared to make fun of you a few times in the past and had shown hostility toward you, I didn’t want to be under him, I didn’t have a good feeling about him from the beginning, people like him, when they give you something, expect you to give back several times more one day."
Lian nodded, this explanation sounded more like the Kain he knew.
"I refused him and nothing special happened at that time either, I thought it was over."
But it was not over.
About one month later, the rumors started.
That the people inside the Special Area were trapped, that they had probably failed and that maybe no one would come back alive.
The Federation had announced several times that such claims had no reliable basis and that exploring a Special Area could take months.
But a rumor did not need truth to survive, it only needed fear and they had already been inside for more than a month and there was still no news from them.
These kinds of rumors were always spread from some baseless sources during times like this and some idiots believed them.
"One day we were in the training hall and Darren was there with a few other people."
Lian could almost guess the rest of the story.
"They started talking about you."
Kain stayed silent for a few seconds and then copied a mocking voice.
"Darren said: ’Could that bastard really be dead? Maybe God finally took revenge for me.’"

Lian’s eyes narrowed slightly, he was not angry, he did not get angry at the words of a clown, it was more that Darren’s belief that God would directly interfere to take revenge for a defeat at the academy was really ridiculous.
"I ignored him, I really had no intention of getting into a fight but then one of the people beside him said that you probably ran away the first time you saw real danger and died there."
"That was when I stood up."

chapters.title: Chapter 418: The New Order In Academy II
paragraphs: Lian could see the scene in his mind, but that was exactly the problem, just by hearing it, he could tell that it had been a trick and a trap.
"I told him to say it again." Kain said calmly.
The man had laughed and said it again, and the result had been an official duel.
"Did you beat him that badly?" the Young Vorhelm asked.
"It depends on what you call ’that badly.’"
"How many days was he in the medical center?"
"Three weeks."
"Then that badly." Lian stayed silent for a few seconds and then nodded.
"He said it again himself, it was his own fault for daring to make fun of my friend." Kain shrugged.
"You know it was a trap?"
"A trap?"
"Right, they wouldn’t say things like that in front of you for no reason when they knew you were my best friend, their goal was to provoke you and they succeeded."
"Damn... so it was my own stupidity." Kain hit his forehead with his hand.
Anyway, it was something that had already happened and could no longer be changed.
That duel was the first time Kain’s name had really spread throughout the academy.
Not only because of the violence he had shown but also because of the power he had shown, before that, many people only knew him as Lian Vorhelm’s friend.
After that, not anymore, he became known because of the power he had shown, because he had dared to beat one of Rodrick’s men almost to death.
"Then Rodrick came to me." Kain continued.
"Was he angry?"
"No, he was very calm, I didn’t think much about it at the time but now that I think about it, it’s strange, and he came and asked, ’You caused all this trouble because of a dead man?’"
"I told him that dead man was my friend." Kain’s face became cold as he remembered that moment.
"Then he said I should accept that you were not coming back anymore, and I told him he could keep his delusions to himself and that I was sure you would come back soon."
"What did he say after that?" Lian asked calmly.
"He said then stay alone until that happens." Kain gave a bitter smile.
And apparently, he had meant exactly that.
After that, everything happened so slowly that he had not expected it.
So slowly that it was not even possible to choose one specific day as its beginning.
First, one of the hunting teams Kain had worked with several times said that they were full.
Then another group canceled his mission.
Some people who used to train with him regularly slowly started keeping their distance.
Mission invitations became less frequent and if he wanted to do academy missions, he had to go alone.
Parties and student gatherings no longer had his name on them.
Even some people who had no problem with Kain preferred not to be seen too close to him when Rodrick’s people were around.
"No one directly said Rodrick told them not to work with me, of course, there was no need, it was completely obvious." Kain said mockingly.
Lian said nothing, now the strange atmosphere of the academy when he had entered finally made complete sense, those looks, those distances, this was not just the popularity of a student.
It was a network.
He could understand the goal behind that bastard’s actions, first he had used a trap to find an excuse to deal with Kain, the only person in the academy who was not considered a member of his group.

He had probably only been after Kain at first because he wanted to humiliate him and then, after Lian returned, show him that he had taken not only his former fiancée but also his best friend away from him.
Bastard actions that came from his old grudges.
But after seeing this boy’s real power in that duel, he had decided to either make him submit to him somehow or make his life miserable.
"At first I thought it would take a few weeks and then end, but it didn’t." Kain continued.
"And what did you do? Just watched?"
"What was I supposed to do? Beg them to let me hunt monsters with them again?"
The corner of Lian’s lips rose slightly.
No.
That was not like Kain at all.
And if it had been like this, considering that this boy had not only managed to complete his first evolution but had also reached his current level, it meant only one thing.
"So you went alone."
"Yeah."
The first month was hard, very hard, Kain was used to group hunting, one person held the enemy, one person supported them and one person covered the back.
But when he was alone, every mistake came directly back to him and every mistake could have been the last mistake of his life, because after that he would die.
"Three times I almost died but then I learned what I had to do." Kain said completely normally.
He had been forced to learn, he had no choice, if he wanted to reach his goal, if he wanted to not fall behind Seraphina and Lian, he had no choice but to keep becoming stronger at any cost.
First he had learned how to choose an escape route, then, how to check the area before fighting. How to follow a monster for hours without being seen.
Where to set traps, when to retreat and more importantly when not to fight at all.
Slowly, what was supposed to be a punishment had become the best training of his life.
"When you don’t have a team, you either become smarter or you die, for now I chose the first option."
"Good choice." Lian smiled.

Unfortunately, four-star classes had a hard time hunting alone, it was not that they could not do it, unlike three-star, two-star and one-star classes that did not have such potential even at their best, a four-star class could do it.
But it was not easy, besides individual power, they needed intelligence and battle sense and had to learn exactly everything Kain had learned.
But five-star classes had an easier time with this, especially if they had at least an A-rank talent.
"I think so too."
But the point that changed everything happened a few months ago, the point that turned him into a rising star.
"I was level 31 and I happened to find a dungeon, but unfortunately, its boss was a level twenty-four Fallen Monster."
Lian’s eyes changed slightly, this time the number was not small, especially for a normal level 31 Awakener there was a very high chance of certain death.
"Yeah, I know." Kain saw his reaction.
A level 24 Fallen Monster was, in terms of real power, comparable to a normal level 37 or 38 monster.
Maybe even higher.
For a level 31 Awakener, a direct fight was almost suicide.
"You were alone?" Lian asked.
"Completely."
"How long did it take?" considering that he was still alive, it was clear that he had either succeeded or escaped and from his tone, the second one did not seem likely.
"Almost six hours."
Kain had not defeated that creature with raw power, that monster had chased him for six hours and he had kept changing its path, leading it to specific places.
He had set traps, created wounds, pulled back, returned again, used up his energy and only when the monster had become weak enough, he entered the final battle.
"In the end, I almost lost my left arm." He added very casually.
"You sound a little too proud of that part."
"Because I still have it, besides, it’s proof that I succeeded." He raised his left hand and moved his fingers.
Lian sighed.
Even so, he could not deny that he was impressed, Kain had been strong before they left.
But this Kain was different.
The System had not ignored the hunt either, after killing the Fallen Monster, a title had been registered for him.
[One-Man Hunter]
This title had been given to him because he had completely hunted a very powerful monster without direct help from others.
Its effect was not very exaggerated; it only slightly increased his resistance, speed and physical strength when chasing and fighting a target alone.
But the title itself was enough and when he brought the monster’s body to the academy to prove that he had killed it and then sold it, that was when the real noise started

chapters.title: Chapter 419: The New Order In Academy ( Final )
paragraphs: the title itself was enough and when he brought the monster’s body to the academy to prove that he had killed it and then sold it, that was when the real noise started
The hunting report entered the news and social networks of the academy students.
Then his name moved higher in the student rankings and then, when he sold the body at the Awakeners Association store, even more attention was drawn to him.
And very soon Kain’s name went beyond the academy and students started calling him more simply, Kain the Lone Hunter.
"I don’t like that name, I feel like it doesn’t sound very impressive." Kain said with a frown.
"I like it." Lian laughed loudly.
"Because it’s not your name."
"Exactly."
The problem for Rodrick was that his plan had the opposite result.
His goal had been for Kain to slowly become weaker without a team, resources and social support, until he had no choice but to submit to him and beg for forgiveness.
But Kain had become stronger and worse than that, he had become famous.
There were five rankings in the academy and one of them was the ranking for students’ solo hunts.
And Kain was ranked first in it while Rodrick was lower in the same category.
That did not mean Kain was stronger than him but because Rodrick took part more often in group missions and large operations.
But Kain was better at solo hunting and people loved stories like this.
A student without the support of a great family, without a group, without unlimited resources who entered the Ruined Realm alone and hunted monsters much stronger than himself.
That was what made his name one of the main topics among the young generation of the capital.
"So that’s why you became famous." Lian finally understood Aldric’s words, killing a Fallen Monster alone was a notable achievement.
He himself had almost done something similar, but he had not made it public and had also sold the monster’s body secretly.
Otherwise, what he had done would have caused a much bigger shock, along with disbelief.
"You finally understand what an important person you share a room with." Kain raised his head proudly.
"But this important person still throws his dirty clothes on the chair."
He unconsciously looked at the chair, his clothes were scattered around the room and
"Fame comes with many responsibilities, cleaning is not one of them." He then said seriously.
Lian laughed, but his laughter disappeared very quickly, because one part of the story was still left.
"So they did this to you for nine months just because you defended me?" He asked quietly.
Kain immediately shook his head.

"Almost but not completely, that was only the beginning, after that I didn’t back down either, every time one of them came after me I answered, I beat several of them in duels and I also directly rejected Rodrick’s offer several times."
"So I don’t want to tell it in a way that makes me sound like a helpless victim, I also helped continue the fight."
"I understand." The Young Vorhelm only looked at him for a few seconds.
His tone was calm, too calm and Kain, who had been his friend for years, noticed it almost immediately.
"Lian."
"Hmm?"
"Don’t do anything."
"I haven’t done anything yet."
"Exactly that sentence worries me, he’s level 39 and you’re only level 23, I don’t want you to put yourself in danger." Kain stared at his face for a few seconds.
"Don’t worry, I’m not stupid enough to face someone I can’t handle." Lian answered honestly.
Kain became a little calmer, at least that answer was logical.
"But if he comes after me himself—"
"I knew there was going to be a ’but.’"
"I didn’t even say anything."
"You don’t need to, your face finished the sentence." And Kain became serious again.

"I’m not joking, Lian. Rodrick is not the same person he was nine months ago. He’s much stronger and it’s not only his family behind him; a large guild supports him and he also has many people among the students."
Lian slowly nodded.
He was not going to go after him right now to teach him a lesson, at least not yet.
Level 39 was no joke, especially with a four-star class, the resources of a great family and one of the most powerful guilds in the country.
From the point of view of a normal person, the difference between Rodrick and level 23 Lian was almost ridiculous.
Sixteen levels.
But he did not feel any special worry because level was not the only thing that determined power.
Besides, he was not afraid of any great supporter, not when he had even dared to stand against the Vorhelms.
"You really didn’t get worried when you heard level 39?" Kain checked his reaction.
"Should I have?"
"At least you could have pretended."
"I’ll practice pretending later." A level 39 Awakener? In the Special Area he had seen a giant bird that was bigger than any building.
He had seen a disaster that could destroy worlds and had fought hundreds of Cindari alone.
"Anyway... the final exams should start soon, right?" He asked after a short pause.
"The day after tomorrow." Kain nodded.

According to what both of them knew, parts of the exam included checking level and evolution status, measuring physical and mana power, solo fights, group competitions and the final ranking of the generation.
But nothing was certain.
"The teachers change some parts every year, half of the things they tell us might be rumors and on the exam day they might put something completely different in front of us." Lian smirked.
No one could know what the real content of the final term exam would be until the last moment.
"Anyway, how was the midterm exam?
"It wasn’t held because you guys were not here." Kain laughed loudly, they were lucky enough that instead of wasting their time because of an exam, they could continue hunting in the Ruined Realm.
The Young Vorhelm gave him an empty look, the midterm exams were not very important so it did not matter.
But the final exams were important, at least for the other Awakeners who had big goals for their future.

The results of these exams would be sent to the Awakeners Association and the great guilds and based on them, they would recruit some of the top-ranked students and might also give them additional benefits.
Almost everyone he knew was going to be there.
Kain, Rodrick, Elena, Darren, Rindo, Selina, Liana, Seraphina, Cassian, Ethan and Marcus.
And probably many students who had become big names of their generation during these nine months.
The timing of his return was really interesting.
"You only have one problem." Kain suddenly said.
"What?"

"Officially, your status has still not been updated, you were gone for nine months and to take part in the exam, you have to register your level and evolution status in the academy system again, the capital’s Awakeners Association also needs to receive your new information."
Lian nodded and he knew about this, he had done these things before and knew the process.
Right at that moment, his phone, which was lying on the bed beside him, vibrated.
Both of them looked at the screen, a new message had arrived.
He picked up his phone and looked at it.
The sender was the blacksmith Ironsoul and when he saw it, his eyes became a little brighter.
The old man had replied faster than he expected, he opened the message.
"You can come in an hour."
The corner of Lian’s lips rose, finally, after nine months, he could receive his Ancient Rank armor within an hour.
But almost immediately, a second message appeared.
"But there is a problem."
His smile stopped a little and Kain, who was looking at his face, raised an eyebrow.
"What happened?"
Lian had not answered yet when the third message arrived and this time he stared at it for a few seconds.
"After the armor was completed, it gained a feature that it was not supposed to have."
A short silence appeared in the room and he raised his eyebrows, a feature that it was not supposed to have? What did that even mean?
Lian did not take his eyes off the screen and then started typing.
"Is the feature good or bad?" and the message was sent.
Three seconds.
Five seconds.
The screen showed that the old man was typing and then the answer came.
"Well..."

chapters.title: Chapter 420: The Ancient Rank Armor! ( Ps Bonus - )
paragraphs: The door of Ironsoul forge opened with a short metallic bell sound.
A wave of heat coming from inside the workshop hit Lian and Kain in the face almost at the same moment.
There was nothing calm about this place.

The sound of hammers hitting metal could be heard from different parts of the workshop, the flames of several furnaces were burning deep inside the workshop, and orange sparks were thrown into the air from behind the blacksmith tables every few seconds.
Dozens of swords, axes, spears, and pieces of armor were hanging on the walls.
Some of them were even releasing a weak flow of mana while inactive.
It had been about nine months since the last time they came here, and during this time, it did not seem like anything had changed.
"Close the door! You’re letting the heat of the workshop escape!" Magnus shouted in a rough voice without even turning his head.
Lian looked at Kain and then closed the door behind them.
"I haven’t been here for nine months and that’s still the first thing you say? Don’t I get a better welcome?" he said with a faint smile.
The sound of the hammer stopped.
The old man standing behind the blacksmith table stayed still for a few moments, then put his heavy hammer on the table and slowly turned around.
Magnus looked almost exactly as Lian remembered him, the same hair and beard, and arms that, despite his old age, still looked more like the arms of a warrior than those of an old blacksmith.
And the same frown that seemed to be permanently carved into his forehead.
But when his eyes fell on him, his frown changed for a moment, enough for Lian to notice the surprise in his eyes.
"So you’re alive and doing well after all." Magnus said in a lower voice.
"I look like it, I guess? Did you expect me to be dead?"
The old man completely put the hammer aside and walked a few steps forward.

His eyes moved over Lian’s body once again, and this time he also noticed the changes after his first evolution; slightly wider shoulders, greater height, and a body that perhaps did not look very different from the outside, but its structure was no longer the same body from nine months ago.
However, there seemed to be something more important to Magnus.
"Nine months! I kept an Ancient Rank armor in my storage for nine months, just because its stupid owner decided to go into a Special Realm one day and disappear."

"Don’t think I did it for you, I worked on that armor for months. I wasn’t willing to see my masterpiece on the body of another idiot." The old man grumbled.
Then he pointed at one of his students and told him to stand in his place behind the furnace, then picked up a thick towel and wiped his hands.
"Before I show it to you, there are some things you need to know." Magnus said to Lian.
"The same problem you mentioned in the message?"
"We’ll get to that too." The old man stayed silent for a moment, then walked through the workshop, and the two of them followed him.
"Do you still remember that corpse you gave me?"
"Unholy Rank World Devourer Giant." Lian answered almost immediately.
Magnus nodded.
"World Devourer Giant." The old man repeated the name of the species in a serious tone.
"Before I cut that corpse apart myself, I thought the reports written about the bodies of these creatures were a little exaggerated."
"They weren’t?" Kain looked at him with curiosity.
"No."
They left the main part of the workshop and entered a narrower hallway.
Unlike the front part, almost no sound of hammers could be heard here, and it seemed that the walls had special protections.

"When people talk about World Devourer Giants, they usually only say one thing; their skin is very tough, this is the simplest and stupidest explanation that has been passed from person to person for a long time."
Lian listened silently, he had read exactly the same thing in books and on the internet, these giants were creatures that were admired because of their bodies.
Magnus raised his hand and tapped his own forearm with his finger.
"Their skin is only the first layer, the bones, muscles, joints, the tissues between the body parts, even the way their internal organs are placed... everything is built to handle pressure."
"The whole body is one single fortress." The old man’s eyes became a little more serious, and he had only just started explaining.
"If a normal monster takes a heavy hit to the chest, all the force is focused there, the skin tears, the bones break, the internal organs are crushed."

"But a World Devourer Giant is different, the structure of its body spreads part of the force around it; the shoulders, spine, sides, hips, and even the legs...to crush one point of its body, it is like having to fight its entire body."

"Then there is their body stability, when a World Devourer Giant fixes its weight on the ground, moving it is almost ridiculous, not because of earth magic or something strange; just the structure of its bones and muscles."
"So it’s like a mountain?" Kain asked thoughtfully.
"Almost." Magnus gave him a short look and then took a few more steps.

"And the last feature was what caused me the most trouble while making it, not that it was bad, no, on the contrary, what bothered me was that if all monsters had such a feature, could we really stand against monsters?"
"Oh? What? You’re raising my expectations too much." Lian asked with more interest.
"You should have high expectations, do you even know what kind of masterpiece you’re about to see? Anyway, this feature is Structural Memory." The old man added and stayed silent for a moment.
Young Vorhelm slightly raised his eyebrows, and it was clear that he expected more explanation.

"The body tissue of that creature hates changing its shape, bend it, press it, even break all of its parts; as long as its structure has not been completely destroyed, it tends to return to its original shape."
"Does it regenerate?" Kain asked.

"Not exactly, this is not body regeneration, it doesn’t create new tissue, but its structure tries to return anything that has changed back to its original place, you can stop regeneration but you can’t stop this."
The old man let out a short sigh.

"I thought that when I purified the materials, this feature would mostly disappear, but it didn’t, I tried every method I could, but every time it returns to its original form and nothing can stop it."
In simple words, it did not matter what happened to the armor, under any condition, it returned to its original state and became completely intact again just like it was at first.
The end of the hallway reached a simple stone wall.
For a moment, Lian thought the path had ended, but Magnus placed his hand on a small metal panel beside the wall.
Mana flowed through the panel, and thin golden lines lit up inside the stone.
Grrrrr...
The stone wall moved backward in two directions, and a staircase going down appeared behind it.
"You have a storage room under the forge?" Kain raised his eyebrows slightly.
"Did you think I would put high-rank equipment next to ordinary swords on the wall?" The old man said sarcastically.
The two entered behind him, and as they went down the stairs, the heat of the workshop slowly decreased.
The space became colder and quieter, every few meters, symbols could be seen on the walls, glowing with a weak light.
They went down almost three floors, and at the end of the stairs, there was a huge gate made of black metal.
This time, even Lian could feel the weak pressure of the protective arrays around it.
Magnus opened three separate locks, one with mana, one with a strange metal key, and the last one with a drop of blood, and finally the gate opened with a heavy sound.
The space behind it no longer looked like a storage room, it looked more like a hall for keeping special items.
A high ceiling and walls made of black stone, several separate platforms, each one inside its own protective field.
On one of them, there was a long sword that still had a weak flow of electricity moving around it even inside the barrier.
On another, there was a broken shield covered with red lines.
But Magnus walked past all of them, and his destination was at the end of the hall, there was a large stone platform inside a multi-layered container made of mana glass.
There was no cloth covering it and no box, and the armor was completely visible inside the protective field, and the moment Lian saw it, his steps became slightly slower.
Black.

That was the first thing that caught his attention, but it was not the blackness of normal metal, instead, the surface of the armor had a color between black and very dark gray, and in some parts, it looked more like polished volcanic rock than metal.
The light from the storage room lamps did not shine on it and instead most of the light seemed to disappear into it.
Very thin silver lines ran along the places where the armor plates connected, looking like natural cracks inside a mountain.
The armor covered the entire body, but unlike what he expected from its main material, it was not bulky.
The chest plates were not too thick, but they were locked together in several layers, creating something that looked like layers of tightly packed rock.
The shoulders were large, but not enough to limit movement, the forearms and lower legs were designed to be thicker.
The joint areas had more flexibility, and almost no exposed and unprotected point could be seen.
There were no horns, no crown, and no useless decorations, it was as simple and minimal as possible.
The armor did not need decorations, its own presence was enough, as if someone had cut a piece of a black mountain and turned it into armor.

chapters.title: Chapter 421: World-Devourer Bastion ( GT Bonus - )
paragraphs: Silence filled the room for a few moments, the armor in front of them was simply a complete masterpiece from an artistic point of view.
"Okay, I’m actually jealous now." Kain said seriously.
The corner of Lian’s lips rose, even he could not take his eyes off the armor, nine months of waiting had been worth it.
Magnus stood beside the wall of the container and deactivated several symbols, the protective layers shut down one by one, and finally the transparent barrier disappeared.
At that moment, the System panel appeared in front of Lian.
[World-Devourer Bastion]
[Rank: Ancient]
His eyes stayed on the rank for a moment.
Ancient.
Above S Rank.
An equipment that even many powerful Awakeners could not own during their entire lives.
And this one belonged to him.
"Before you touch it, I’ll explain." The old man warned him.
Lian stopped his hand, which had almost reached toward the armor.
"Most armor has a simple principle; be hard, take the hit, if the hit is stronger than what you can handle, break." Magnus tapped the chest plate with his knuckle.
A deep sound came from inside the armor.
"This one doesn’t work like that."
Another panel appeared.
[Mountain Frame — Passive]

"I took this structure from the body of that giant, when a hit lands on one point, the armor does not allow all the force to stay there. It spreads the pressure between the plates and transfers it through the internal structure to the rest of the body."
He pointed from the chest toward the shoulder, side, and lower part of the armor.
"If the hit lands here, the shoulders, spine, sides, hips, and even the legs take part of the pressure."
"So instead of one part being crushed, the whole armor takes the hit." Kain kept his eyes on the armor.

"Exactly, to break one point, you have to break almost the entire fortress and I can guarantee that the resistance of this armor is strong enough that the whole thing will not collapse that easily." Magnus nodded and looked at Lian.

Young Vorhelm gave a small smile, he liked this part, he really liked it, until now, his problem with armor was that they were destroyed too often, and if one part of them was destroyed, they became completely useless.
But it seemed this one did not have that problem.
The next panel appeared.
[Mountain Anchor — Active]
"This one was given to me by the giant’s own structure, when both of your feet are on a stable surface and you activate it, the armor locks the pressure of your body to the ground."

"Your resistance against being pushed back, thrown, knocked down, and having your stance broken becomes several times stronger, and part of the force of the impact is also transferred directly to the surface under your feet."
"Does it have any limitations?" Lian asked.
"It’s almost useless in the air, if the ground under your feet is destroyed, its effect becomes much weaker, and you also can’t fully use it while moving at high speed."
He nodded, it was logical, the ability was powerful, but it was not without conditions.
[Giant’s Momentum — Passive]
This time Magnus gave a small smile.
"This one will probably be the most useful for you."
"Why?"

"When you move directly forward, the structure of the armor focuses the mass and force of your body behind the point of impact, a direct punch, shoulder, full body collision, or landing from a height."
Lian was already calculating a combination in his mind.
Iron Fortress Charge already increased the force of his body when charging.
Now Giant’s Momentum also focused the mass of the armor and the force of direct movement behind the same impact.
With the new structure of his body, the result could be really unpleasant ...for the enemy, of course.
"This is the last feature I expected." Magnus said.
[Structural Memory — Passive]
The old man placed his hand on one of the forearm plates.
"If the plate bends, twists, or gets a surface crack, its structure returns to its original state."
Lian asked:
"Does it repair itself?"
"Yes, of course it has some limitations too, but generally, it repairs itself using the owner’s mana." He then continued in a more serious tone.

"But don’t think it’s immortal, if a piece is completely separated or destroyed, it cannot create new material from the air, but dealing a destructive amount of damage to this armor is not easy, this thing increases resistance and physical strength by at least 2500%, and it is also as tough as a mountain."
Lian nodded, even that was incredible for armor that was probably going to receive the strongest attacks again and again.
But there was still one problem, and he looked at the old man.
"So, which part of these is the problem? The problem you messaged me about?"
"None of them." Magnus became silent, his face returned to the same serious expression as before.
"The problem is that the armor I made...is no longer exactly the same armor I made."
"What do you mean?" Kain also frowned, the sentence they had just heard made no sense at all, what did it even mean?
The old man did not answer and only placed his hand on the chest plate of the armor and sent a little mana into it.
Several silver lines on the surface of the armor lit up, and a new panel appeared in front of them.
But this one was different from the previous panels.
[Unknown Growth Trait detected.]
[Mountain Evolution]
[The armor remembers pressure.]
"A growth trait?" Lian stayed still for a few seconds.
"Exactly." Magnus let out a heavy sigh.
[Mountain Evolution — Growth]
[Repeated survival against extreme physical pressure gradually reinforces the armor against similar structural forces.]
[Only significant physical and structural pressure can trigger adaptation.]
[Adaptation speed is dependent on intensity, frequency, and survival.]
[Each adaptation possesses a natural limit.]
[Current Adaptations: None.]
Lian’s eyes slowly narrowed, now he understood why Magnus had said "There is a problem" in his message.
Not because the ability was bad, but because it was too good.
"Well... I don’t exactly understand why this is bad." Kain read the text for a few seconds.
"Because I didn’t make it, and this part of the armor is not my work." The old man looked at him with a deep frown.

"I checked all the materials, I did every step of the creation myself, the World Devourer Giant’s body spreads pressure, rejects changes in its shape, and has insane toughness." He pointed at the panel with his finger.
"But it doesn’t learn from attacks, this should not be part of its structure."
Lian looked at Mountain Evolution again.

"If this armor is repeatedly exposed to one type of extreme pressure and survives, its structure will slowly make itself better at handling that same type of pressure, I don’t know exactly how fast its adaptation is and you need to test it."
"For example, if they attack it with fire again and again..." Kain said.
"Its structural resistance against fire will improve and it might even gain complete immunity." Magnus finished his sentence.
"Claws?"
"If the claw power is strong enough to really put the armor under pressure, the force distribution structure will adapt itself to that type of attack."
"And this is the bad part?" Kain looked at Lian.
"Idiot, the bad part is that I don’t know why this feature appeared." Magnus immediately answered.
"I have three possibilities, first, the giant you brought was not a normal example of its species."
"Second, one of the additional materials I used during the creation reacted with the giant’s tissue in an unexpected way."
"And third?" Lian asked.
"The rank."
"Normal equipment is nothing more than material and structure, the higher the rank of the materials becomes, the more their internal features show themselves."
"High-rank equipment can have skills, S Rank equipment may have several very powerful skills or a special effect."
Magnus looked at the armor again.
"But the materials used to make this thing are Unholy Rank... and they are extremely rare and unpredictable in their own way."
"Besides, sometimes when equipment truly reaches the Ancient Rank, it gains something unexpected."
"A unique feature." Kain added quietly.

"Exactly, something that may never happen again, even if you bring me another Unholy Rank World Devourer Giant corpse tomorrow and I make it again using exactly the same materials, the same furnace, and the same method, there is no guarantee that Mountain Evolution will appear again." The old man nodded.
Lian looked at the armor again. This was no longer just an Ancient Rank armor, it was a unique creation even among its own kind.
"If it were yours and you wanted to sell it, how much would it be worth?" Kain asked after a few seconds.
"If it were mine, I wouldn’t sell it." Magnus answered without hesitation.
"I didn’t ask if you would sell it or not, I said if you wanted to sell it, how much would you sell it for?"
"And I answered, I wouldn’t sell it."
Lian laughed.
"Hypothetically! Just give me a hypothetical price." Kain raised his hand with a disappointed expression.
"It doesn’t have a fixed price." The old man thought for a few seconds this time and then shook his head.
"An Ancient Rank armor is already rare enough, a full-body armor made from an Unholy Rank World Devourer Giant, and it also has a unique growth trait?"
He gave a smirk.
"This is no longer about the price, you have to see which of those crazy Level 100 Awakeners would be willing to give what to get it."

"And this is the bad part?" Kain looked at Lian.
"Idiot, the bad part is that I don’t know why this feature appeared." Magnus immediately answered.
"I have three possibilities, first, the giant you brought was not a normal example of its species."
"Second, one of the additional materials I used during the creation reacted with the giant’s tissue in an unexpected way."
"And third?" Lian asked.
"The rank."
"Normal equipment is nothing more than material and structure, the higher the rank of the materials becomes, the more their internal features show themselves."
"High-rank equipment can have skills, S Rank equipment may have several very powerful skills or a special effect."
Magnus looked at the armor again.
"But the materials used to make this thing are Unholy Rank... and they are extremely rare and unpredictable in their own way."
"Besides, sometimes when equipment truly reaches the Ancient Rank, it gains something unexpected."
"A unique feature." Kain added quietly.

"Exactly, something that may never happen again, even if you bring me another Unholy Rank World Devourer Giant corpse tomorrow and I make it again using exactly the same materials, the same furnace, and the same method, there is no guarantee that Mountain Evolution will appear again." The old man nodded.
Lian looked at the armor again.
This was no longer just an Ancient Rank armor, it was a unique creation even among its own kind.
"If it were yours and you wanted to sell it, how much would it be worth?" Kain asked after a few seconds.
"If it were mine, I wouldn’t sell it." Magnus answered without hesitation.
"I didn’t ask if you would sell it or not, I said if you wanted to sell it, how much would you sell it for?"
"And I answered, I wouldn’t sell it."
Lian laughed.
"Hypothetically!
Just give me a hypothetical price." Kain raised his hand with a disappointed expression.
"It doesn’t have a fixed price." The old man thought for a few seconds this time and then shook his head.
"An Ancient Rank armor is already rare enough, a full-body armor made from an Unholy Rank World Devourer Giant, and it also has a unique growth trait?"
He gave a smirk.
"This is no longer about the price, you have to see which of those crazy Level 100 Awakeners would be willing to give what to get it."

chapters.title: Chapter 422: Testing The Armor
paragraphs: Lian kept his eyes on the armor for a moment.
That sentence was clear enough, an Ancient Rank armor with such quality and materials could really not be given a price.
"Put it on." Magnus suddenly turned toward Lian.
He nodded and stepped forward.
"Put your hand there and give it mana." The old man then pointed at the chest plate.
The young Vorhelm placed his palm on the black surface of the armor and slowly put mana into it, just as he had been told.
For a moment, nothing happened, but suddenly the silver lines on the armor lit up.
[Owner Synchronization initiated.]
[Analyzing Mana Signature...]
[Compatible.]
[User recognized.]
Suddenly, a heavy mechanical sound came from inside the armor.
Click.
The chest plate opened, then the shoulders, forearms, and thighs...the armor pieces separated from their stands one after another.
He did not even have time to move when the leg guards suddenly wrapped around his lower legs first.
Click. Click.
The thigh plates moved up, the hip guard locked into place, and then the main chest plate separated from its stand and landed heavily against his body.
The forearms.
The arms.
The shoulders.
And finally, the last long plate was placed over his back.
Click!
The entire armor locked into place, and at that moment he almost felt as if a mountain had fallen onto his body, enormous pressure settled on his shoulders and spine.
Hundreds of kilograms, and maybe even more, his knees were ready to bend for a fraction of a second, but then the silver lines became brighter.
[World-Bearing Frame synchronized.]
The weight suddenly changed, of course, it was not that the armor had actually become lighter, Lian could still feel its huge mass, but the pressure was no longer on one point.
It was spread across his entire skeleton and body, as if the armor itself knew how to carry its own weight.
He moved his fingers and then tested more parts, his forearms, shoulders, neck, and then took a step, the movement was almost natural and there was no problem.
Well, there was almost no problem, the armor did not seem to fit his height very well, as if it had been made according to his old measurements.
It was not annoying because his physical changes were not very large, but it was something he could still feel.
"For a moment, it felt like several hundred kilograms landed on me." He then looked at the blacksmith and said.

"The armor is heavy because of the materials and base materials, its mass has not disappeared even now and the World-Bearing Frame only spreads its weight across the owner’s body structure." Magnus nodded.

Lian’s eyes became a little brighter, so the mass was still there and that meant all of that real weight would be present during an impact and his attacks could carry the weight of this armor with them.
It could indirectly increase the power of his attacks.
This armor was performing beyond his expectations.
"What you are thinking is correct, you can use the weight of the armor for heavy attacks." Magnus said as if he had read his thoughts.
The corner of the young Vorhelm’s lips rose even more, a skill like Iron Fortress Charge had just become much more dangerous and useful.
Then suddenly the armor moved.
"Wait." The old man frowned.

Lian stayed still, the shoulder plates opened a few millimeters with a quiet sound, the side part of the chest stretched, the thigh guards moved lower, and the back plate also changed its shape slightly.
All of this took less than three seconds, then the armor locked again.
This time it fit completely against his body and there was no extra pressure or empty space anymore.
"Damn..." The blacksmith stared for several seconds and then said quietly.
"What happened?" Kain looked at him.

"When I made it, I made it according to his measurements from nine months ago and apparently the armor itself just changed to completely fit and match his body." Magnus moved a few steps closer and checked the shoulder connection.
It seemed that Structural Memory did not only preserve its original structure and after fully connecting to its owner, it also learned the proper shape of his body.
The blacksmith clearly had not designed this behavior either, the armor was acting as if it had a consciousness of its own.
And at that moment, no one knew whether this was a good thing or not.
A few minutes later, the three of them left the treasury, but they did not return to the main workshop, Magnus took them through another path.
Behind the treasury, there was another stone corridor that led to a deeper part of the underground area.
At the end of it was a huge hall.
The floor and walls were reinforced with gray metal, and the marks of hundreds of impacts could be seen on their surfaces.

Several large machines stood on both sides, the machines included pressure columns, testing plates, impact absorption arrays, and in the center was a huge mechanical arm with a hammer almost the size of a human’s upper body at its end.
Kain looked at the machine and then at the old blacksmith.
"This is under your forge?"
"Yes."
"Exactly how many hidden floors do you have under your forge?" How could this small building next to a street have so many underground floors?
"More than you need to know." Magnus said without reacting, he was one of the greatest blacksmiths in the country and the Blacksmith Association.
His blacksmith shop was very important to the country and no matter how much was needed, they were willing to invest in him and his blacksmith shop.
"Go to the center." He then stood beside the machine’s control panel.
Lian entered the marked area.
"For now, do not activate any skills, just stand there."
He nodded.
Magnus made several adjustments, and the huge arm of the machine slowly moved back.
"Is this really going to hit him?" Kain looked at the size of the hammer.
"Yes."
"How strong is it? Because I doubt a normal hammer would even be worth testing."
"If you were wearing A-Rank armor, you would die instantly."
Lian silently looked at the hammer, one of his previous armors was A-Rank and had helped him a lot and its power was completely clear.
And this thing could destroy such armor instantly? Then what exactly was it made of to have such power?
At that moment, Magnus pulled the lever down and the hammer was released.
BOOOOOM!
The impact hit the young Vorhelm directly in the chest and his entire vision shook for a moment, enormous pressure entered his body.
The old man had not even told them the full power of that damn hammer, this thing was enough to turn the body of a Rank 35 Awakened into ashes instantly.
Lian even doubted whether his body could survive it without the armor.
And the strangest part was that the pain did not stay focused on his chest, the force spread through the entire armor like a wave.
Chest, shoulders, back, sides, hips, and finally legs, the ground under his feet cracked with a dry sound and his body moved half a step backward.
That was it, an impact that could turn his body into ashes without armor had been blocked just like that.
[Mountain Frame activated.]
[Impact dispersed.]
Lian stood there for several seconds and then ran his hand over the armor’s chest, there was no dent and the armor was completely fine.
"...It’s awesome." He then said with clear satisfaction.
"This is the only part that I am sure I made myself." Magnus crossed his arms over his chest.
"If this was the first test, what is the second test going to be?" Kain looked at the impact point, he had also felt the force of that impact, he was sure that his body had no chance of surviving it.
"Stronger." The old man looked at him and then prepared the machine again.
"Activate Mountain Anchor, both feet completely on the ground, do not move."
Lian adjusted the position of his feet and mana flowed inside the armor.
[Mountain Anchor activated.]
At that moment, he felt something strange, as if his weight had suddenly become several times heavier.

Not in terms of pressure on his body, but in terms of his connection to the ground, and the plates under his feet matched the surface below them and the structure of the armor locked the lower legs, thighs, hips, and back spine together in one line.
"I am ready." He then took a calm breath.
Magnus increased the power of the machine.
The second impact was even heavier and a wave of air came out from the point of impact.
Dust rose from the floor and the cracks under the young Vorhelm’s feet spread farther, part of the ground directly behind his heels broke apart.
But Lian did not move and the force of the impact passed through the armor and went directly into the ground.
When the dust settled, he was still standing in the same place.
"I am really jealous now, this armor is like a miracle for solo hunting." Kain said with admiration.
After the test ended, Lian opened the armor’s full panel.
[World-Devourer Bastion]
[Rank: Ancient]
[Type: Full Body Armor]
[Primary Material: Unholy World-Devourer Giant]
[Owner: Lian Vorhelm]
[Increases the defensive power of the user’s body by 2500% based on the user’s own resistance]
[Skills]
[Mountain Frame — Passive]
[Mountain Anchor — Active]
[Giant’s Momentum — Passive]
[Structural Memory — Passive]
[World-Bearing Frame — Passive]
[Unique Trait]
[Mountain Evolution — Growth]
[Repeated survival against extreme physical pressure gradually reinforces the armor against similar structural forces.]
[Current Adaptations: None.]
Unique traits for artifacts were extremely rare and depending on their type and abilities, they could be even rarer.
It was very rare for S-Rank or even Ancient artifacts to have a Unique Trait, and they were still mostly found among the strongest types of artifacts.
He read the panel for several seconds, comparing this armor to his previous equipment was almost ridiculous because it was not just a simple increase in resistance.
It changed the entire way his body took impacts and moved, and the strongest part of his body was also much more resistant now after the first evolution.
Magnus had noticed the same thing and moved a few steps closer and tapped the armor’s shoulder with his finger.

"Your body has clearly gone through positive changes too, and it can distribute and endure power and pressure very well, much better than what a human body should be able to do, to the point that it feels like it is not a human body..."
He had no idea how correct his guess was.

chapters.title: Chapter 423: The Price Is Already Paid
paragraphs: Lian looked at his armor one last time and finally, with a mental command, cut off the armor’s connection.
The silver lines on the plates turned off one after another and the quiet sound of the locks opening spread through the hall.
The chest plate opened slightly.
Then the shoulders, forearms, and leg guards separated from each other and the armor pieces moved away from his body in a controlled way.
He sent all of them directly into his own storage space.
Only when the last armor plate disappeared did something come to his mind that was necessary to complete the process of making his armor.
Money.
Lian had provided the body of the Unholy Rank World Devourer Giant himself, but even with the main material, turning that body into an Ancient Rank armor could not be cheap.
The extra materials and arrays that might have been used, and Magnus’s months of work and the equipment that had probably been used or even destroyed while working on such material.
"By the way, how much did the construction cost?"
"Already paid." Magnus answered normally.
"Excuse me? The cost was paid? How?"
"As I said, the full cost was paid, and by the President." The old man answered.
Lian frowned very slightly.
"I think I heard wrong, by whom?"
"The President."
"...What?" Kain, who was standing beside the wall, stared at the old man with his mouth half open.
Lian was also silent for a moment, what surprised him was not that the President knew about the existence of the armor.
The head of the Blacksmith Association personally knew about this order.
An Ancient Rank armor made from the body of an Unholy Rank World Devourer Giant was also not something that could be made without attracting the attention of high-level people.
Besides, to make this armor, Magnus had to get a special hammer from the Blacksmith Association and this alone could attract that man’s attention.
It was natural for the information to eventually reach the government as well.
But why would the President personally pay for the cost of his armor?
He thought in silence for a few seconds.
Two possibilities came to his mind before the others.
First, Kael.
If the President knew about Kael and what had happened between them, this payment might have been a kind of reward or thanks.
But the second possibility was his own name.
Vorhelm.
As far as he knew, the President’s relationship with the Vorhelm family was not very good, if this matter was really related to his family, paying for his armor would be strange behavior.
But his own relationship with his family was not good either and someone like the President should know about this, so it was possible that he wanted to invest in him by doing this.
"Why?" In the end, it was better to ask.
"I don’t know either. I sent the bill, the President’s Office paid it and I got my money, if you want to know why, ask him yourself." Magnus answered simply.
Lian stared blankly at the old man’s back for several seconds, the suggestion was very simple but there was one small problem.
How exactly was he supposed to randomly meet the President of the country?
Should he go in front of the President’s Office and say that he had come to ask about the money for his armor? Of course, maybe that would work too?
"Sure, next time I randomly see him on the street, I’ll ask him." He finally said sarcastically.
Kain could not stop himself from laughing, but the old man did not care at all.
"Your problem." He answered without mercy.
The young Vorhelm let out a short sigh, apparently he was not going to get any more help from this man.
A few minutes later, they returned to the main floor of Ironsoul.
The sound of hammers and the intense heat from the furnaces filled the area around them again and Magnus almost immediately walked toward his own table.
But before Lian and Kain could reach the door, the old man’s voice stopped them.
"Vorhelm."
"Working with you was not bad, if you have another crazy order, you can come again."
A small smile appeared on Lian’s face, coming from Magnus, this sentence was almost like a friendly invitation.
In any case, he did not refuse either because he might bother him more in the future.
Then he opened the door and left the blacksmith shop with Kain, the cool night air hit their faces almost immediately.
They had only walked a few steps when his friend turned his head toward him.
"You really have no idea why the President would pay for an Ancient Rank armor for you?" He asked with most of his surprise still remaining.
"No." Lian answered simply.
"Not even a guess?"
"Maybe two, but I’m not sure." But neither of them was strong enough for him to want to talk about them.
Kael.
The Vorhelm family.
Or maybe something that he knew nothing about.
"Until he says something himself, I doubt we’ll ever know why."
"Then you have to talk to him."
"Sure, just let me first take his personal number out of my pocket." Lian gave him a short look.
Kain laughed.
That was the reality.
Even if the young Vorhelm wanted to know the reason for this, meeting the President was not something he could simply reserve time for tomorrow morning.
For now, this question had to wait.
The next task was much simpler, the National Awakened Center.
After his first evolution, Lian had to update his official status.
Less than an hour later, he and Kain were sitting in front of one of the counters in the status registration section.
The young woman behind the desk looked at Lian’s file.
"Current level?" She asked in a professional tone.
"Twenty-three."
The woman nodded and this time, instead of directly registering the information, she took a transparent orb from under the desk.
Very thin blue lines moved inside the orb.
"Put your hand on the orb."
"Last time I came to register, there was nothing like this." Lian said with curiosity.
He remembered that the previous time, they had only asked for his level and had not made any attempt to confirm it, apparently they did not care.
At that time, he had not cared about it either.
"You were below level twenty at that time, right?"
"Level ten."

"Then there was no need, before the first evolution, whether someone lies about their level is almost meaningless to us; you do not have a support payment, transfer priority, access to special areas, or rank benefits and only basic information is registered." The woman moved the orb a little closer.
"After the first evolution, government and association benefits become active, so from this stage onward, the level must be confirmed."
He was silent for a few moments, so they were not only lazy last time, there was also an economic reason for their laziness.
At least it was clear that the government was not willing to give free benefits to people without proof.
Lian placed his hand on the orb and blue light passed through his fingers for a few seconds.
[Level: 23]
[First Evolution: Completed]
The woman checked the information and completed the final confirmation.
With the registration of his first evolution, a set of new benefits became active for Lian;

Discounts on some government transfer portals, access to higher-level official missions at the Awakened Center, limited priority for buying some resources, the ability to use special training areas, and a reduction in part of the fee for selling monster loot.

Better medical services for injuries from the Ruined Realm, access to some closed auctions, and permission to enter hunting areas that were forbidden to Awakened before their first evolution were also part of the same benefits.
In simple terms, the benefits were pretty good.
"Would you like your class and class rank to also be registered in the public file?" The woman asked after completing the registration.
"No."
The staff member nodded without asking any extra questions.
And with that, his status was also updated and the ID card he had received before was canceled and a new one was issued to him.
On their way out, they passed the association’s large buying and selling hall.
Rows of counters for selling monster materials, equipment, cores, and different resources were placed on both sides of the hall and many Awakened were busy making deals.
"Don’t you have anything to sell?" Kain looked at him.
Lian really thought about it for a moment.
He did.
There were still many bodies in his storage space, before returning, he had planned to sell at least some of them.
But now? He had several hundred million dollars in his account.
The cost of the armor, which he had expected to be his biggest expense, had also been completely paid.
So he had no immediate need for more money.

On the other hand, the Devourer Egg still needed a huge amount of energy and biological materials to fully develop and selling the bodies for money he did not need, when he could use them to make that creature be born faster, did not make much sense.
In any case, he would rather see what that creature that had been able to help him in the Ruined Realm would become when it was finally born.
For that reason, he shook his head and simply said that he had nothing to sell.
Of course, aside from the corpses, he also had some other things that could be sold.
