Lian was also silent for a moment, what surprised him was not that the President knew about the existence of the armor.
The head of the Blacksmith Association personally knew about this order.
An Ancient Rank armor made from the body of an Unholy Rank World Devourer Giant was also not something that could be made without attracting the attention of high-level people.
Besides, to make this armor, Magnus had to get a special hammer from the Blacksmith Association and this alone could attract that man’s attention.
It was natural for the information to eventually reach the government as well.
But why would the President personally pay for the cost of his armor?
He thought in silence for a few seconds.
Two possibilities came to his mind before the others.
First, Kael.
If the President knew about Kael and what had happened between them, this payment might have been a kind of reward or thanks.
But the second possibility was his own name.
Vorhelm.
As far as he knew, the President’s relationship with the Vorhelm family was not very good, if this matter was really related to his family, paying for his armor would be strange behavior.
But his own relationship with his family was not good either and someone like the President should know about this, so it was possible that he wanted to invest in him by doing this.
"Why?" In the end, it was better to ask.
"I don’t know either.
I sent the bill, the President’s Office paid it and I got my money, if you want to know why, ask him yourself." Magnus answered simply.
Lian stared blankly at the old man’s back for several seconds, the suggestion was very simple but there was one small problem.
How exactly was he supposed to randomly meet the President of the country?
Should he go in front of the President’s Office and say that he had come to ask about the money for his armor?
Of course, maybe that would work too?
"Sure, next time I randomly see him on the street, I’ll ask him." He finally said sarcastically.
Kain could not stop himself from laughing, but the old man did not care at all.
"Your problem." He answered without mercy.
The young Vorhelm let out a short sigh, apparently he was not going to get any more help from this man.
A few minutes later, they returned to the main floor of Ironsoul.
The sound of hammers and the intense heat from the furnaces filled the area around them again and Magnus almost immediately walked toward his own table.
But before Lian and Kain could reach the door, the old man’s voice stopped them.
"Vorhelm."
"Working with you was not bad, if you have another crazy order, you can come again."
A small smile appeared on Lian’s face, coming from Magnus, this sentence was almost like a friendly invitation.
In any case, he did not refuse either because he might bother him more in the future.
Then he opened the door and left the blacksmith shop with Kain, the cool night air hit their faces almost immediately.
They had only walked a few steps when his friend turned his head toward him.
"You really have no idea why the President would pay for an Ancient Rank armor for you?" He asked with most of his surprise still remaining.
"No." Lian answered simply.
"Not even a guess?"
"Maybe two, but I’m not sure." But neither of them was strong enough for him to want to talk about them.
Kael.
The Vorhelm family.
Or maybe something that he knew nothing about.
"Until he says something himself, I doubt we’ll ever know why."
"Then you have to talk to him."
"Sure, just let me first take his personal number out of my pocket." Lian gave him a short look.
Kain laughed.
That was the reality.
Even if the young Vorhelm wanted to know the reason for this, meeting the President was not something he could simply reserve time for tomorrow morning.
For now, this question had to wait.
The next task was much simpler, the National Awakened Center.
After his first evolution, Lian had to update his official status.
Less than an hour later, he and Kain were sitting in front of one of the counters in the status registration section.
The young woman behind the desk looked at Lian’s file.
"Current level?" She asked in a professional tone.
"Twenty-three."
The woman nodded and this time, instead of directly registering the information, she took a transparent orb from under the desk.
Very thin blue lines moved inside the orb.
"Put your hand on the orb."
"Last time I came to register, there was nothing like this." Lian said with curiosity.
He remembered that the previous time, they had only asked for his level and had not made any attempt to confirm it, apparently they did not care.
At that time, he had not cared about it either.
"You were below level twenty at that time, right?"
"Level ten."

"Then there was no need, before the first evolution, whether someone lies about their level is almost meaningless to us; you do not have a support payment, transfer priority, access to special areas, or rank benefits and only basic information is registered." The woman moved the orb a little closer.
"After the first evolution, government and association benefits become active, so from this stage onward, the level must be confirmed."
He was silent for a few moments, so they were not only lazy last time, there was also an economic reason for their laziness.
At least it was clear that the government was not willing to give free benefits to people without proof.
Lian placed his hand on the orb and blue light passed through his fingers for a few seconds.
[Level: 23]
[First Evolution: Completed]
The woman checked the information and completed the final confirmation.
With the registration of his first evolution, a set of new benefits became active for Lian;

Discounts on some government transfer portals, access to higher-level official missions at the Awakened Center, limited priority for buying some resources, the ability to use special training areas, and a reduction in part of the fee for selling monster loot.

Better medical services for injuries from the Ruined Realm, access to some closed auctions, and permission to enter hunting areas that were forbidden to Awakened before their first evolution were also part of the same benefits.
In simple terms, the benefits were pretty good.
"Would you like your class and class rank to also be registered in the public file?" The woman asked after completing the registration.
"No."
The staff member nodded without asking any extra questions.
And with that, his status was also updated and the ID card he had received before was canceled and a new one was issued to him.
On their way out, they passed the association’s large buying and selling hall.
Rows of counters for selling monster materials, equipment, cores, and different resources were placed on both sides of the hall and many Awakened were busy making deals.
"Don’t you have anything to sell?" Kain looked at him.
Lian really thought about it for a moment.
He did.
There were still many bodies in his storage space, before returning, he had planned to sell at least some of them.
But now?
He had several hundred million dollars in his account.
The cost of the armor, which he had expected to be his biggest expense, had also been completely paid.
So he had no immediate need for more money.

On the other hand, the Devourer Egg still needed a huge amount of energy and biological materials to fully develop and selling the bodies for money he did not need, when he could use them to make that creature be born faster, did not make much sense.
In any case, he would rather see what that creature that had been able to help him in the Ruined Realm would become when it was finally born.
For that reason, he shook his head and simply said that he had nothing to sell.
Of course, aside from the corpses, he also had some other things that could be sold.

chapters.title: Chapter 424: Once The Strongest, Now The Weakest
paragraphs: However, corpses were not the only things he had brought back from the Special Area.
Several rare materials that he had found with the help of the Celestial Book of Treasure were still inside his storage space.
Among them were Emberglass Resin and Bootfire Marrow.
Both were valuable, but both also had uses for himself.

After being processed, Emberglass Resin could become a material with extremely high resistance to heat and mana flow, and it was excellent for making the inner layers of armor, joint protection, and stabilizing mana arrays.

Bootfire Marrow was also a material full of life and heat energy that could be used to make powerful regeneration potions; potions that did not only close wounds, but also accelerated the healing of tissue, muscles, bones, and damage caused by extreme pressure.
Selling either of them was not an attractive choice.
The first one might not be useful for himself, but he could definitely give it to his friend so that he could use it to make armor.
When they returned to the academy, night had completely arrived.

The two of them ate a simple dinner and then returned to the dormitory, Lian kept the World-Devourer Bastion in his storage space and checked his new messages for a short time before sleeping, but there was still no reply from Gareth.
Tomorrow, the others were supposed to return, and after that there would be no more days of rest, the final term exams were finally going to begin.
And these exams were not going to go peacefully.
The next morning, the main area of the academy was much busier than the day before.
The young Vorhelm and Kain waited near the entrance until several special student transport vehicles finally entered the academy grounds.
The first person to get out was Rindo.
Then Seraphina.
Liana.
Selina.
Cassian.
Ethan.
And Marcus.
Seeing all of them in the academy felt strange.
Only a few days ago, the last image Lian had of most of them was their bodies covered in blood among the giants’ graves.
Now they were wearing clean clothes and walking among normal students again.
After a few short greetings, the members of the group had to go directly to the academy’s administration department so their return could be registered and their first report could be submitted.
Lian did not go with them, Aldric had already taken care of his part the day before.
Almost an hour later, when the others came out of the administration building, Rindo almost immediately changed his direction.
"I have to go to the Student Council, I have nine months of reports and unfinished work."
He said seriously before leaving.
"There is something you need to know first." The young Vorhelm called him before he could leave.
The Student Council President stopped.
He looked at his face, and Lian’s tone was enough for him to understand that this was not something unimportant.
"Okay." Rindo answered shortly and walked with the others.
On the way to the academy cafe, the looks from the people around them quickly caught everyone’s attention.
The students were openly turning their heads.
Some looked at them with surprise and some with curiosity, all of them were well-known faces.
And some looked at them with something that was almost pity.
Nine months ago, these people had been among the most famous and strongest students in the academy, but now people looked at them like people who had returned from the past.
"What is going on? Why is everyone looking at us like this?" Liana asked while looking confused at several nearby students.
It was not hard to see the pity in their eyes, but what the hell were they pitying them for?
Kain let out a short sigh.
"You will find out soon." Lian answered without slowing his steps.
This answer did not make the girl’s expression any better.
A few minutes later, everyone was sitting around one of the large tables in the cafe.
And the young Vorhelm started his explanation with the simple changes, first the growth of the students and the fact that a large part of them had already completed their First Evolution.
The academy’s average level was currently above 22, and it might even reach 24-25.
And the problem was already clear from the beginning, none of them were even level 24.
But he quickly reached the main part, Roderick.
When he mentioned his name, Seraphina almost immediately frowned and Lian explained a summary of what Kain and Aldric had told him.
Roderick had completed his First Evolution very early.
His last recorded level was 37 and he had now reached 39, a large guild supported him and his family had given him huge amounts of resources.
Of course, this part was not important to him, no matter how powerful a family or guild was, all of them became less important compared to the name Vorhelm.
And they would simply never be willing to insult a Vorhelm, even if there were rumors around him, they were not willing to take that risk.
He only mentioned this so they would understand that he had probably reached the maximum potential of his class’s stats.
And most importantly, during Rindo and the others’ absence, he had built a network of students around himself that controlled a large part of hunting, resource trading, and student missions.
The young Vorhelm also told Kain’s story, with Kain’s permission of course.
From Roderick’s offer, its rejection, the conflict that followed, and the isolation that had slowly been created around him.
He said all of this to make them understand that the bastard had built a network that allowed him to suppress his opponents in the academy.
The more he talked, the colder Rindo’s face became, this was no longer just a personal conflict between a few students.
During the Student Council President’s absence, a parallel structure had formed inside the academy, a structure whose power came not from the rules, but from influence and resources.
"So that is why everyone is looking at us like that." Liana said quietly.
"Part of it, the other part is that everyone knows you were gone for nine months." Kain answered this time.
"So they think we became weaker?" Ethan frowned.
Kain gave him a short look.
"From the level? They do not think, you really fell behind, that is obvious."
Ethan stayed silent for a few seconds, the answer hurt because it was true.
"We cannot let this continue like this, I already did not like Roderick and Elena before, but this is no longer just a personal matter." Seraphina placed her hands on the table.
"Then let’s go beat them up as much as we can." Ethan said almost immediately.
Marcus gave him a calm look.
"With what?" Marcus asked dryly.
"We are probably among the weakest main students in the academy right now, most of us are around level twenty and we have not even completed our First Evolution yet."
This time the silence became truly heavy, no one could argue.
Roderick was level 39, Elena was level 31.
Darren and many people from Roderick’s group had also passed level twenty and evolved a long time ago.
But the people who had been among the strongest generation nine months ago had not even had the chance to complete their First Evolution.
After a few moments, Cassian turned toward Rindo.
"We are members of the Student Council, can’t we use the council to stop this monopoly?"
"In theory? Maybe, but in practice, no." Rindo stayed silent for a few seconds and then answered calmly.
Everyone looked at him and he continued his explanation.

"If the council passes a law that half of the powerful students are not willing to follow, that law is only a piece of writing, we can stop obvious violations, but we cannot force someone to form a team with another person, give them a discount, or trade their resources with them." His face became a little colder.

"Roderick moved exactly into a place where the rules cannot easily touch him, what he is doing is not illegal, he has only created a faction, I can see if they do anything against the rules and restrict them through that, but I doubt it."
Lian calmly drank his drink and when silence appeared, he put the cup on the table.
"There is another problem too, the final term exams start tomorrow, with your current situation, there is a high chance you will get the last ranks."
"Did you really have to say that part?" Ethan asked with dissatisfaction.
"Yes." He answered without hesitation.
Marcus sighed and Kain could not hide his smile, but the joke only lasted for a few seconds because everyone knew the young Vorhelm was right.
Lian himself did not have the same concern, on paper he was only level 23 but the level number had become almost the least important part of his real strength.
Four thousand base points, the Fallen Monster body, his skills, the Ancient Rank armor, and even thirty seconds of Black Silence’s power in the worst situation.
A low rank in the final exam was the last thing on his mind.
The sound of a chair being pulled across the floor suddenly caught everyone’s attention.
Rindo was standing.
"Where are you going?" Liana asked.
"I do not have time to waste here, my Evolution Mission was already completed, I have to do my First Evolution today."
The Student Council President could not and should not be the weakest student in the academy.
What good was this position if no one respected him at that time?

chapters.title: Chapter 425: The Final Exam Begins
paragraphs: "Student Council President cannot be one of the weakest students in the academy, and I am not going to let this power structure continue like this, a student should not have to go under someone’s banner just to get missions, resources, or even find a team."
It was not like Rindo’s usual tone, but there was a seriousness in his voice that no one doubted.
For him, the matter was not only about his own position, the school year was almost over.
This was considered his final year at the academy, and after graduation, a new Student Council election would be held.
Before they entered the Special Area, Cassian was one of the main choices to replace him.
But now there was someone else, Rodrick.
In terms of level, fame, wealth, and a large network of students, he had a very big advantage, and if he decided to enter the election, he would no longer be just a minor name.
He had a real chance of winning.
From Rindo’s point of view, combining Rodrick’s unofficial power with the official authority of Student Council President could destroy the entire balance of the academy for next year.
He had no intention of allowing something like that to happen without resistance before graduation.
"I’m going too, my Evolution Quest condition was completed already." Seraphina stood up a few seconds later.
Then Selina.
Liana.
Cassian.
Ethan.
Marcus.
Each of them was in a different situation, but almost all of their Evolution Quests had reached a point during the events in the Special Area where they could complete the process that same day.
The rest was over, only a few days had passed since they escaped from a disaster, but the world had not stopped for them.
If they did not want to end up at the bottom of the ranking in front of the entire academy tomorrow, they had to start moving again.
Less than a minute later, the large table was almost empty.
Only Lian and Kain remained, and the latter watched the others leave for a few seconds before turning toward the former.
"Do you think we have a way to crush Rodrick’s face into the ground tomorrow? Because right now, they do not seem able to help much."
"You were the one who said yesterday that I should not get into a conflict with Rodrick." The young Vorhelm gave him a meaningful look.
Kain was silent for a moment.

"Well... things have changed and it is not just my problem, if the people who were the strongest students in the academy nine months ago get defeated in front of everyone tomorrow, the last thing left of the Student Council’s and your group’s former influence will also disappear."
"Then this place will really no longer be called the National Academy, it will become Rodrick’s Academy." He gave a bitter smile.
"Don’t worry." Lian looked at him for a few moments and then said very calmly.
"Does that mean you have a plan?" Kain raised an eyebrow.
"No. There is no need." He picked up his cup and drank the last sip of his drink.
He said it so calmly and confidently that his friend did not even know what to say for a few seconds.
The rest of the day passed quickly.
Rindo and several others spent almost all their time inside the academy’s special rooms that had been built for completing the Evolution.
By night, a large part of the group had completed their First Evolution.
The academy also became busier hour by hour.
Students who had been active for months in Base #3, remote areas, and other areas of the Ruined Realm returned one after another.
Almost all the important names of the academy were gathered in one place again.
And the next morning, the day of the test arrived.
The final-term test for Awakened students was nothing like a normal exam.
The score was important, but it was only a small part of what the test result decided.
The official rank of every student for the next year would be updated based on this test.

Access to some important missions, priority for using resources and training areas, position in exploration teams, and even the ability to choose certain teachers directly depended on the student’s performance.
And more importantly, people outside the academy were watching.
Unions, families, the Awakened Association, guilds, military organizations, and even the government and federation.
For many students, an excellent performance in the final-term test could create the first professional contract of their lives.
A guild might pay for their future Evolution, a family might become their sponsor, or a powerful teacher might accept them as a student.
This test was the showcase of the country’s next generation of Awakened.
This was even more important for the third-year students, who were already in the final days of their time at the academy.
And this year, there was much more attention on it than usual, the current generation had been known as an unusual generation from the very beginning of the year.
This generation had appeared at the same time as the opening of a new Ruined Realm, and then famous geniuses such as Rodrick, Kain, and Lian Vorhelm were among the young people in the academy.
And now, the return of those who had been lost in the Special Area for nine months.
Everyone wanted to know who was really standing at the top of this generation.
The academy’s main hall was almost completely full.
Thousands of seats were placed in several sections, and huge floating screens were ready above the hall to display the test results.
The teachers were sitting in their own section.
Several officials from the National Awakened Center were present on the upper floor, and representatives of different guilds and families could also be seen in the special seats.
The first-year students filled the central section of the hall, and in one of the front rows, Lian was sitting completely comfortably.
There was no sign of nervousness on his face, and not even clear excitement, he was sitting as if he owned the hall.

His body was against the back of the chair and one of his legs was slightly forward, as if he had come to watch other people’s test, not take part in one of the most important evaluations of the year.
World-Devourer Bastion was inside his storage space.
There was no reason to reveal one of his biggest cards from the beginning.
But even without the armor, many eyes were on him and whispers came from the rows around him.
"Is that him? Lian Vorhelm?" one of the students asked quietly.
"I thought he was dead." another person answered.
"They say he is barely above Level 20."
"What? Are you serious?"
"He is nine months behind, what did you expect his level to be?"
Lian could hear almost all of them and none of it mattered to him, his calmness was not a show of pride, he did not even need to try to look confident.
Several hundred students whispering about his level really could not raise his heartbeat even a little.
Rindo was sitting several rows ahead with the members of the Student Council.
He had completed his First Evolution the night before.
Seraphina had also managed to use the condition she completed in the Special Area and complete her First Evolution.
Cassian had also managed to finish his own process.
Everyone was ready, or at least they had done the best they could in one day.
The sound of conversations in the hall was still loud when the large entrance doors suddenly opened.
At first, only a few people turned their heads, then more people looked, and the whispers became quieter.
"Well, he finally came." Kain whispered quietly.
Rodrick entered the hall, unlike what might be expected at first, he entered completely normally, but apparently he no longer needed to do things like that.
His presence alone was enough.
His body was more trained than nine months ago, and the proud teenager Lian remembered had been replaced by a much stronger confidence.
Mana was flowing through his body in a very controlled way, not enough to be released for show, but it could still clearly be felt.
He had become stronger, really strong, and Elena was walking beside him, she had changed too.
Her hair was neater and her appearance had become more mature, and the way she moved was also full of confidence,
There was a kind of satisfaction in her eyes, as if seeing the shock of others toward herself and her boyfriend filled her with satisfaction.
That was right! Everyone should be shocked when they saw her and her partner, or at least those were her thoughts.
Behind them, Darren and several main members of Rodrick’s group were walking.
The students in their path unconsciously made some space.
Seeing this scene, Lian finally saw with his own eyes everything Kain had said about Rodrick’s influence.
But at that moment, Elena’s eyes moved between the rows and stopped on him, for a fraction of a second, her steps became slower.
Only by such a small amount that perhaps no one else would notice, but Lian did.
The girl’s eyes opened slightly wider for a moment, the man whose death had been possible nine months ago was sitting there.
Completely healthy and without injuries, and stranger than everything else, he did not even seem to consider their return an important event.
Signs of shock, anger, disbelief, and dissatisfaction appeared in her eyes, although her expression was quickly controlled,
But it was enough, and Rodrick also noticed the direction of her gaze, he turned his head and then his eyes reached the young Vorhelm.
For several seconds, there was no one between the two.
At least, that was how it felt.
Nine months ago, Rodrick was one of the most famous students among the new students.
A four-star class, a powerful family, guild offers.
And Lian?
A student with a failed Awakening whom many people even mocked for being present, and who had been exiled from his family.
Now Rodrick was close to Level 39 with the support of a large guild, dozens of powerful students around him, and an influence that covered a large part of the academy.
On the other side, Lian was only Level 23 ...at least that was what everyone could see.
A very short moment of surprise passed through Rodrick’s eyes, he had probably already heard about Lian’s return, but hearing news was different from seeing someone he preferred to be dead.
His eyes moved very briefly down from Lian’s face and it was clear that his body had changed, but the thing that mattered on paper was his Level 23, and this gave Rodrick a false confidence.
Then the corner of his lips slowly rose and he gave a very small smile that was somewhere between amusement and contempt.
As if Lian’s nine months of absence had already decided the result and he was completely sure that he would win.
The young Vorhelm looked at him for a few seconds, but there was no emotion in his eyes except that deep calm as deep as the sea, and he only leaned a little more against the back of his chair.
This reaction, or rather the lack of a reaction, made Rodrick’s smile become a little stiffer for a fraction of a second.
Lian only had one thought in his mind, this bastard still has the same annoying face.
At that moment, all the lights around the central stage turned on, the sound of conversations in the hall became quiet, and the powerful voice of the Academy Principal spread through the entire area.
"Students."
All eyes turned toward the stage, and the Academy Principal looked over the crowd for a few seconds.
A man who looked to be in his sixties, with neatly styled white hair and a face without any facial hair, wearing a suit.
"This year’s final-term tests begin from this moment."

sentences.text: "Student Council President cannot be one of the weakest students in the academy, and I am not going to let this power structure continue like this, a student should not have to go under someone’s banner just to get missions, resources, or even find a team."

For him, the matter was not only about his own position, the school year was almost over.
This was considered his final year at the academy, and after graduation, a new Student Council election would be held.
Before they entered the Special Area, Cassian was one of the main choices to replace him.
But now there was someone else, Rodrick.
In terms of level, fame, wealth, and a large network of students, he had a very big advantage, and if he decided to enter the election, he would no longer be just a minor name.
He had a real chance of winning.
From Rindo’s point of view, combining Rodrick’s unofficial power with the official authority of Student Council President could destroy the entire balance of the academy for next year.
He had no intention of allowing something like that to happen without resistance before graduation.
"I’m going too, my Evolution Quest condition was completed already." Seraphina stood up a few seconds later.
Then Selina.
Liana.
Cassian.
Ethan.
Marcus.
Each of them was in a different situation, but almost all of their Evolution Quests had reached a point during the events in the Special Area where they could complete the process that same day.
The rest was over, only a few days had passed since they escaped from a disaster, but the world had not stopped for them.
If they did not want to end up at the bottom of the ranking in front of the entire academy tomorrow, they had to start moving again.

"Do you think we have a way to crush Rodrick’s face into the ground tomorrow?

Students who had been active for months in Base #3, remote areas, and other areas of the Ruined Realm returned one after another.
Almost all the important names of the academy were gathered in one place again.

The final-term test for Awakened students was nothing like a normal exam.
The score was important, but it was only a small part of what the test result decided.
The official rank of every student for the next year would be updated based on this test.

Access to some important missions, priority for using resources and training areas, position in exploration teams, and even the ability to choose certain teachers directly depended on the student’s performance.
And more importantly, people outside the academy were watching.
Unions, families, the Awakened Association, guilds, military organizations, and even the government and federation.
For many students, an excellent performance in the final-term test could create the first professional contract of their lives.

chapters.title: Chapter 426: The Broken Crown
paragraphs: "This year’s final-term tests begin from this moment." The Academy Principal’s voice spread across the huge hall and silenced even the last scattered whispers.
Thousands of pairs of eyes were fixed on the central stage.
The students who had been talking about rankings, Rodrick, the return of the people from the Special Area, or even Lian’s Level 23 only a few moments ago, were now almost all silent.
Even the representatives of guilds and families who were sitting in the higher seats turned their attention toward the stage.
The Academy Principal himself had come to manage the final-term tests, of course, this was something he did every year.
The final-term tests were very important to the academy and his presence was necessary.
He looked at the crowd for a few seconds.
Then, contrary to expectations, he did not start explaining the rules himself.
"This year, the design and direct supervision of the test have been given to one of the academy’s senior professors, Professor Silas Wern."
For a moment, the silence continued, and then whispers started in several parts of the hall.
"Oh... this is not good." Kain, who was sitting beside Lian, showed a change in his expression for a moment.
"Why? Do you know him?" He had never heard this professor’s name before, he had not spent enough time in the academy to know all the professors.
But with one look around, he could see that he was very well known among the other students.

"Of course I know him, I have also had a few encounters with him and they were not good at all, he is extremely strict, unlike Professor Aldric who is kind inside, this man is like a stone even on the inside! You may not believe it, but during the time you were gone, he got three students expelled."
Lian raised an eyebrow and then the corner of his lips rose slightly.
In general, and at least from what he had seen, all the academy professors had serious appearances and behavior and always kept a certain distance from the students.
Some of them were kind and helpful inside, but there were also people who were cold and serious both inside and outside.
And according to his friend’s explanation, this man seemed to be both.
"Then why are you worried? At least we won’t get bored and we don’t need to worry about the test being easy." But he had no problem with a strict professor.
The harder the test was, the better he could crush Rodrick’s face into the ground, that bastard would not leave him alone and sooner or later he would cause trouble for him.
So as long as he had the chance, he would take his throne in the academy.
Then he suddenly felt a gaze from far away and his attention returned to the Academy Principal, the old man who was looking at him with eyes that did not even hide his hostility.
’Does this old man still not want to let go of his hatred toward me?’ He did not know whether to laugh or cry, he had expected him to let go of it after all this time.
But it seemed that Seraphina’s father still did not have positive feelings toward him ...who knew? Maybe he would use this final-term test to give him a warning.
"You are really happy to hear this?" Kain gave him a short look, he also did not mind working hard.
But there was a difference between working hard because of normal difficulty and working hard for something that had been deliberately designed to make you suffer.
And from what he knew about the person who designed this year’s final-term test, it was definitely the second one.
Lian wanted to answer but did not get the chance, and a man walked out from the teachers’ section without any hurry.
He looked about forty years old.
His dark gray hair was neatly combed back and several white strands could be seen among it.
He wore thin glasses and the academy’s formal teacher uniform.

Even his facial expression did not have Aldric’s dry seriousness and there was a very faint smile at the corner of his lips, as if the presence of thousands of students, dozens of important people, and all the pressure of the test were nothing more than daily entertainment to him.
However, almost all the students immediately sat up straighter when they saw him.

There was something strange about the man, unlike the other professors, he was not trying to hide his presence at all, instead, he used his heavy presence to make sure that all the students felt the pressure.
And this pressure coming from him was enough for Lian to realize that this man had completed at least three Evolutions!
A true Enlightened One, just like Professor Aldric, people who had permission and the ability to enter the Heavenly Realm.
"An Enlightened One is designing this year’s test?" This thought appeared in all of their minds.
Enlightened One.
A title given to Awakened after their Third Evolution.

The First and Second Evolutions could change the body, class, talents, and capacity of an Awakened, but it was said that the Third Evolution was the point where the nature of a person’s perception also changed.
Mana was no longer only energy to be used, skills were no longer only something that could be activated.
And the battle environment was no longer considered something separate from the person.
People who had passed their Third Evolution saw the world differently from everyone else.
That was why they were called Enlightened Ones, and the number of such people in the entire country was not large at all.
The presence of one of them as the direct designer of the first-year test alone showed that the academy had no intention of making things easy this year.
Normally, ordinary professors were always the ones who designed the tests and sometimes discussed them with senior professors as well.
But it seemed that this year was going to be different.
Silas reached the center of the stage and the Academy Principal stepped aside without saying anything else, and the professor looked at the hall for a few seconds.
He did not take any device to increase his voice and did not even change his standing position, yet when he spoke, his voice could be heard throughout the entire hall without the slightest effort.
"Probably half of you expected to stand in front of a device today, punch it, have your level recorded, and then have several one-on-one fights."
Several students instinctively looked at each other, this was almost exactly what most of them had expected.
Silas paused for a moment.
"I’m sorry, my time is worth more than something this cheap."

"Level is important, raw power is important, speed, mana, skills, and equipment are also important, but if the final-term test only measures these things, we could buy a machine and all the professors could stay home today." His smile slowly disappeared.
"What I want to see today is what you do when things do not go as you expected."

"Survival, decision-making, adaptation, combat, resource management, leadership, choosing a target, and the ability to move under pressure; the level number alone cannot show any of these things." He raised his hand slightly and the huge screen behind him turned on.
"That is why this year, you will have something different."
The image was completely dark at first, then light slowly appeared and showed a gray sky with an endless sea of dark clouds and lightning moving deep inside the clouds.
Among them, islands could be seen, dozens of huge islands were floating in the sky.
Some were covered in thick forests, some were white and frozen, and some were only huge masses of rock with waterfalls falling from their edges into the sea of clouds.
Ruins of stone and old temples could be seen on several islands.
Broken stone bridges connected some areas, and chains as thick as towers hung between several islands.
But the thing that almost immediately attracted everyone’s attention was the center of the image.
A huge upside-down mountain whose peak pointed down toward the sea of clouds while its wide part floated in the sky.
And on its highest point, a golden crown was floating, the crown’s weak light could even be seen from this distance in the image.
Silas turned toward the screen.
"The name of this year’s test... is Broken Crown."
The students looked at each other, if that screen was showing the test environment, then this no longer looked like an exam, it looked more like a real operation.

chapters.title: Chapter 427: The Rules And Rewards
paragraphs: The image changed, and hundreds of glowing points appeared on different islands.

"The first rule is simple; when you enter, everyone will be randomly scattered, there is no guarantee that you will appear next to your friends, teammates, or group members." His eyes moved across the crowd for a moment.
"If all your power depends on having twenty people around you, today is a good time to understand that this itself is a weakness."
Several eyes unconsciously moved toward Rodrick, everyone understood that the senior professor was directly referring to him.
But Rodrick did not even blink, he was simply sitting in his seat and looking at the platform with the same calm expression.
It was not clear whether he had taken the sentence personally or not, he did not show it and it was not clear what he was thinking about.
"Every participant starts with one hundred points."
A large number appeared on the screen.
[Starting Points: 100]
"Defeating monsters, passing environmental trials, discovering special locations, finding hidden targets, collecting seals, and defeating other participants can increase your points."
One of the students raised his hand.
"If we defeat another student, do we get all of their points?" the boy asked.
Silas tilted his head slightly.
"No. Only part of their points will be transferred, and the amount depends on how they were defeated, the difference in power, and the conditions of the fight."

"And before some of you get excited, I have one piece of advice; if you think that the person who defeats the most people or monsters will definitely become first place, you should forget that idea right now."
Lian thought about the sentence for a moment.
So points were not the entire result, or at least Silas did not want them to think that way and this test was not based on who defeated the most people.
It depended on how they defeated them, the academy wanted to see the students’ strategies.
The professor moved his hand, and a small silver seal appeared on the screen.
"Each of you will receive a protective seal when you enter, this seal is connected to the test’s monitoring system and will constantly check your physical and mental condition."
A human figure appeared on the screen, an attack came close to its body and suddenly, before the attack hit, the body turned into light and disappeared.

"If the system detects that the next attack has a high chance of causing death, permanent disability, or irreversible damage, the seal will activate and you will immediately be pulled out of the realm." Silas pushed his glasses up slightly.
"So you do not need to worry too much about killing your classmates."
"Of course, I would prefer that you do not intentionally test how fast the seal works."
The message was completely serious, the fights were real, the students could release more of their power without constantly being afraid of killing the other side.
For a test that was supposed to determine the best academy, this made a big difference.
Silas raised another finger.
"The next rule."
This time, an island appeared on the screen, a monster appeared on it, then the image changed and a larger monster took its place.
"The realm itself will watch your performance and react to it."
"What does that mean?" a girl asked loudly.
"It means you will find out soon enough.
Unhappy sounds came from several people in the hall, some of them had guesses, but the others did not understand what the professor meant.
Lian, on the other hand, became a little interested, the test reacted to their performance and based on this man’s previous explanations, he could guess what was going on.
It meant that there was not going to be one fixed path for everyone.
The screen changed again, this time five islands much larger than the others stood out and a different symbol appeared on each one.

In the distance, huge trees with golden leaves stood above the surrounding forest.
White mountains could be seen on the horizon.
The sky was blue and clear, unlike the fog and strange color of the normal sky of the Ruined Realm and without the heavy and suffocating feeling that most areas of the Ruined Realm had.
Several large herbivorous creatures moved beside the river, but there was no sign of violence or chaos in the image.
This place almost did not look like the Ruined Realm, it looked more like an image of heaven.

"That’s right... You should not know where this place is, after all, it was discovered only a few months ago."

chapters.title: Chapter 428: The Land Of First Dawn
paragraphs: Silas started explaining at the same time, the Land of First Dawn had been discovered about seven months ago.
It was quickly discovered that it was different from most known areas of the Ruined Realm.
The mana in the environment was much purer and denser, and unknown plant species had been found there, some of which had medicinal or enhancement properties.
Some could temporarily increase physical strength by up to ten percent after each use.
The water of some springs had the ability to increase stats up to a certain limit.
Rare crafting materials naturally existed in some areas, materials that could be used to create Rank A and Rank B artifacts.
And even stranger, the number of attacking monsters was unusually low, some species were even completely peaceful.
The temperature in the mapped areas almost always remained moderate, and even simply resting in that area increased the natural speed of mana recovery.
Kain leaned toward Lian.

"You have probably heard news about it almost every week during these past few months, several new plants have come from there that have crazy prices and can almost bring a dead person back to life, of course, if you are actually dead, then no, as long as you are alive, no matter how badly you are injured, after consuming that plant, you will become completely healthy."
"I even heard that if you have already reached your stat limit, the springs there can help you increase your stats and go beyond the limits."
Along with his interest, a strong desire appeared in Lian’s eyes, he had never heard that something like this was possible and all these descriptions sounded exactly like a description of heaven.
How could such a place exist inside the Ruined Realm?

But whatever the reason was, it was truly tempting, especially the plants, resources, and treasures that could be found there ... with the help of the Celestial book of treasure, it was possible that he could find even more unusual things.
This was exactly something he could need.
But then his eyes fell on that sun, that Hollow sun ... for some reason, he had a bad feeling about it.
"If this place is so good, why is entry limited?" one of the students asked loudly.
Silas answered directly this time.

"Are you stupid? The resources there are too valuable and important, of course it will not be open to everyone." In fact, if it were up to the government, they did not even want these students to enter.
Unfortunately, the interference of some forces had made things difficult for them and they had found a way to get out from under this pressure.
And this was the first part of their plan.
Anyway, now the reason for the hall’s excitement was completely clear, this was not a simple ticket for a trip.
For a young student, a few weeks in such a place could make a huge difference in their growth speed.
The rewards appeared on the screen.
[Third Place]
[Seven-Day Entry Permit to the Land of First Dawn.]
[Second Place]
[Fourteen-Day Entry Permit to the Land of First Dawn.]
And then—
[First Place]
[Thirty-Day Entry Permit to the Land of First Dawn.]
[Access to the Inner Ring.]
[Registered Personal Companion Permit: 0]
[Right to personally collect resources according to exploration limits.]
[One choice from the special section of the academy store.]
[One private guidance session with one of the Enlightened Ones.]
[The first-place winner will obtain one skill with Holy Rank potential.]
[Each of the top three has the right to choose between any guild, the government, and the Federation and join them.]
But apart from that land, there was now another attractive reward, a skill with Holy Rank potential could be obtained, and a reward like this was extremely rare.
Lian was no longer just a little interested, now he truly wanted to take first place.
The images of the area changed one after another.
A plain, a river, a forest with golden trees, a blue lake, a small ruin with white roots growing around it.
Then, for less than two seconds, an image of a stone pillar appeared, the pillar was almost half broken.
Golden moss covered its lower part and a symbol was carved into its upper surface.
A circle that looked like a sun, but its center was completely empty, a ring with an empty heart, exactly like the sun in the sky.
Lian’s eyes stopped on it for a moment, there was something strange about the symbol and its similarity to the sun also showed that the sun itself was not shaped like that in this area for no reason.

In an unclear way, it caught his attention and once again gave him a bad feeling, but before he could look more carefully, the images disappeared and the islands of the Broken Crown appeared on the screen again.
"Now that I finally have your real attention, one last point." Silas said calmly.
"In the Broken Crown, having a higher Level is an advantage, but it is not a guarantee, having a larger group is also an advantage, better equipment is the same, having a stronger class is the same."
"But none of them are guarantees, the only thing that increases your chance of reaching the end is learning about the monsters and enemies faster than the test itself."
And once again, his words were said in a way that no one could understand.
The professor raised his hand and the huge array under the main platform lit up.
White and blue lines spread across the floor and passed through the stone like glowing veins.
A few seconds later, the space above the platform twisted, a huge ring of light formed and a weak wind blew through the hall, then the ring opened.
Behind it, the gray sky of the test could be seen, a sea of black clouds and islands floating in the distance.
The excitement in the hall immediately turned into tension, what they were seeing was real, not a picture on a screen, they were really going to enter that realm.
Of course, this was more of a simulator than reality and they were not actually going to enter some kind of realm or Area.
"Participants will enter according to their registration numbers, from the moment you pass through the gate, your test will begin."
The students stood up from their seats one after another, the rows began to move.
Rodrick also stood up, before moving toward the entrance, he gave Lian a short look, this time there was no smile.
The competition had begun.
Lian calmly looked away.
A few minutes later, it was Kain’s turn, before moving, he raised his fist toward him.
"We’ll find each other inside." He said with a confident smile.
"If you don’t get eliminated before that." The young Vorhelm gently bumped his fist against his.
"I’m Level 34 and I won’t be eliminated that easily." Kain looked at him.
"And the test reacts to your performance, not your Level, be careful and try to use your brain."
"Damn, I’ll try."
"Good luck."
"You too."
Kain entered the light and disappeared.
A few more minutes passed.
"Lian Vorhelm."
He stood up from his seat, more eyes turned toward him.
Some of those who had heard his Level were still whispering.

But he paid no attention to them, he calmly walked through the rows and reached the platform, Silas looked at him for a moment, only for a moment, but Lian felt that unlike most people, the man’s gaze did not stop at his Level or appearance.
It was as if he was checking something.
"Good luck, Vorhelm." The professor said calmly.
"Thank you, Professor." And then he entered the gate.
The world became dark and the sounds disappeared, for a moment, that same feeling of weightlessness from the transfer came over him again.
But this time it only lasted for a fraction of a second, and then the wind was the first thing he felt, a strong wind hit his body.
Lian opened his eyes, the huge gray sky was above his head and several black birds were moving very far away among the clouds.
He stood still for a few seconds and then lowered his gaze, only a few meters ahead, the ground ended, he had appeared right near the edge of a floating island.
There was nothing under his feet except an endless sea of black clouds.
Lightning flashed deep inside the clouds and the sound of their distant thunder reached his ears with a delay.
The young Vorhelm took one step away from the edge and then raised his head, more islands could be seen in the sky.
Dozens of islands, some very far away, some higher and some lower, and in the center of all of them was the upside-down mountain.
The golden crown shone like a small star on its highest point.
A panel appeared in front of him.
[The Broken Crown test has begun.]
[Participant: Lian Vorhelm.]
[Initial Crown Points: 100.]
[Protective Seal: Active.]
[Adaptive Evaluation: Active.]
[First Stage: Survival and Advancement.]
Lian read the text for a few seconds, then closed the panel, the island he was standing on was mostly covered by a dense forest.
Trees with gray trunks grew between the rocks and a thin mist moved close to the ground, no other student could be seen.
Good.
He took a few steps toward the forest and at that moment, he heard a sound...
Grrrrrrrrr...
A heavy sound came from between the trees, the branches moved and several birds flew out from among the leaves.
Then something large moved among the shadows.
He stopped and saw two yellow eyes open in the darkness, a few seconds later, a four-legged monster came out from between the trees.
Its body was almost three meters tall and thick gray skin covered its muscles, two curved horns came out from both sides of its head and its black claws dug into the ground beneath its feet.
The test panel appeared.
[The first test has been created.]
[Simulated Monster.]
[Level: 24.]
Lian looked at the creature for a few seconds, the monster showed its teeth and another growl came from its throat.
He only let out a short sigh.
"Only twenty-four?" Then he muttered with a little disappointment.
The monster roared and charged toward him.
And somewhere far away in the academy’s monitoring hall, the first evaluation data of Lian Vorhelm began to be recorded.

"Only twenty-four?" Then he muttered with a little disappointment.
The monster roared and charged toward him.
And somewhere far away in the academy’s monitoring hall, the first evaluation data of Lian Vorhelm began to be recorded.

chapters.title: Chapter 429: The Broken Crown II
paragraphs: [Simulated Monster.]
[Level: 24.]
The monster let out a heavy roar and its black claws dug into the ground, its three-meter-tall body charged toward Lian with a speed that did not match its size.
He stood right there and calmly followed the monster’s movement with his eyes, a heavy creature with a muscular body, thick gray skin, and two curved horns coming out from both sides of its skull.
For a normal Level 23 Awakened, it was not a simple enemy...
The distance between them went from twenty meters to five meters in a few seconds.
The monster lowered its head and its two large horns aimed directly at his chest, the weight of its entire body was behind the attack and the sound of its footsteps shook the ground around it.

Right when the horns were about to reach him, Lian took one step forward and his right fist moved, the attack hit the middle of the monster’s forehead directly and the sound of something breaking spread through the air.
The creature stopped at that exact moment, its front legs left the ground and its huge body was thrown several meters backward.
Its back hit the trunk of one of the trees.
The gray tree broke with a heavy sound and the monster’s body fell to the ground and was dragged several meters across the dirt and wet leaves.
Silence returned to the forest and the young Vorhelm looked at the motionless creature for a few seconds, the front part of its skull was almost crushed.
[Simulated Monster defeated.]
[Points increased.]
The monster’s body suddenly began to change and turned into thousands of small blue particles that spread through the air like ash.
Lian waited without hurry.
One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
But no other notification appeared, apparently, killing monsters only gave them points and there was no other reward.
"Predictable." He said calmly and took his eyes away from the last mana particles disappearing in the air.
Silas had said before they entered that the creatures in this test were not real, it was a little disappointing.
If each of these creatures had been real, such a test could have turned into a feast for Glutton and Butcher.
Lian raised his head and examined his surroundings more carefully.
The island was much larger than it had seemed from the images inside the hall.
The forest continued for several kilometers in every direction and gray trees several dozen meters tall covered a large part of the sky.
The sounds of different creatures could be heard from far away and sometimes there was a sound like something heavy being dragged across stone.
The wind also blew into the forest from the edge of the island almost without stopping and moved the mist away every few moments.
Through the gaps between the trees, he could see parts of other islands floating in the sky at different heights.
But even with this view, the main destination could not be lost.
The central upside-down mountain could be seen behind all the islands and the golden crown on it shone like a small star in the gray sky.
"So just running toward that isn’t going to be enough." He muttered while giving the crown a short look.

Silas had clearly talked about exploration, special locations, hidden targets, and decision-making, if the only goal was reaching the center quickly, a large part of his explanation would make no sense.
Lian moved forward a few steps and then stood on one of the large roots to get a better view.
Three paths caught his attention more than the others.

On the left, at an unclear distance, a thin line of white smoke was rising from the forest, its source could not be seen, but the smoke did not look completely natural and despite the strong wind, it was rising almost straight up.
On the right, on a rocky high area, the tops of several broken pillars could be seen through the trees, something like a small ruin was located there.
The direct path was also almost in the direction of the central mountain, but the trees in that area were much denser and the ground slowly went downward.
Lian only thought for a few seconds and his eyes returned to the ruin.
"Let’s first see what you hid here." He then said with a little curiosity in his voice and jumped down from the root.
He changed his direction and moved toward the rocky high area, about five minutes later, something in the forest changed.
He slowed his steps.

At first, the change was so small that someone less careful might not have noticed it at all, the sounds of the forest were still there, the wind was still blowing and the mist was still moving between the roots.
But something did not match the natural rhythm of the area.
Lian continued moving without turning his head.
A few seconds later, the mist behind him moved against the direction of the wind for a moment.
Left.
Then he heard the very weak sound of a claw touching stone from ahead.
Three.
The corner of his mouth rose slightly.
"First strength and now perception?" The first test had tested his strength and now it seemed to be targeting his perception.
The mist around him slowly became thicker.

The nearby trees were still visible, but the viewing distance decreased from several dozen meters to less than fifteen meters, something moved inside the mist and the thin shadow of a body could be seen for a fraction of a second.
Then it disappeared.
Lian stopped and at that exact moment, he heard the sound of a claw scratching behind him, his body leaned slightly to the left and a black claw passed beside his neck.
Boom!
A wolf-like creature with a long and thin body jumped out of the mist, but before it could change the direction of its movement, the young Vorhelm’s fist hit its side.
The sound of several bones breaking could be heard and the monster was thrown to the side, but before it even reached the ground, a second creature came out from a blind spot.
Lian took one step backward and its claw passed only a few centimeters from his chest, and suddenly a third one attacked from above, this one had been hiding on a branch high above.
He raised his head and at that moment several short notifications appeared in front of his eyes.
[Simulated Monster.]
[Mistfang Hunter.]
[Rank: Normal.]
[Level: 26.]
Three creatures and all of them were Level 26, but their Level was not the problem.

The body of the first creature that had been hit disappeared into the mist and became visible again several meters away, the injury on its side was real, but its presence disappeared into the layer of white mist again.
"Interesting." This time, there was some interest in his eyes.
He could sweep through the entire area with raw speed or use Predator’s Instincts and finish everything quickly, but for now, he did not need to.
If the test was testing something, it was better to first understand what it was, now was the time to test his own guesses.
The two creatures disappeared again and he narrowed his eyes slightly.
True Sequence.
His eyes stayed fixed on the mist around one of the hunters.
At that moment, what had previously been only an unclear movement of energy became a clear structure.
Mana moved through the creature’s four limbs, gathered in the lower part of its stomach, and then spread over the surface of its body in a thin layer.
That layer was what mixed with the surrounding mist and hid the creature’s physical presence.
But it was not perfect, and at the moment of attack, the mana flow had to change direction.
The young Vorhelm waited without moving and one second later, the mana moved from the hind legs of one of the creatures back toward its spine.
Before its body could even become visible in the mist, Lian turned, his leg moved and the attack hit the creature directly under its jaw, forcing its head backward at an unnatural angle.
Its body was still in the air when it turned into mana particles.

The second one attacked from behind, the same change in the mana flow happened and Lian moved half a step to the side, grabbed its front claw by the wrist and slammed its body into the ground with one movement.
The ground under the monster cracked and before it could stand up, his heel came down on its skull.
The third one did not attack this time and only moved through the mist for several seconds.
Suddenly, the mana flow changed and moved to the right, and at that exact moment Lian raised his hand.
The monster’s claw stopped between his fingers a few centimeters before his face and the creature’s yellow eyes widened for a moment.
"Found you." He then said calmly and slammed his other hand into the monster’s chest.
The creature’s body bent immediately.
The attack did not come out from its back, but its force was enough to crush a large part of its rib cage.
The three bodies dissolved into mana one after another and the artificial mist around them also slowly disappeared.
[Simulated Monsters defeated.]
[Points increased.]
And a few moments later—
[Adaptive Evaluation updated.]
Lian stared at the last notification, no other explanation appeared.
"So my guess was correct, each wave of monsters is stronger than the previous ones, not only in Level but also in tactics, intelligence, and special abilities."
This was no longer just a group of monsters.
The first enemy had directly tested his physical strength and when it had achieved nothing, the test had not simply sent a bigger enemy, it had changed the type of challenge.
He was now almost sure that this was what Silas had meant, the test was trying to find his weakness and every new wave of monsters that came toward him would be stronger than the previous one.
But he did not care, he doubted that this test could find his weakness.

chapters.title: Chapter 430: The Broken Crown III
paragraphs: He continued on his way, and about fifteen minutes later, the ruins appeared among the trees, at first glance, there was nothing impressive about them.
On top of a rocky hill, a circular platform about thirty meters wide had been built.
There had once been four pillars around it, but three of them were broken and their pieces had fallen among the grass and tree roots.
The only remaining pillar was about ten meters tall and its surface was covered with faded lines.
Several half-collapsed walls could also be seen around the platform, and one of them had a carving of a broken crown on it.
Lian walked up the cracked stairs and entered the center of the ruins.
In the middle of the platform, there was a stone panel with five small slots.
None of them had anything inside, and at first glance, he could not understand what they were used for.
But the moment his foot touched the center of the platform, a faint light appeared on the stone lines.
[Sub-Test discovered.]
[Participation in the test is optional.]
He raised an eyebrow.
Optional.
Then he could turn back right now and continue on his path.
He looked around for a few seconds, if the goal was only speed, stopping here would be a waste of time.
But if Silas had intentionally mentioned special locations, ignoring the first one he found did not make much sense.
"We’ve already come this far, so there’s no problem with testing it, and besides, there is no time limit for the test."
[Sub-Test accepted.]
[Broken Path.]
A sound of stone came from behind the platform.
Lian turned around.
A large part of the mist moved away and revealed a narrow cliff behind the ruins, on the other side of the cliff, a small stone platform was floating in the air about one hundred meters away.
There was no bridge between them, and then the first piece of stone appeared in the air.
Then the second.
The third.
In less than a few seconds, a path made of floating stone pieces was formed toward the platform on the other side.
But before he could take a step, the first stone disappeared.
A few seconds later, it appeared again.
The second stone disappeared.
Then the fourth.
At first glance, the pattern looked random.
Lian stood beside the cliff and watched for almost a minute.
Each piece remained for three to five seconds and then disappeared for a different amount of time.
If someone was fast enough, they might be able to run across them without thinking, but one mistake was enough to fall into the sea of clouds below the island.
Of course, the protective seal would probably activate before death, but being removed from the test just because of a stupid rush was not worth it.
He looked more carefully, there was something on the first stone, a very small symbol.
He bent down a little to see it better, there was a nearly faded symbol on the surface of each piece, and every time just before the stone disappeared, its shape changed slightly.
"So it’s not only about speed, reaction time is also important," he whispered to himself.
Or at least it was not only about speed.
The symbols warned him before each stone disappeared.
If he could read the pattern, even someone who was not very fast could cross it.
He watched a few more cycles, then took a step and jumped onto the first stone, the symbol changed and he moved to the second without rushing.
The third was still there, but Lian did not jump onto it, two seconds later, the same stone disappeared.
He waited on the second piece, then moved to the fourth.
Every step was based on timing, and instead of racing against the disappearing stones, he let the path itself decide when he should move.
However, this strategy stopped working halfway through, because the order changed.
The stone that was supposed to appear did not appear.
The young Vorhelm stayed on the piece under his feet instead of jumping, the symbol on it was still unchanged.
Two seconds later, a new path appeared on the left.
"You even change it in the middle of the test?"
There was no answer, but now he knew what the test wanted.
A few minutes later, he landed on the platform on the other side and a short golden light appeared around the platform.
[Sub-Test completed.]
[Points updated.]
[Current Points: 164.]
Lian looked at the number for a moment, he still did not know exactly how many points he had received for killing each monster or completing this test.
It was probably intentional.
The test probably did not want them to know how many points they received for each action.
Then another light appeared in front of him.
[Sub-Test Reward]
A round metal token, almost the size of his palm.
Its surface was dark, and the design of a broken crown with silver lines could be seen on it.
[Broken Crown Token ×1]
[Use: Helper.]
"Helper? What does that mean?" He picked up the token and turned it between his fingers for a few moments.
No other notification appeared.
"Alright."
He placed the token in his storage space and returned through the stone path.
When he entered the forest again, he stopped after a few steps, a strange silence had filled the forest, and there was truly no sound.
The birds had gone silent, the sounds of distant creatures had stopped.
Even the wind, which had been moving through the trees almost without stopping since he entered, had now become a very weak breeze.
The mist around his feet was almost completely still, and he slowly raised his head.
[Performance Evaluation completed.]
[Adjusting difficulty level.]
The ground shook.
The roots sticking out of the ground moved, and several rocks fell down the slope beside the forest.
The birds that had remained silent until that moment suddenly flew up from the deeper parts of the forest and moved together toward the sky.
Something was approaching through the trees, this time, its footsteps were heavier than the monsters from the previous waves.
But it was not fast, every step was slow, and yet the ground shook under it.
Then two trees moved aside and a four-legged creature nearly four meters tall came out of the forest.
Its body looked more like a combination of black wood and stone than flesh.
Thick and uneven plates covered its chest, shoulders, and sides, and large roots were wrapped around its four legs.
Two bone blades came out from above its shoulders, and its small orange eyes lit up inside its stone-like head.
[Simulated Monster.]
[Ironroot Ravager.]
[Rank: Fallen.]
[Level: 18.]
Lian looked at the last number for a moment.
Level 18.
It was lower than the previous wave of enemies, but the Rank changed everything.
A real Fallen Monster at this level could give a Level 30 Awakened a lot of trouble and even kill a nornal one
The Ironroot Ravager roared and moved.
Unlike the previous monsters, it did not charge blindly, with every step, it kept its body lower, and the thick plates on its shoulders covered the front of its head and neck.

What had first looked like a simple movement of energy now had a clear path.
This creature did not have unlimited mana to strengthen its entire body.
Every time a part of its body came under pressure, mana was gathered from other parts and moved to that exact location.
Its defense increased, but at the same time, another part became weaker.
He attacked several more times on purpose.
Chest.
Leg.
Shoulder.
The monster reacted every time, and every time the young Vorhelm understood more clearly how the mana moved, and finally, his fist moved toward the front part of its chest.
The Ironroot Ravager strengthened all the central plates, its mana was released from the back of its body and gathered right in the lower part of its neck.
"No... you’re still too slow," Lian said mockingly, and his body disappeared.
He moved past the monster’s head, his foot landed on one of the large roots beside its body, and he used it to push himself upward.
His fist came down, right on the point where the mana had moved out of a moment ago.
Crack!
A large crack spread from the back of its neck down to its artificial spine.
The Ironroot Ravager’s legs bent, and its four-meter body fell heavily to the ground, sending some of the soil around it into the air.

[Points increased.]
The Ironroot Ravager’s body began to collapse and turned into thousands of pieces of light.
He gave it a short look and continued on his way.
He had already seen something in the northern part of the island from the height of the ruins, and after about ten minutes of moving, he reached it.
A bridge.
Or something that had once been a bridge.
Two huge stone chains stretched from the edge of the island toward another island in the distance, and large pieces of stone were placed on them.
But the middle part of the bridge was completely destroyed.
Lian walked to the edge.
The next island was about 150 meters away.
Below them, there was nothing except a sea of black clouds, and lightning sometimes lit up the depths of the clouds, with the weak sound of thunder reaching his ears a few seconds later.
The wind was much stronger in this area, beside the bridge, there was a short stone pillar, and three circular slots were carved into its surface.
He only needed one look to understand what belonged in them.
He took the Broken Crown Token out of his storage space, its size was exactly the same, and now he understood where this thing was used.
But he was still curious to know what it was supposed to do.
He placed it into the first slot.
Click.
The token locked into the stone, and silver lines on the pillar lit up, with light moving from it toward the bridge.
Part of the large gap began to rebuild.
New stones appeared in the air one after another and covered almost one-third of the empty distance.
Then everything stopped.
[Passage Activation: 1/3.]
Lian looked at the two remaining empty slots, so there were probably two more Sub-Tests somewhere on the island.
If he found them, he could complete the bridge and safely move to the next island.
It was logical and safe, and it was probably what most participants would do.
But he looked at the forest behind him for a few seconds, if each test took fifteen to twenty minutes, he might spend almost an hour just finding the other two tokens.
Then his eyes returned to the gap, with about one hundred meters still remaining.
"Should I find two more?"
"No."
He left the first token there, then stepped back a few steps from the edge.
Lian took a calm breath and lowered his body slightly.
[Thunder Step]
Blue lightning wrapped around his legs for a moment.
First step.
The ground under his foot cracked.
Second step.
A short explosion sounded in the air.
Third step.
He left the edge of the island, the stone under his last step shattered, and his body was thrown toward the sky like a bullet.
The wind hit his face with great force, for a few seconds, there was no ground, tree, or wall around him.
Only the gray sky, the next island in front of him, and the sea of black clouds hundreds of meters below his feet.
To some extent, it was a beautiful and amazing scene.
Then lightning flashed below him, Lian calculated his path, he had enough speed.
But right at that moment, a panel appeared in front of his eyes.
[Unauthorized crossing method detected.]
"Excuse me??"
[Method accepted.]
[Adaptive response created.]
"What—"
The black clouds below his feet exploded, and suddenly, a huge creature came out from them.
Two gray wings with a wingspan of nearly fifteen meters opened in the air and disturbed the wind around Lian.
The creature’s body looked like a combination of a bird of prey and a reptile, it had a long neck, black claws, and a beak full of thin teeth.
Its red eyes locked directly onto the young Vorhelm.
The creature flapped its wings once and charged directly toward him while he was still dozens of meters away from the nearest surface.
[Simulated Monster.]
[Fallen Sky Predator.]
[Rank: Fallen.]
[Level: 23.]
Lian looked at the notification for a few moments, then at the huge creature coming toward him at high speed.
There was nothing under his feet, and dozens of meters of empty space were behind him.
The island in front of him was atleast 50 meters away.
"Really?" He let out a short sigh.
