chapters.title: Chapter 432: The Broken Crown V
paragraphs: [Simulated Monster.]
[Fallen Sky Predator.]
[Tier: Fallen.]
[Level: 23.]
The wind passed strongly beside Lian’s face.
There was no ground under his feet, and the huge sea of black clouds stretched hundreds of meters below him.
The destination island was still dozens of meters away, and now a creature with two fifteen-meter wings was coming directly toward him.
Could things get any better?
The Fallen Sky Predator opened its mouth, and a row of long, curved teeth appeared inside its beak.
Its two huge claws opened under its body and it dived toward Lian at a terrifying speed, it was clear that it did not intend to simply knock him out of the way.
If those claws reached the body of a normal Level 23 Awakened, a large part of his body would probably be turned into pieces of flesh before the protective seal activated.
He looked at the creature for a few moments, then his eyes returned to the island in front of him.
"Really?" He let out a short sigh and lowered his right hand.
A sudden cold exploded around him.
Frost Dominion.
The moisture in the air froze in a fraction of a second and the sound of cracking ice spread right below Lian’s feet.
An ice platform about one meter below his feet formed.
He landed on it.
Crack!
His knee bent slightly, but before the platform could crack under his weight, a second platform formed a few meters ahead in the empty space.
Then he jumped.
The third platform.
The fourth platform.
The fifth platform.

In less than a few seconds, the young man who had been falling through the sky a moment ago was now moving several hundred meters above the sea of black clouds on a path that he created with every step.
He did not create a complete bridge, he did not need to, creating that much ice would only waste mana.
Each time, only one or two platforms formed in front of his feet, and immediately after he passed them, the previous platforms cracked under the pressure and fell into the depths of the clouds.
The roar of the Fallen Sky Predator spread through the sky again and the huge creature changed its path.
Lian only gave it a short look and the bird moved its right wing with all its strength.
Boom!
A strong wave of wind formed in the sky and the ice platform in front of him exploded before his foot could reach it.
Dozens of pieces of ice spread through the air and the platform under his feet also broke.
"Damn that bastard bird." His body began to fall again.
The Predator came down from above and opened its two black claws.
This time, the distance was so short that Lian could see the details of the gray scales on its legs.
The monster wanted to tear him apart right there in the air.
The young Vorhelm also lowered his hand and another ice platform formed right below his feet.
Thunder Step.
Blue lightning exploded around his right foot.
Crack!
"Since you want it this way, let me teach you a lesson." The ice platform under the pressure of his power shattered and his body shot out from its place like a bullet.
But not toward the island, instead, he shot directly toward the Predator and the creature’s red eyes changed for a moment.
This reaction probably did not exist in the information the test had created for it.
Lian opened his right hand and the air around his arm froze.
Ice crystals formed over his skin and in one moment turned into a huge claw with long and clear blades.
[Glacial Reaper Claw]
The bird brought its own claw forward and the two attacks collided in the sky.
Boom!
The impact wave exploded around them.
Three ice blades broke, but the bird’s huge claw was also pushed away from its path.
Lian’s body passed beside it and he swung his ice claw.
Slash!
Glacial Reaper Claw passed through the root of the Predator’s left wing.
No blood came out, instead, hundreds of blue and red mana particles spread through the air from the huge cut that had opened on its wing.
The bird screamed and its damaged wing stopped working for a moment, causing its huge body to spin in the air.
But Vorhelm also had no surface under his feet anymore and gravity was pulling his body down.
But he did not even look down and an ice platform formed beside his right foot, he stepped on it and changed the direction of his fall.
The second.
The third.
Each platform existed for only a moment, and on the fourth one, Thunder Step activated again.
Lian’s body was thrown forward and the remaining distance to the island disappeared in a few seconds, his hand reached the rocky edge and his fingers dug into the stone.
With one movement, he pulled himself up and landed on the ground, and at the same time, a terrifying roar came from behind him.
Lian turned around.
The Predator had tried to correct its path with its damaged wing, but it was already too late.
Its body crashed into the wall of the island at great speed.
Boom!
Part of the cliff exploded.
Cracks several meters long spread across the wall and the bird’s body was buried among the rocks.
It was still moving for two seconds, then it stopped, and at the same time, its body turned into thousands of pieces of light and the wind spread them across the sea of clouds.
[Simulated Monster defeated.]
[Unconventional Traversal completed.]
[Adaptive Evaluation updated.]
Lian looked at the notifications for a few moments.
"For a bastard that attacked with that much confidence, didn’t you die a little too quickly?" Then he snorted.
Although the bird was annoying, he had become a little more familiar with his Frost Dominion and had partly understood how it worked.
The ability to create ice from nothing was much more useful than he had expected and could be a great help.
Then he looked around.
The second island was completely different from the previous one.
The gray forest had been replaced by a dry and red land.
Huge rocks rose throughout the area and narrow valleys stretched between them like deep wounds in the ground.
Stone pillars sometimes reached hundreds of meters in height, and hot steam came out from cracks in the ground.
The wind howled between the valleys.
He moved without stopping, now he was almost certain that each island had been designed to test a different type of ability.
Only three minutes had passed when a panel appeared in front of his eyes.
[Performance Evaluation completed.]
[Previous challenges insufficient.]
"Now you understand that you shouldn’t underestimate me? If you want to entertain me, at least send something stronger." Lian said with a slightly amused expression.
It seemed that the academy system had heard his words, and suddenly the notification changed.
[Adaptive difficulty increased.]
The ground shook.
This time, the shaking did not come from the whole island, only the area in front of him and the red rocks a few meters ahead began to crack.
Pieces of the ground rose into the air, and thick lines of mana formed between them, pulling the rocks toward one point.
First, two legs formed, then the body, two arms, and finally an armor, its final form was a human figure made of stone.
But it was not a normal human.
It was more than two and a half meters tall and its entire body was covered in black and gray armor.
The armor plates were locked together without any gaps and a smooth helmet with no opening covered its entire face.
A sword almost as tall as itself was in its hand, and the tip of the sword dragged across the ground, the sound of metal scratching against stone spread through the valley.
The panel in front of Lian changed.
[Composite Challenge generated.]
[Crownless Executioner.]
[Rank: Fallen.]
[Level: 30.]
Lian’s eyes remained on the last number for a few moments.
Not only was it seven levels higher than his registered Level, it was also a Fallen Monster.
If the normal Level standard was used, sending such a creature against a Level 23 Awakened was almost ridiculous.
In fact, a group of hundreds of Rank 30 Awakened would be needed to kill such a monster.
"Looks like my words upset you a little." Lian gave a very faint smile.
He was sure that the academy teachers were watching him, and the sudden increase in difficulty was very large.
A Level 30 Fallen was not something to joke with, defeating it was not going to be easy even for him.
Another notification appeared.
[Combat Model: Adaptive.]
[Recorded Combat Patterns loaded.]
This time, his smile did not disappear.
So it had not only made it stronger, all the information the academy system had collected until now had also been given to it, it had basically been created only to kill him.
The knight lifted its sword from the ground and disappeared, and Lian’s eyes opened slightly wider for a fraction of a second.
It was fast.
Much faster than what the size of the creature suggested.
Suddenly, the sword came down from above and he moved his body to the side.
Whoosh!
The blade passed a few centimeters above his shoulder and struck the ground.
Boom!
The rock under them split and an almost ten-meter-long cut opened on the ground, sending pieces of stone into the air.
If Lian had received that attack directly, even his body after the First Evolution would not have been able to endure it without damage.

Even the strengthened body of a Fallen Monster would not have remained unharmed against such an attack.

But right before the attack landed, the Crownless Executioner lowered its left forearm.
Bang!
A sound like two heavy pieces of metal hitting each other spread through the valley.
The young Vorhelm’s fist hit the thick plate on the knight’s forearm and the force of the impact pushed away the dust around them, but the result was much less than he expected.
The knight only moved half a step backward and Lian’s eyes narrowed slightly.
"It has strong defense."
The sword was pulled out of the ground at the same moment and the blade moved horizontally at a terrifying speed.
Lian lowered his head and the edge of the sword passed only a few centimeters above his hair, but the knight did not stop its attack.
Its armored knee came directly toward the man’s chest and he raised both forearms in front of his body.
Boom!
The force of the impact lifted him off the ground.
His body moved almost ten meters backward through the air and then he landed on his feet, but the force had not stopped yet.
The soles of his shoes dragged several meters across the stone and left two deep lines behind his feet.

Lian lowered his forearms, a dull pain was rising from his bones, it was not real damage but it was enough to prove that this creature was not something he could simply push aside with a few punches like the previous enemies.
The Crownless Executioner moved again.
This time, he did not wait for it.
[Thunder Step]
Blue lightning wrapped around his legs and his body disappeared from its place in an instant.
But the knight’s sword moved almost at the same time, not toward where he had been standing but, surprisingly, toward the empty space on his right.
The exact point where he was supposed to appear after Thunder Step.
How did this bastard know?
How did it know so well where he wanted to appear?
Was the mechanism behind it really this advanced that it could basically understand the entire process of his battle?
Lian changed his direction in the middle of his movement, he had no other choice and at that moment the blade passed right in front of his eyes.
The pressure from the air burned the skin of his face.
If he had completed his path, his head would have been exactly in the sword’s path, he moved back several meters again and this time his smile became clearer.

"The more I think I have the upper hand, the more you show me that it is not enough." He was not angry, on the contrary, he was a little happy that he had finally found an opponent that did not get crushed immediately.
Maybe now he had a chance to try a few things.
The Crownless Executioner gave no answer, naturally, it was not supposed to, but it held its sword with both hands and lowered its body slightly.
The young Vorhelm immediately understood that the next attack was different.

A large amount of mana gathered inside the sword and the black blade was slowly covered with gray light, the pressure around it increased so much that the small stones near the knight’s feet started to shake.
Then the attack came, but not as a direct strike, instead, it pulled the sword from bottom to top.
Whooooom!
A huge gray slash separated from the blade and the ground split along its path.
Lian jumped to the left and the slash passed beside him and reached the rocky wall one hundred meters away.
Boom!
A large part of the cliff exploded.
Several tons of stone were thrown into the air and the wall, which had probably stood there for a very long time, suddenly gained a crack dozens of meters long.
He only gave it a short look.
"Alright, let’s stop joking around." His smile became a little weaker and his expression became more serious.
The knight attacked again and this time he also moved forward.
Metal and flesh collided several times at a speed that a normal Awakened could barely follow with their eyes.
Bang!
Boom!
Bang!
Lian punched the knight’s shoulder with his left fist and the armor plate cracked, but the Crownless Executioner seemed to know no pain.
Its sword came back from an unnatural angle and he was forced to pull his body back as the blade passed across his chest.
His clothes were cut and a very shallow line appeared on his skin.
Lian had not even had time to move away when the knight kicked him in the side.
Boom!
This time, his body hit the stone wall and the cliff behind him cracked.
Before the dust could disappear, the huge shadow of the stone knight appeared through it and the sword came down from above.
The young Vorhelm’s eyes widened for a moment, it was very close.
Frost Dominion.
A thick layer of ice formed between him and the blade.
Slash!
The sword shattered the ice like glass, but that short resistance changed the direction of the blade by a few centimeters.
Lian threw himself to the right.
Boom!
The blade smashed the place where his head had been a moment ago and the stone exploded, sending pieces of rock past his face.
He landed on one knee and immediately moved away, the look in his eyes had completely changed.
He was still calm but there was no simple amusement in his eyes anymore, this enemy could really hurt him.
A Level 30 Fallen Monster was already extremely powerful by itself, it would not be wrong to say that it was not much weaker than normal Level 45 monsters.
And this one was even worse for him because it knew his fighting process.
The Crownless Executioner pulled its sword out of the rocks.
Lian let out a short sigh.
"Alright, I admit it, I did not expect something like this for a school test, but do you think you’ve seen all of my power?"
He raised his hand and his storage space opened, dark light formed around his body.
A moment later, black-gray plates appeared over his body one after another.
Chest.
Shoulders.
Arms.
Forearms.
Legs.
The plates locked together like pieces of a living fortress and very thin silver lines lit up between them, and a huge weight fell onto the ground for a moment.
The stone under his feet cracked.
[World-Devourer Bastion.]
[Rank: Ancient.]
The Ancient full-body armor covered him, and the young Vorhelm opened and closed his hand once.
Despite the terrifying real weight of the armor, World-Bearing Frame spread a large part of the pressure across his entire body.

His movement was natural and without any problem, exactly like when he was not wearing any armor, but the mass of the armor was still real and that meant every attack he made from this moment would no longer be the same as before.
The knight showed no visible reaction and simply attacked, its sword came down again and this time Lian did not dodge, instead, his feet became fixed on the ground.
Mountain Anchor.
And he raised both forearms.
BOOOOOOM!
The impact was so strong that the surface of the cliff sank within a radius of several meters.
The impact wave threw dust and stones in all directions, but he remained in his place, he was not thrown back and did not even move one step backward.
The pressure of the blade spread from the point of impact across the entire armor.
Mountain Frame.
The force that could have broken his bones a few moments ago was now spread across the entire structure of the armor.
Lian looked at the knight from behind his forearms and a calm smile returned to his face.
"Try again." He then said in a cold tone.
His right hand became a fist and mana exploded inside his arm.
[Thunder Calamity]
Blue and purple light formed on his shoulder, ran down through the armor plates and covered his entire right fist.
The sound of exploding thunder spread through the space between them.
The Crownless Executioner pulled its sword back, and the young Vorhelm moved first.
His fist hit the center of the knight’s chest.
BOOOOOOOOM!
The thunder explosion lit up the entire valley for a moment, the two-and-a-half-meter stone creature’s body was lifted off the ground.
This time, it was not half a step.
The knight was thrown back several dozen meters like a bullet, it passed through a stone pillar and turned it into thousands of pieces.
But even that was not enough to finish it, its body rolled through the ruins and the sword fell from its hand.
Its movement stopped for a moment, then it placed its hand on the ground and stood up.
The central plate of its armor was pushed inward and several cracks spread across it, but it was still standing.
"Looks like you’re really tough." Lian’s eyes narrowed slightly.
The knight opened its hand and the sword rose from among the rocks and flew back toward its hand.
Bang!
The handle landed in its palm, and at the same time, the mana inside its body changed, its fighting stance also changed and it no longer held the sword with both hands.
Its left hand became free and the center of its body became lower and the position of its legs completely changed.
Then it attacked, although faster than before and the blade hit the side of his armor.
Bang!
Sparks spread through the air, Lian punched and the knight bent down and the attack passed beside its helmet.
The handle of the sword came close to the first one’s head and he was forced to pull his head back.
The stone knight’s knee hit his stomach.
Mountain Frame spread a large part of the force, but even with the armor, Lian moved one step backward.
The Crownless Executioner immediately entered his range and they began exchanging attacks.
This no longer looked like a fight against an artificial creature, it looked like a warrior who had survived for years on a battlefield.
Lian blocked several attacks with his armored forearm.
One of the blades scraped across his shoulder plate and created a deep cut on the surface of the armor.
[Structural Damage detected.]
[Structural Memory activated.]
The silver lines around the cut lit up and the black metal began to return to its original shape with a faint sound.
He looked at his armor’s skill with satisfaction, but the sword came again a moment later and this time the knight changed the movement halfway through.
He expected an attack toward his neck, but the blade changed direction and went for his knee!

chapters.title: Chapter 434: The Broken Crown VII
paragraphs: Lian pulled his leg back, the knight had almost managed to trick him.
The test was adapting, and this process was happening too quickly, as if the Academy’s simulation system and the teachers had decided to show him what this test was capable of.
Could they have been upset because of what he said?
In any case, he could no longer move forward using only his natural reactions.
True Sequence.
His eyes stayed fixed on the Crownless Executioner, and the mana flows inside the creature’s artificial body became visible.
But unlike the previous monsters, the image was not simple, dozens of paths were active at the same time.
Some went to the legs, some to the arms, some to the sword, some to the armor, and every few seconds the paths changed.
The knight intentionally did not leave a fixed pattern, and the sword came again.
Young Vorhelm blocked it with his forearm and his left fist hit the empty face of the helmet, the knight moved back but before he could continue, mana gathered inside the sword.
Another gray slash was released, and this time Lian did not want to dodge and brought his right hand forward.
Cataclysm Pulse.
Mana was compressed inside his closed fist, for a moment nothing happened, at least until he slammed his fist hard into the ground.
Then—
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!
A powerful compressed wave exploded from his fist, the air twisted in its path and dirt and rocks were torn from the ground.
The gray slash collided with the wave in the middle of its path and a huge explosion formed between them, causing the sky to be covered by dust for a moment.
The rocks around them cracked and the knight’s attack was destroyed, but Cataclysm Pulse did not stop and the remaining wave hit the Crownless Executioner directly.
BOOM!
The knight was pushed back several meters, its feet created two deep lines in the stone, but it still did not fall.
Lian did not take his eyes off it.
"You learned another attack, the problem is that the more you learn about me, the more I understand how you work too, this is a two-way relationship."
The knight attacked again and young Vorhelm allowed it, he needed to watch more of its attacks to understand what this monster’s weakness was.
One attack.
Two attacks.
Three attacks.
True Sequence followed the paths.
Before every change in fighting style, the knight’s mana returned to its chest for a moment, at first he thought it was only part of the normal process of controlling its body.
But no, every time, exactly every time, before changing the way it fought, the central core of its body redistributed the mana for less than half a second.
And at that moment, the defense around its neck and left shoulder became weaker, it was very small but it was there, and he understood.
Now he only needed to create that moment himself.
[False Presence]
A second presence appeared on his right side and both of them moved at the same time.
This time, the Crownless Executioner did not even turn its head toward the false presence and the sword came straight toward the real Lian.
The corner of young Vorhelm’s lips rose, but he did not care and reached half a meter from the enemy, then twenty centimeters, and then—
Frost Dominion.
A very thin layer of ice formed exactly under the knight’s front foot.

Not to stop it, but only to change the angle of its foot by a few degrees, and the Crownless Executioner stepped forward, its foot slipped, only a few centimeters, but a sword moving at such speed needed perfect balance to keep its path.
The blade passed beside Lian’s head and its edge scraped across the shoulder plate of the World-Devourer Bastion, creating a long shower of sparks in the air.
The knight reacted to correct its body position, mana gathered in its chest, and at that moment young Vorhelm was waiting for exactly this.
Thunder Step.
The explosion of thunder broke the ground under his feet and he disappeared from in front of the knight.
The Crownless Executioner turned its head, but the World-Devourer Bastion, with all of its real weight, was now behind it.
Thunder Calamity.
Blue and purple lightning wrapped around Lian’s arm again, but this time it did not stop and the lightning spread across his shoulder, chest, and both arms.
The sound of thunder roared throughout the valley and he planted his foot firmly on the ground.
Giant’s Momentum.
The mass of the armor, his body, and his movement speed were gathered in one direction, and his right hand moved backward.
"Let’s see if you can predict this one too." Then he said with a cold smile.
His fist moved.
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Thunder Calamity, together with the huge weight of the World-Devourer Bastion, hit the weak point behind the stone knight’s neck directly.
For a moment, it seemed as if time had stopped, and then the knight’s armor exploded.
CRACK!
A huge crack started from its neck, the plates on its shoulder collapsed, lightning entered the cracks, and blue light came out from inside its artificial body.
But the Crownless Executioner still did not fall, even in that condition, it turned around and raised its sword with one hand.
"You still don’t want to give up?" Lian was genuinely surprised for a moment.
The blade came toward his neck and he raised his left hand, the sword hit the armored forearm.
BOOM!
The forearm plate was pushed deeply inward, but it did not break, and he wrapped that same hand around the blade, the fingers of the World-Devourer Bastion locked around the metal.
The knight tried to pull its sword free but ...could not.
Lian looked directly at its empty helmet.
"You were really fun, but from here on, you’re just wasting my time." His right hand opened and mana gathered.
Cataclysm Pulse.
His palm was placed directly against the knight’s cracked chest.
"Fucking break!"
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The explosion happened at zero distance and the Crownless Executioner’s armor plates exploded from the inside out.
Its entire two-and-a-half-meter body was lifted from the ground and thrown backward at a terrifying speed.
It passed through one stone pillar, then a second pillar, and finally crashed into the wall of the valley.
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Half of the wall collapsed and hundreds of tons of rocks fell onto the place of impact, causing only the sound of falling rocks to be heard for several seconds.
Lian stood there and the lightning slowly disappeared from his armor, his breathing was slightly heavier than before, this fight had really consumed mana.
Frost Dominion.
Thunder Step.
True Sequence.
Thunder Calamity.
Cataclysm Pulse.
Even the World-Devourer Bastion had consumed part of his mana for Structural Memory and to maintain some of its functions.
But it was still not over, he could feel it, mana still existed under the rocks.
Suddenly—
BOOM!

Several large rocks were thrown into the air and the stone knight came out from the ruins, half of its chest armor was destroyed, its left shoulder almost no longer existed, and its sword was also broken in half.
But it was still moving.
Young Vorhelm stayed silent for a moment and then laughed, only a short laugh that came from real satisfaction.
"Damn... now I understand why your name is Executioner, fine, let’s finish this."
The Crownless Executioner attacked, bringing its broken sword forward.
Lian also ran, no complicated skill was needed this time and only a direct collision happened.
Giant’s Momentum.
Thunder Calamity.

Lightning exploded around his right fist and the knight brought its broken blade down, he moved his head to the side and the blade scraped across the shoulder of the World-Devourer Bastion and sent a long shower of sparks into the air.
Then his fist passed through the defense and hit the center of the bright core inside the stone creature’s chest directly.
Click.
For a moment, a strange sound came, and lightning passed through the Crownless Executioner’s body.
The light inside its chest went out, the knight took two more steps forward, and the broken sword fell from its hand.
Click.
Its body dropped onto one knee, then its head fell down and light came out through the cracks in its armor.
Its huge body slowly turned into particles of mana.
[Composite Challenge defeated.]
[Combat Difficulty exceeded recommended range.]
[Performance Rating: Exceptional.]
[Crown Points increased.]
[Crown Points: 356.]
[Adaptive Evaluation recalibrating.]
Lian looked at the last notification for a few seconds and thought a little about whether he should make another sarcastic comment, in the end, he decided not to.
He did not want to make the teachers so angry that they suddenly sent an Awakened who had completed three Evolutions after him.
Maybe he could fight a Level 30 Fallen that was equal to a normal Level 45 monster right now, but he had no chance against those who had completed three Evolutions.
Even defeating this one had taken a lot of effort and struggle.

The gap between the First Evolution and the Second Evolution was something that could be partly covered by some monstrous geniuses and with the help of Ancient Rank artifacts or Holy and Eternal Rank skills.

But no Awakened who had completed two Evolutions could fight even the weakest Awakened who had completed three Evolutions, after all, there was a reason why Awakened who had completed three Evolutions and above were given titles.
After the Third Evolution, every Power jump between each Evolution was very large.

Right now, against an Enlightened One, he was no different from an ant, even when he reached the Second Evolution, it was unlikely that he could cover the difference in power, that was how large this difference was, unless his talents experienced a greater evolution.

His palm was placed directly against the knight’s cracked chest.
"Fucking break!"
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The explosion happened at zero distance and the Crownless Executioner’s armor plates exploded from the inside out.
Its entire two-and-a-half-meter body was lifted from the ground and thrown backward at a terrifying speed.
It passed through one stone pillar, then a second pillar, and finally crashed into the wall of the valley.
BOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Half of the wall collapsed and hundreds of tons of rocks fell onto the place of impact, causing only the sound of falling rocks to be heard for several seconds.
Lian stood there and the lightning slowly disappeared from his armor, his breathing was slightly heavier than before, this fight had really consumed mana.
Frost Dominion.
Thunder Step.
True Sequence.
Thunder Calamity.
Cataclysm Pulse.
Even the World-Devourer Bastion had consumed part of his mana for Structural Memory and to maintain some of its functions.
But it was still not over, he could feel it, mana still existed under the rocks.
Suddenly—
BOOM!

Several large rocks were thrown into the air and the stone knight came out from the ruins, half of its chest armor was destroyed, its left shoulder almost no longer existed, and its sword was also broken in half.
But it was still moving.
Young Vorhelm stayed silent for a moment and then laughed, only a short laugh that came from real satisfaction.
"Damn... now I understand why your name is Executioner, fine, let’s finish this."
The Crownless Executioner attacked, bringing its broken sword forward.
Lian also ran, no complicated skill was needed this time and only a direct collision happened.
Giant’s Momentum.
Thunder Calamity.

Lightning exploded around his right fist and the knight brought its broken blade down, he moved his head to the side and the blade scraped across the shoulder of the World-Devourer Bastion and sent a long shower of sparks into the air.
Then his fist passed through the defense and hit the center of the bright core inside the stone creature’s chest directly.
Click.
For a moment, a strange sound came, and lightning passed through the Crownless Executioner’s body.
The light inside its chest went out, the knight took two more steps forward, and the broken sword fell from its hand.
Click.
Its body dropped onto one knee, then its head fell down and light came out through the cracks in its armor.
Its huge body slowly turned into particles of mana.
[Composite Challenge defeated.]
[Combat Difficulty exceeded recommended range.]
[Performance Rating: Exceptional.]
[Crown Points increased.]
[Crown Points: 356.]
[Adaptive Evaluation recalibrating.]
Lian looked at the last notification for a few seconds and thought a little about whether he should make another sarcastic comment, in the end, he decided not to.
He did not want to make the teachers so angry that they suddenly sent an Awakened who had completed three Evolutions after him.
Maybe he could fight a Level 30 Fallen that was equal to a normal Level 45 monster right now, but he had no chance against those who had completed three Evolutions.
Even defeating this one had taken a lot of effort and struggle.

The gap between the First Evolution and the Second Evolution was something that could be partly covered by some monstrous geniuses and with the help of Ancient Rank artifacts or Holy and Eternal Rank skills.

But no Awakened who had completed two Evolutions could fight even the weakest Awakened who had completed three Evolutions, after all, there was a reason why Awakened who had completed three Evolutions and above were given titles.
After the Third Evolution, every Power jump between each Evolution was very large.

Right now, against an Enlightened One, he was no different from an ant, even when he reached the Second Evolution, it was unlikely that he could cover the difference in power, that was how large this difference was, unless his talents experienced a greater evolution.

chapters.title: Chapter 435: The Broken Crown VIII
paragraphs: Lian did not remove the World-Devourer Bastion from his body.
After what he had seen just a few minutes ago, there was no guarantee that the next enemy would be weaker, and he had no reason to put the armor on again in the middle of a sudden attack.
However, he did not slow down, the goal of the First Stage was now clear to him.
The test did not want to count the number of corpses, it wanted to see how far you could go.
And a few minutes later, three wolf-like creatures appeared in one of the narrow rocky paths.
[Level: 27.]
[Level: 28.]
[Level: 29.]
Lian did not even stop, the first one jumped and his armored fist hit the creature’s face and smashed it into the wall like a piece of stone.
The second one attacked from the right.
Frost Dominion.
Ice formed around its legs and connected all four of its limbs to the ground for a moment.
Then the ice covered the rest of them too, and before they could even realize it, all three wolves were completely frozen.
And it did not take long for the ice to break and all three monsters were killed.
He continued along his path without even looking at them, and at the same time he noticed something, it seemed that not all the monsters were supposed to become as powerful as that stone knight.
That was not bad news either, he did not think he could handle more than two of them at the same time.
A little further ahead, a gap of almost forty meters cut across the path, but it was not enough to stop him.
Frost Dominion.
Ice came out from the edge of the cliff and formed a narrow, curved path directly in front of his steps.
He ran across it.
Every few meters, a new part of the ice was created in front of him, and the part behind him cracked a few seconds later and fell into the sea of black clouds.
Lightning flashed under the temporary bridge, and Lian reached the other side without even looking down once.
An ability that he had only started to understand less than an hour ago had now almost become like a natural extension of his body.
The test was adapting to Lian, but Lian was also adapting to the test.
[First Stage remaining time: 3 minutes.]
He slowed down for a moment, the central upside-down mountain now looked much larger.

The golden crown was still shining at its highest point, and even though several islands were between him and it, it was clear that the distance between them was much shorter than it had been at the beginning of the test.
In the distance, on another island, several small human figures could be seen, they were the first students he had seen since the beginning of the test.
He only gave them a short glance and turned his attention back to the notification.
The end of the First Stage? He expected the only goal to be reaching the upside-down mountain and obtaining the crown, but it seemed the test had more parts than it appeared to have.
In any case, he did not stop and continued along his path, he did not know what would happen at the end of the First Stage, but he preferred to get closer to the upside-down mountain.
[Remaining time: 1 minute.]
A few seconds later, mana gathered in front of his path again.
A large creature with six legs, a black body, and two long horns appeared.
[Simulated Monster.]
[Level: 30.]
[Rank: Normal.]
It seemed the test was still trying to cause extra trouble for him.
The monster lowered its head and Lian continued moving, the creature roared and ran toward him at high speed.
Frost Dominion.
Ice rose from the ground and wrapped around its two front legs.
CRACK!
The monster immediately broke the ice, but then dozens of ice blades appeared from nowhere and tore it apart.
Like the previous ones, he ignored this one too and after only making sure it was dead, he continued along his path.
The closer he got to the upside-down mountain, the more islands appeared in his sight, and he could see more students on them.
Some were trying to go toward the crown like him, while others were hunting monsters.
A countdown appeared.
Lian climbed up the rocky slope.
The wind around him became stronger.
He reached the highest part of the rock.
A large part of the Broken Crown appeared before his eyes.
Dozens of islands at different heights.
The entire realm shook and he stopped at that exact moment, a deep sound came from a very far distance.
At first it sounded like thunder, but it continued.
GRRRRRRRRRRR...
The ground under his feet moved, it was a real movement, the island had started to move.
[First Stage ended.]
The huge sound of rocks scraping against each other spread across the entire sky.
Young Vorhelm moved closer to the edge of the high ground, what he saw in front of him made even him stay completely silent for a few seconds.
The islands were moving, not just a few islands, all of them were moving.
Rock masses several kilometers wide were moving through the sky, some were going up, some were coming down, and some were slowly being pulled toward each other.
The black clouds below them became chaotic.
Lightning flashed one after another deep inside the clouds, and its roar mixed with the sound of the moving islands.
Chains as thick as towers came out from the sides of several islands.
BOOOOOOM!
One of the chains hit the wall of another island and sank into the stone.
Pieces of broken bridges came out from between the rocks and moved across the empty space.
The stones locked together one after another, and paths that had not existed a few seconds ago were forming before Lian’s eyes.
Two islands far away even directly crashed into each other.
BOOOOOOOM!
The shockwave from the collision could be felt even from several kilometers away.
Part of the rocks around them broke and thousands of tons of stone fell into the black clouds, and a huge panel appeared in front of the sky.
[Second Stage has begun.]
[Convergence.]
[All remaining participants will now be connected to each other.]
[The Royal Seals will soon activate.]
Lian ran his hand over the edge of one of the World-Devourer Bastion’s plates and looked around.
The individual stage was over, on an island that was slowly moving closer to his area, three human figures could be seen.
A few seconds later, two more people came out from behind a rock.
Five people.
On another island, more people could be seen.
And in the farther distances, human figures were appearing one after another as they moved closer to each other.
Groups were forming again.
Lian did not need to think much to understand who would benefit the most from such a rule.
Rodrick.
The initial spread had removed his biggest advantage, but now the people in his group could find each other again.
Ten people.
Twenty people.
Maybe even more.
The sound of the last piece of the stone bridge locking into place in front of him rang out.
Click!
He calmly looked at the newly formed path.
"So the crowded part starts now."
At that exact moment, BOOOOOOM!
A huge pillar of red light shot into the sky in the distance.
Lian raised his head.
The second pillar, blue.
Third, white.
Fourth, purple.
And finally, the fifth pillar, golden in color, rose from an island near the central mountain and broke through the thick layer of gray clouds.
Five pillars of light were shining in five locations, and a new panel appeared in front of all the participants.
[The Five Royal Seals have awakened.]
[Strength Seal.]
[Spirit Seal.]
[Speed Seal.]
[Resistance Seal.]
[Mana Seal.]
[To open the Crown Path, at least three Royal Seals must reach the central gate.]
[To obtain the Seals, defeat their guardians.]
Lian’s eyes moved between the five pillars, one of them was not very far from his current location.
White light, the Resistance Seal.
A calm smile on his face became a little deeper.
A Level 30 Fallen had managed to force him to bring out the World-Devourer Bastion.
So what would the guardian of one of the Five Royal Seals be?
But he was still curious to know the exact reason behind the name of each Seal, although a guess came to his mind.
"Could it be...?"
The First Stage had only been a warm-up, now the real competition had begun.

chapters.title: Chapter 436: The Test Adapts
paragraphs: Lian looked between the five pillars for a few moments.
The closest pillar to him was white.
Resistance Seal.
With the start of the Convergence, the islands around them continued to slowly move, and new paths kept forming between them one after another.
Stone bridges came out from the rocks, huge chains connected two islands to each other, and gaps that had been impossible to cross a few minutes ago had now turned into direct paths.
The First Stage had kept all the participants separated from each other for almost an hour.
But now the exact opposite was happening, the entire realm was pushing them toward each other again.
He stepped onto the newly built stone bridge and walked across it for a few minutes until he heard footsteps coming from the other side.
Five people were approaching from the other side of the bridge.
Lian slowed down, but it only took a few seconds for one of them to raise his hand.
"That armor can be recognized even from two kilometers away." Kain said with a big smile and walked faster.
"I thought you would have been eliminated by now." He replied calmly and raised his armored fist.
Kain hit his own fist against it.
Clack!

"I’m Level 34, and you’re still 23, if one of us was going to be eliminated, it would make more sense for it to be you." Kain said in a completely serious tone, but his smile made it clear that even he did not believe what he was saying.
"That would make sense, unfortunately, the test made the same mistake at first."
"At first?"
"I’ll explain later."
Behind Kain, Selina and Marcus also came closer, along with two other students whom Lian only knew by face.
Selina stared at Lian’s armor for a few seconds, and her eyes moved from the black plates on his chest to the thin silver lines between the joints.
"It’s beautiful."
And Marcus had the strongest reaction after her and practically checked every part of the armor, as a heavy warrior, or what was called a tank, this armor looked amazing.
If he had something like this, he could show his best.
"Where did you buy something like this?"
"That’s not something you can just find." Kain laughed when he heard his question and then answered honestly.
"Why?"
"Well, let’s just say that the materials used to make it don’t exist on the market." Lian answered this time, and he was not lying either, finding a World Devourer Giant was not possible.
Right at that moment, the sound of shaking stone came from the left.
A huge chain stretched between two islands and another bridge connected to their path.
Three figures appeared on the new bridge.
Rindo was moving ahead of the others, with Cassian and Ethan behind him.
"Finally." They increased their speed when they saw the group.
Ethan was still several meters away when his voice became louder.
"I’m glad you weren’t eliminated." And the Student Council President calmly added.
"Personally, I thought he would be eliminated, it’s really impressive that he managed to continue this far." Ethan looked at Marcus and said sarcastically.
Marcus only gave him an empty look.
For a few moments, despite the huge chaos happening around them, the atmosphere of the group became almost like the days before.
The same people.
The same jokes.
Only one big difference existed between them and nine months ago.
They had become stronger.
They had become more mature.
And most of them had seen things that normal Academy students might never see.
Rindo gave Lian’s armor a short look, but unlike the others, he did not immediately ask about it.
"Have you seen Seraphina and the others?" Instead, he asked about the others.
"No, I found Selina and Marcus about twenty minutes ago, it probably won’t take long for the others to find each other too." As soon as he said this, Lian looked toward the sky.
Almost at the same moment, a sound came from above, the sound of large wings pushing the air with great force.
Everyone raised their heads.
A silver shadow came out from behind one of the stone pillars.
A creature with a lion-like body and two huge wings was moving through the sky.
Its feathers were bright silver and became dark gray at the edges of its wings, four black claws were pulled under its body, and its eagle-like head had two bright blue eyes.
Its body was about three meters tall and its wings had a span of more than ten meters.
Two people were sitting on the creature’s back.
Liana and Seraphina.
The silver griffin made a short circle above the bridge and then slowly came down, the wind caused by its wings spread dust all around them.
Clack!
Its four large claws landed on the stone and Liana jumped down from its back and placed her hand on the creature’s neck.
"Flying is much cooler than I thought." Liana said with satisfaction and then looked at the rest of her friends.
"When did you guys find each other?"
Lian looked at the griffin for a few moments, he had never seen this creature before, if he remembered correctly, this girl had lost both of her summons in the Special Area.
A new summon should not normally be possible unless her First Evolution had given her the ability or allowed her to summon another creature.
And compared to her previous two summons, this one was truly much more impressive.
"Is this your new summon?" He asked while his eyes were still on the silver creature.

"That’s right! I got it after my First Evolution, the First Evolution increased my summoning capacity and opened a new slot, after that I was able to complete the contract with it." Liana said with controlled pride and stroked the feathers beside the griffin’s neck.
"Does it have a name?" Lian examined the creature again.
"Silvercrest Gryphon."
The griffin raised its head slightly, as if it was happy to hear its own name.
"This is so cool! A real griffin! You’re really lucky that you were able to summon something like this." Kain immediately interrupted their conversation.
"..." Liana looked at him with a frown, lucky? She had lost her two summons that had been with her for two years.
In the Special Area, she and all of her friends had almost been killed many times, and the hardships they had gone through were impossible to imagine.
And now someone was saying that she was lucky to obtain this griffin? After all that suffering, this was at least something she deserved.
But she did not know this boy, in fact, none of them knew him very well and they only knew that he was Lian’s friend.
And the griffin, feeling the anger of its master, opened its mouth and growled when Kain tried to pet it.
"Okay, okay." The boy immediately moved away from it.
The others who noticed this scene burst into laughter.
Seraphina climbed down from the griffin’s back and fixed her clothes.
When her eyes fell on Lian, they stayed on the World-Devourer Bastion for a few seconds.
"It’s really beautiful, congratulations."
"Thank you." Lian accepted the congratulations with a smile, normally no one congratulated someone for getting new armor.
But all of them could see that this was not normal armor, apart from its structure, this armor gave them a very strange feeling and it was not hard to understand that it was at least Rank S armor.
But they did not waste much time and after making a decision, the group started moving again.
They passed through several newly formed paths and chose the white pillar of the Resistance Seal as their first destination.
Among the five Seals, that one was the closest to them.
Rindo moved at the front and sometimes checked the positions of the other pillars, while the Silvercrest Gryphon flew above the group and Liana watched the area around them through her summon link.
"How was the First Stage for you?" Seraphina asked to pass the time when she saw that they still had some time before reaching their destination.

"Annoying, after a few fights, the test understood that I hunt more than I fight directly, then it started creating monsters that left no tracks, hid their smell, or created fake paths." Kain said with an annoyed expression.
The test’s mechanism had also identified the way he hunted and fought, and based on that, it simulated monsters for him.
"One of them was injured, or at least it looked injured, and it even left a complete blood trail, I thought I could easily kill it and get a lot of points."
"And that’s why you followed it?" Lian asked after thinking for a moment.
"Obviously."
"Was it a trap?"
"That’s not an important part of the story." Kain pressed his lips together.
"So it was a trap." Young Vorhelm laughed.
"Yeah, it was a trap, three other monsters were waiting for me, but the point is that I’m still here and they aren’t."
"For me, it was the opposite, most of the time I did not even have to fight." Rindo said from the front.
The others looked toward him, they had almost been forced to fight, and now hearing that one of them had not been like that naturally caught their attention the most.

"Choices, two paths, three targets, limited time, and almost always a situation where choosing one meant losing the other, every time it tried to force me to choose between something more valuable and something safer."
"My stage was almost the same, but it focused more on responsibility." Cassian also nodded.

"The main problem with the test is not that it is difficult, the problem is that it understands your personality very quickly and also understands how you fight." Rindo stayed silent for a few seconds.
"Exactly, after the third monster I had to fight, they could predict my attacks." Lian nodded.
The test was not simply about forcing them to fight the monsters in front of them.
It practically identified their personalities and adapted to them, Cassian was a responsible person, Rindo had the personality of a leader and the test had targeted his decision-making.
And Kain was a hunter and the test was testing exactly that.
And what about him? He was a direct fighter, he always tried to open his path with his fists and only used strategies and plans when the enemy was too powerful for him.
And the test also did exactly that instead of wasting time, it only made his enemies stronger to see his limit.

’Interesting, so if my guess is correct, the teachers want to completely find the students and their potential through this, and find out where each person’s limit is, this also benefits the guilds, they can see the strengths and weaknesses of the Awakened they want to recruit this way.’ He thought to himself.
So this was not just a test to determine the strongest student.
"What did it send after you?" Seraphina turned her eyes toward him.
"I only needed to fight monsters, each monster was stronger than the previous one, both in Level and Rank, but none of them were strong enough to stop me, except one, a stone knight."
"A stone knight? What was different about it compared to the other monsters? A much higher Level?" Liana asked curiously.
"It wasn’t only about the Level, its Rank too... it was a Level 30 Fallen." Lian answered calmly, as if he was only stating a normal fact.
But in their eyes, this was anything but normal, and Kain and Marcus’s jaw dropped as much as possible from shock.
The others were not doing much better...

And Marcus had the strongest reaction after her and practically checked every part of the armor, as a heavy warrior, or what was called a tank, this armor looked amazing.
If he had something like this, he could show his best.
"Where did you buy something like this?"
"That’s not something you can just find." Kain laughed when he heard his question and then answered honestly.
"Why?"
"Well, let’s just say that the materials used to make it don’t exist on the market." Lian answered this time, and he was not lying either, finding a World Devourer Giant was not possible.
Right at that moment, the sound of shaking stone came from the left.
A huge chain stretched between two islands and another bridge connected to their path.
Three figures appeared on the new bridge.
Rindo was moving ahead of the others, with Cassian and Ethan behind him.
"Finally." They increased their speed when they saw the group.
Ethan was still several meters away when his voice became louder.
"I’m glad you weren’t eliminated." And the Student Council President calmly added.
"Personally, I thought he would be eliminated, it’s really impressive that he managed to continue this far." Ethan looked at Marcus and said sarcastically.
Marcus only gave him an empty look.
For a few moments, despite the huge chaos happening around them, the atmosphere of the group became almost like the days before.
The same people.
The same jokes.
Only one big difference existed between them and nine months ago.
They had become stronger.
They had become more mature.
And most of them had seen things that normal Academy students might never see.
Rindo gave Lian’s armor a short look, but unlike the others, he did not immediately ask about it.
"Have you seen Seraphina and the others?" Instead, he asked about the others.
"No, I found Selina and Marcus about twenty minutes ago, it probably won’t take long for the others to find each other too." As soon as he said this, Lian looked toward the sky.
Almost at the same moment, a sound came from above, the sound of large wings pushing the air with great force.
Everyone raised their heads.
A silver shadow came out from behind one of the stone pillars.
A creature with a lion-like body and two huge wings was moving through the sky.
Its feathers were bright silver and became dark gray at the edges of its wings, four black claws were pulled under its body, and its eagle-like head had two bright blue eyes.
Its body was about three meters tall and its wings had a span of more than ten meters.
Two people were sitting on the creature’s back.
Liana and Seraphina.
The silver griffin made a short circle above the bridge and then slowly came down, the wind caused by its wings spread dust all around them.
Clack!
Its four large claws landed on the stone and Liana jumped down from its back and placed her hand on the creature’s neck.
"Flying is much cooler than I thought." Liana said with satisfaction and then looked at the rest of her friends.
"When did you guys find each other?"
Lian looked at the griffin for a few moments, he had never seen this creature before, if he remembered correctly, this girl had lost both of her summons in the Special Area.
A new summon should not normally be possible unless her First Evolution had given her the ability or allowed her to summon another creature.
And compared to her previous two summons, this one was truly much more impressive.
"Is this your new summon?" He asked while his eyes were still on the silver creature.
"That’s right!

I got it after my First Evolution, the First Evolution increased my summoning capacity and opened a new slot, after that I was able to complete the contract with it." Liana said with controlled pride and stroked the feathers beside the griffin’s neck.
"Does it have a name?" Lian examined the creature again.
"Silvercrest Gryphon."
The griffin raised its head slightly, as if it was happy to hear its own name.
"This is so cool!
A real griffin!
You’re really lucky that you were able to summon something like this." Kain immediately interrupted their conversation.
"..." Liana looked at him with a frown, lucky?
She had lost her two summons that had been with her for two years.
In the Special Area, she and all of her friends had almost been killed many times, and the hardships they had gone through were impossible to imagine.
And now someone was saying that she was lucky to obtain this griffin?
After all that suffering, this was at least something she deserved.
But she did not know this boy, in fact, none of them knew him very well and they only knew that he was Lian’s friend.
And the griffin, feeling the anger of its master, opened its mouth and growled when Kain tried to pet it.
"Okay, okay." The boy immediately moved away from it.
The others who noticed this scene burst into laughter.
Seraphina climbed down from the griffin’s back and fixed her clothes.
When her eyes fell on Lian, they stayed on the World-Devourer Bastion for a few seconds.
"It’s really beautiful, congratulations."
"Thank you." Lian accepted the congratulations with a smile, normally no one congratulated someone for getting new armor.
But all of them could see that this was not normal armor, apart from its structure, this armor gave them a very strange feeling and it was not hard to understand that it was at least Rank S armor.
But they did not waste much time and after making a decision, the group started moving again.
They passed through several newly formed paths and chose the white pillar of the Resistance Seal as their first destination.
Among the five Seals, that one was the closest to them.
Rindo moved at the front and sometimes checked the positions of the other pillars, while the Silvercrest Gryphon flew above the group and Liana watched the area around them through her summon link.
"How was the First Stage for you?" Seraphina asked to pass the time when she saw that they still had some time before reaching their destination.

"Annoying, after a few fights, the test understood that I hunt more than I fight directly, then it started creating monsters that left no tracks, hid their smell, or created fake paths." Kain said with an annoyed expression.
The test’s mechanism had also identified the way he hunted and fought, and based on that, it simulated monsters for him.
"One of them was injured, or at least it looked injured, and it even left a complete blood trail, I thought I could easily kill it and get a lot of points."
"And that’s why you followed it?" Lian asked after thinking for a moment.
"Obviously."
"Was it a trap?"
"That’s not an important part of the story." Kain pressed his lips together.
"So it was a trap." Young Vorhelm laughed.
"Yeah, it was a trap, three other monsters were waiting for me, but the point is that I’m still here and they aren’t."
"For me, it was the opposite, most of the time I did not even have to fight." Rindo said from the front.
The others looked toward him, they had almost been forced to fight, and now hearing that one of them had not been like that naturally caught their attention the most.

"Choices, two paths, three targets, limited time, and almost always a situation where choosing one meant losing the other, every time it tried to force me to choose between something more valuable and something safer."
"My stage was almost the same, but it focused more on responsibility." Cassian also nodded.

"The main problem with the test is not that it is difficult, the problem is that it understands your personality very quickly and also understands how you fight." Rindo stayed silent for a few seconds.
"Exactly, after the third monster I had to fight, they could predict my attacks." Lian nodded.
The test was not simply about forcing them to fight the monsters in front of them.
It practically identified their personalities and adapted to them, Cassian was a responsible person, Rindo had the personality of a leader and the test had targeted his decision-making.
And Kain was a hunter and the test was testing exactly that.
And what about him?
He was a direct fighter, he always tried to open his path with his fists and only used strategies and plans when the enemy was too powerful for him.
And the test also did exactly that instead of wasting time, it only made his enemies stronger to see his limit.

’Interesting, so if my guess is correct, the teachers want to completely find the students and their potential through this, and find out where each person’s limit is, this also benefits the guilds, they can see the strengths and weaknesses of the Awakened they want to recruit this way.’ He thought to himself.
So this was not just a test to determine the strongest student.
"What did it send after you?" Seraphina turned her eyes toward him.
"I only needed to fight monsters, each monster was stronger than the previous one, both in Level and Rank, but none of them were strong enough to stop me, except one, a stone knight."
"A stone knight?
What was different about it compared to the other monsters?
A much higher Level?" Liana asked curiously.
"It wasn’t only about the Level, its Rank too... it was a Level 30 Fallen." Lian answered calmly, as if he was only stating a normal fact.
But in their eyes, this was anything but normal, and Kain and Marcus’s jaw dropped as much as possible from shock.
The others were not doing much better...

chapters.title: Chapter 437: The Battle for the Seals I
paragraphs: Everyone except Kain had seen strange things from Lian during their time in the Special Area.
They had witnessed his power, they had seen him fight against an army of creatures that were above his own Level.
They knew that in terms of power, none of them could truly be compared to him, this was obvious, and they were not stupid enough to ignore it.
But they had always hoped that maybe they could catch up to him, maybe the First Evolution would be the point where they could finally reach this boy.
Each of them had gained a lot from their First Evolution, which made them truly hopeful again that maybe they could catch up to this monster in human skin.

But now, after hearing that he had been able to fight a Level 30 Fallen, and with his current Level, they understood even more than before how much they had underestimated the difference between them.
This difference was not something they could even think about reaching right now, in the future? Maybe, would they give up on competing with him? Of course not.
But how? How was this boy such a monster? Weren’t they the same age? All of them were among the best of their generation.
So where did this ridiculous and absurd difference come from? Even a genius with a five-star class should not be able to reach such a monstrous level.
They had already wondered before what rank and how many stars this boy’s talent and class had.
And once again, this question appeared in their minds, and this time they could not simply ignore it.

"You know how annoying you look when you talk about a Level 30 Fallen so casually?" Kain noticed the expressions of the others and immediately added this so they would not enter a discussion that his best friend would not like.
"Do you want me to say it was very scary?" Lian shrugged.
"No, because I know you would be lying, anyway, what is your score?"
"I have to check, wait...well, 391."
"Damn." Kain’s expression changed at that moment, he changed the subject but did not expect the new subject to hit him in the face like a slap again.
"You?"
"337, I was really proud of it until you told me your number."
"That is a good number."

"Compared to 391, that doesn’t count as a compliment anymore, what about the rest of you? Please don’t tell me your scores are also crazy like his." He looked at the others, hoping that they would be lower than him.
"I’m 315 too." Rindo opened his score.

"I’m 307, I never thought I would see the day when you could be above me." Seraphina laughed softly, but she realized that Kain had definitely gained something that allowed him to make such a big improvement.
Such a speed of progress and Leveling Up was not something a three-star class should be able to have, so what exactly happened to her cheap friend?
"I’m 291, maybe it is lower than yours but I’m completely happy with it, before this I thought I might even fail the test." Liana said with some satisfaction.
The Silvercrest Gryphon gave a short cry from above them.
Before this test, and before completing her First Evolution, she had been worried that she might really fail the test because she had no summons.
She was a summoner, and without her summons, she could barely fight and lost a large part of her power without them.
"I owe it all to that one, of course, having a summon with the ability to fly isn’t that useful in this test." Liana said while looking at her summon.
"After the test realized that I could scout from the sky or fly, it started creating things that were specifically made to bring it down."
"I’m 302." Cassian also said his score after checking it.
"I feel a little embarrassed, but it seems like I had the lowest score, I got 267." Marcus sighed after hearing their scores.
"If it makes you feel better, my score is 266." Ethan said with a not-so-happy expression, until now he thought he had a very good score.
But after seeing these people, he understood that this was not the case, comparing yourself really kills joy.
Everyone’s eyes fell on Selina, she was the only one who had not said her score.
"What did you get, Selina?" Liana asked curiously, they had not had much time to talk yesterday because each of them had been busy with their First Evolution.
But with the talent of her best friend, she had no doubt that her First Evolution must have gone well too.
"Well, my score is 295." The girl slowly said after seeing everyone looking at her.

"Really? I got higher? Then I won this time! How about you invite the Gryphon to dinner after this? No joke, I don’t think its food is cheap, especially because unlike the previous ones, it doesn’t only feed on Mana."
"The test isn’t over yet, how do you know? Maybe my score will be higher at the end." Selina shrugged and it was obvious that she did not want to pay for that monster’s food.
"Then let’s make a bet, if your score is higher, I will pay for the Gryphon’s food myself, but if my score is higher, you will do it for a year, okay?" Liana asked with a smile.
To buy food for tamed monsters, they only needed to use Student Points, but she did not want to spend them for now.
There was a Skill Book she had wanted to buy for a long time and she needed to save her Student Points, and if she had to pay for the Gryphon’s food too, she could not do that.
"Why should I pay for your summon’s food?" Selina snorted and refused.
Lian raised the corner of his lips, for a moment, he had a strange feeling, in the Special Area, he had seen this group many times at the edge of death.
The people who were now arguing about scores and simulated monsters had faced a Calamity from their own point of view just a few days ago.
But one person was not here and thinking about her made him unconsciously miss her.
’Did I really just miss that girl?’ Even he felt surprised and shook his head to get these thoughts out of his mind.
"Enough with the random discussions, we are getting close to the Seals, get yourselves ready." Rindo said seriously after seeing their stupid discussion.

chapters.title: Chapter 438: The Battle for the Seals II
paragraphs: After hearing his voice, the talking stopped and everyone got ready.
A few minutes later, a new notification appeared in front of all the participants.
[Each Royal Seal represents one Primary Stat.]
[Upon entering a Royal Seal Guardian’s combat zone, the corresponding Stat will be completely sealed.]
[The sealed Stat cannot be accessed, enhanced, recovered, borrowed or substituted until the Trial ends.]
[Strength Seal — Physical Strength Stat sealed.]
[Spirit Seal — Spirit Stat sealed.]
[Speed Seal — Speed Stat sealed.]
[Resistance Seal — Resistance Stat sealed.]
[Mana Seal — Mana Stat sealed.]
Lian looked at the notifications for a few moments, his guess was correct, each Seal represented one of the five Stats and fighting its Guardian meant that Stat would be sealed.
Then his eyes fell on the last line.
Mana Seal.
This one was truly cruel, if Mana was completely locked, all Skills would basically become unusable.
Another notification appeared.
[Skills, Talents and Equipment remain usable unless their activation directly requires the sealed Stat.]
[Registered Summons and Companions entering the Trial Zone will be subject to the same restriction.]
"Even summons?" Liana immediately looked at the Silvercrest Gryphon and her eyes showed tension and worry.
Maintaining a summon required Mana and without Mana she might not even be able to keep it for a few seconds and she could use those few seconds only to run away.
"Seems like it." Rindo nodded.
"This got much better." Ethan smiled widely.
"Which part of having one of your five Primary Stats locked became better?" Marcus looked at him.

"I mean Mana, this way we can see which of us is stronger without Skills...of course the other Stats aren’t bad either, this way we can understand your weaknesses and strengths, and see which ones you depend on more."
"Without Mana? Then mages have no chance." Selina said and the color of her face changed slightly.
For a Water Element user like her, having her Mana completely locked was the worst possible situation, she would completely lose her ability to fight.

"Then it is better if we don’t go toward that one for now." Lian gave her a short look and added, he would definitely lose part of his power without Mana, but it was not as bad for him as it was for the others.

Seris was probably one of the few people who would have no problem without Mana, or at least the person who would have the least problem, that girl got a large part of her power from her swordsmanship which required Speed and Strength.
"I completely agree."
"Resistance is the closest one and from this, it seems like the best choice too." Rindo pointed toward the white pillar.
"And apparently one of us decided to wear a castle today, even without Resistance you shouldn’t have any problem." Kain looked at the World-Devourer Bastion.
Lian looked at his armor, his Resistance Stat would be sealed.
This meant his body’s natural resistance, his ability to withstand attacks and many of the advantages he directly gained from that Stat would become unavailable.
But the World-Devourer Bastion was not part of the Resistance Stat.
Mountain Frame would still distribute the impact through the entire structure of the armor, World-Bearing Frame would still control the armor’s weight and Mountain Anchor would still exist.
"That’s right, this Seal might be the best choice." A smirk appeared on his face.
"Can you take the front line?" Rindo looked at him.
"Yeah, you can leave the front line and the main attacks to me."
"Then we’ll take that one for now."
"Three Seals are needed to open the center, do we want to take all three ourselves?" Cassian asked.
"Not necessarily." Lian answered.
Several looks turned toward him and he pointed toward Professor Silas’s explanation.
"He said three Seals need to reach the central gate, he didn’t say all three had to belong to the same group."
"Exactly, even if three different groups each have one Seal, the path to the center will still open." Rindo immediately nodded.
"Then why fight for the Seals at all?" Ethan asked.
"Because they give points? And points are still one of the most important things for deciding student rankings, the higher the rank, the better." Kain looked at him.

"Besides that, we can’t be lazy and create a bad image of ourselves, if the others get a bad impression of us, other factions might gain more control over the academy, you guys can stay out of it if you want, but the Student Council cannot just sit around." Rindo answered seriously.
Lian did not need to ask which faction he meant and could understand the Student Council President’s logic.
Rodrick wanted to rule the academy, it was not clear why, because naturally there were no direct benefits from it, maybe it was ambition or some other reason.
And he was definitely trying to get the highest rank in this test and create an absolute image of himself in the minds of the other students.

But Young Vorhelm was not stupid enough to stay silent and wait for the day that bastard came after him, doing such a thing would be stupid, especially when he was sure that sooner or later they would face each other.

He did not have an ambition like ruling the academy, but he was not going to let someone like Rodrick rule the academy either, and besides, isolating Kain just because he was Lian’s friend was not going to go unanswered.
This old grudge had to end as soon as possible, so he could focus on more important goals, such as clearing the Ruined Realm and finding the Calamity Anchor that had spread across their world.
And at that moment, the Silvercrest Gryphon flying above them suddenly changed its direction.
Liana remained still for a few seconds and her eyes focused on a distant point, she was using her summon’s vision.
"There is a large group northwest of us moving, very large...my God, I think group is not the right word, this looks more like an army."
"How many people?" Rindo asked with a frown.
"At least seventy...no, more are arriving."
"At least seventy? There is only one person who can bring this many students with him." Kain muttered.
Everyone looked in the same direction.
From a distance of several kilometers, the figures could only be seen as small dots, but their number was clearly increasing.
Students from two other bridges were also moving toward the same point.
There was no need to see Rodrick’s face, and the fact that people were gathering at one point with such speed almost made the answer clear.
"The First Stage forced him to be alone, but the Second Stage is giving him back his biggest advantage." Rindo’s face became more serious.
But a few seconds later, the large group changed and almost divided into three sections, each section moving toward a different pillar of light.
Kain was silent for a moment.
"Well...it seems some people don’t need to make decisions like we do." Seraphina pointed out an obvious fact.
"That is exactly the problem." The Student Council President did not take his eyes off the group, he felt like he had lost his position.
If Rodrick kept all his people together, he could have made a big mistake.
But he had not, he had sent three groups toward three Seals.
If all three succeeded, his faction could open the central path by itself.
And even if he did not take the Crown himself, controlling three Royal Seals would create a huge political and point advantage in the test.

Besides, losing to Rodrick’s group, especially when the Student Council President, his Vice President and the most likely next successor were all in one group, would destroy all the prestige and status they had left.
Now all their thoughts and plans were messed up, they did not want to let this bastard create an unbeatable and legendary image of himself in the minds of the other students.
But now how were they supposed to stop something like this? He was making a move that they could not make with their limited numbers.
"Lian, you don’t have an idea what we should d--where did he suddenly go!" Kain’s eyes fell on his friend, hoping that he had a plan.
But Lian was nowhere to be seen! Where the hell had that fucking vorhelm disappeared to?
Could it be...?
