"So there are even bonus points for who opens the gate." He muttered to himself and once again realized the importance of points.
Apart from the points, almost everyone’s eyes were on the broken crown on the upside-down mountain and they thought it would decide the final winner and first place.
But something told him that there was something wrong with that crown.
At that moment, the ground in the distance shook and several kilometers ahead, on the last island connected to the central path, a huge crack opened in the ground.
Two black pillars came out from the rock.
Ten meters.
Twenty meters.
Thirty meters.
Until the height of each one passed fifty meters.
Between them, a stone arch slowly formed and a dark golden surface filled the empty space inside it, something like still water with no waves on its surface.
At the bottom of the arch, three stone platforms also rose from the ground and each one had a place for a Seal.
Only three places.
Behind the Gate there was still nothing and only empty space, the sea of black clouds and the upside-down mountain floating kilometers away in the sky.
Lian looked at the scene for several seconds and then opened his points panel.
[Points: 994.]
His eyebrow rose slightly.
"Nine hundred and ninety-four..."
Before entering the second stage, he had not even reached four hundred, but two Royal Seal Guardians, two Seals and his performance in the battles had caused his points to almost triple.
The main question was where everyone else stood.
How many points did Rodrick have?
He knew the points of his friends, and it was unlikely that they had changed much.
And maybe there was only one person who had a chance of having points close to his, and even that person was unlikely to have a performance anywhere near his.
But in any case, the answer did not matter for now and he headed toward the Gate.
About ten minutes later, Lian found his group of friends.
Even before getting completely close, it was clear that the battle against the Resistance Seal Guardian had been hard enough for them.
A temporary bandage was wrapped around Rindo’s right arm and a red spot was slowly appearing under the cloth.
Seraphina was sitting beside a large rock and pouring a healing potion over the deep cut on her shoulder.
Kain’s armor was torn at the side and a large bruise covered almost the entire left side of his body.
Ethan was wiping the dried blood under his nose with the back of his hand and Marcus was drinking the last bit of a recovery potion with an unhappy expression.
Even Liana’s Silvercrest Gryphon had not escaped without injuries.
Several long feathers on its right wing were broken and there was a mark from a heavy hit on the natural armor of its chest.
Selina was bandaging the wound on Cassian’s forearm when the sound of the heavy steps of Ancient armor spread along the path.
Everyone raised their heads and Liana was the first to smile.
"Finally, there he is."
Kain immediately turned around.
"Where did you disappear—" His words stopped halfway and his eyes fell on the young Vorhelm’s hands.
There were two Seals in his hands!
They had heard it from the system notification, but seeing it with their own eyes ...was even more shocking.
For several seconds, his mind seemed unwilling to accept what he was seeing.
"Wait a second...are these two both real?"
"As far as I know, yeah."
Kain first looked at the Seals, then at the rest of the group and then back at Lian.
"We all went and got one Seal, all of us!
We had to go through so much trouble just to defeat one Guardian and ...you got two during the same amount of time?" He thought that the distance between him and his best friend had disappeared.
But it seemed that it had not only failed to disappear, it had reached an unbelievable level instead ...how was something like this even possible?
"That doesn’t matter, what matters is that we have three Seals now." Lian was too lazy to answer and he really had no idea how he could explain it in a logical way.
Seraphina stood up and her eyes stayed on the two Seals for a few moments before slowly settling on his face.
He had defeated two Guardians in almost the same amount of time as all of them had needed to fight one Guardian.
She already knew that the difference between Lian and the others was large.
But every time she thought she had finally understood the real size of that difference, this boy did something that made her previous estimate look ridiculous.
Rindo also said nothing but his calculating eyes had reached almost the same conclusion.
"Well...at least we don’t have to worry about whether we have three Seals anymore." He finally added and brought them back to the main matter.
"Now we have to worry about who reaches the Gate before us." Lian reminded them of an important point.
If Rodrick arrived earlier and placed two Seals into the platforms, his group could still get the highest points from this part.
That sentence was enough to end the jokes and the Student Council President immediately nodded.
"We move, drink your potions while we go, we don’t know how much time we will have after the Gate opens."
The group started moving again.
The farther they went, the larger the huge upside-down mountain became, from this distance it was no longer just a black mass in the sky.
Huge floating rocks could be seen around it and several strange rivers flowed across its surface, rivers that moved upward from the lower part of the mountain against gravity.
Chains as thick as buildings hung from different parts of it, but some of them were connected to nothing and their ends floated in empty space.
Ruins could also be seen on the surface of the mountain.
Broken towers, huge stairs, walls with parts of them buried inside the rock and above everything else ...the golden and black crown.
It was still floating like a small star at the highest part of the mountain.
But there was no bridge or path between the island and the mountain.
The only way was that Gate.
When Lian’s group reached the central field, no one else was there yet.
They stood in front of the three Seal platforms.
"I think we arrived first." Rindo looked around.
"I think more accurately, we arrived at the same time." Seraphina said calmly and it was clear that she had sensed something.
A sound came from one of the bridges behind them, the sound of many footsteps.
Everyone turned to see what was happening and saw a few people appear first, then ten ...twenty...thirty and the number continued to grow.
Rodrick’s group entered the field from the end of the bridge, although there was no longer any sign of that army of more than seventy people.
Some had been eliminated in the Guardian battles and some were still on the way but there were still more than forty people with him, practically several times more than their group.
Rodrick was walking in front, with a Seal shining in his hand.
Strength Seal.
A little behind him and to his right, Elena was walking and had the Mana Seal.
So all five Seals now had holders.
The two groups stopped on opposite sides of the field, no one attacked and no one even spoke, but the air became noticeably heavier.
Rodrick’s eyes first fell on Rindo, then on the Resistance Seal and then slowly moved toward Lian.
The two Seals were not in his hands, but the public notifications had already made it clear who had obtained them.
Rodrick’s face remained cold and no extra emotion could be seen except for one long and calculating look.
The young Vorhelm also looked directly at him, several moments passed and then the corner of his lips rose slightly.
"It’s been a while since we’ve seen each other." He said calmly.
Rodrick looked at him for several seconds.
"It should be around ten months, right?
Of course, it seems less time has passed for you, but it’s clear that you’ve changed as much as ten months."
"Long enough." Lian answered, another gaze was also still on him.
Elena.
The girl’s eyes first stayed on his face.
Then they moved down to the World-Devourer Bastion.
Then to his hands and the two Seals that she knew he had taken by himself and a complicated feeling passed through the depths of her eyes.
Shock?
Regret?
Sadness?
Maybe something else.
None of them were clear enough to give them a name, perhaps even she did not know exactly what she was feeling.
Lian kept his eyes on her for a moment, only a moment and then looked away without any special reaction.
Something in Elena’s expression became tense for a fraction of a second, but she controlled it immediately.
The young Vorhelm was now looking at someone else.
Darren.
He was standing in the second row beside Rodrick and from the moment they entered the field, he had deliberately tried not to look at him even once.
Unfortunately for him, Lian had not forgotten and his smile became a little deeper.
"Oh, good that you came too, it’s time to do your bet." He then said in a friendly tone.

chapters.title: Chapter 444: A Bet Must Be Paid
paragraphs: Darren’s body froze for a moment.
Several people who had witnessed the previous bet also had strange expressions, one of them lowered his gaze while another pressed his lips tightly together to stop himself from laughing.
"What bet?" Rodrick turned his gaze toward Darren, it was clear that his subordinate had not dared to tell him the whole truth about what had happened.
"It’s nothing important." But his face changed slightly.
"It’s important to me." Lian raised an eyebrow.
"I asked what bet?" His voice was not loud, but Darren immediately understood that he could not avoid the subject.
Before he could say anything himself, one of the people in the group who had been at the Speed Seal explained what happened with some hesitation.
The ten-minute bet.
Lian entering alone.
Defeating the Guardian in seven minutes and forty-one seconds.
And the punishment for the loser.
When he finished speaking, a strange silence appeared.
"You really made that bet?" Kain slowly turned his head toward his best friend.
"Yeah, actually he made that bet, and I just repeated the same thing as what I wanted."
After hearing the explanation, he started laughing loudly, and a big smile appeared on his face.
Rodrick did not laugh, however, and stared at his stupid subordinate for several seconds.
Darren expected him to say something to save him, or at least declare the bet unimportant, he did not want to suffer such humiliation, he did not want to do something like this.
If he did such a thing, how was he supposed to continue living after this? How could he hold his head up in front of everyone?
How could he remain his right-hand man?
"Do it." But Rodrick only said two words.
"What?"
"You lost your bet. So do it."
"But Rodrick, it was just a stupid bet and he—"

"You were the commander of one of my groups, you made that bet in front of the members of that same group, if you go back on your word now, you won’t just lose your own reputation, you’re telling everyone that the word of one of my people has no value."
"But—" Darren clenched his fists.
"I won’t say it twice." Rodrick’s gaze became even colder, and it was clear that this was his final warning.

Everything was over, and Darren knew there was no way to back down anymore, even if he could endure the humiliation in front of Lian, directly disobeying Rodrick in front of dozens of people would be much worse for him.
His face had turned red, his jaw was shaking from the pressure, but in the end he slowly lowered himself.
One knee.
Then the other.
Then he put both hands on the ground.
Kain immediately turned his head away and covered his mouth with one hand, his shoulders shaking from laughter.
"No... no, this is really happening." He said between laughs.
He had never thought he would be able to see such a scene, this bastard had humiliated and made fun of him throughout all these months, he had insulted Lian many times.
Many times, whenever he had the chance, he caused trouble for him and was responsible for making sure that just because he was Lian’s friend, he would not have an easy life.
It went so far that they isolated him and cut off all his connections.
And now he was barking in front of everyone like this... Karma really could be a strange thing.
Darren started the first round, his face almost purple from shame.
"Woof... woof..."
"Louder, the sound of the wind is louder than you." Lian tilted his head slightly.
Darren stopped for a moment, gave him a look full of hatred, and then clenched his teeth.
"Woof! Woof!"
Kain could no longer hold himself back, and his laughter spread across the field.
Even several people from Rodrick’s group turned their eyes away, because if they looked directly at Darren, they might lose control of their expressions.
Three rounds.
Each round was more painful than the one before, and when it was over, he almost jumped off the ground and moved back without looking at anyone.
"Acceptable." The young Vorhelm nodded with satisfaction.
If looks could kill, Darren would probably be trying to kill him a hundred times right now.
But Rodrick did not look at him even once, the matter was already over for him, and this time he turned toward Rindo.
His manner became formal again.
"Student Council President, your group’s result is truly respectable. Three out of five Seals is not something that can be explained by luck, congratulations." He said with apparent respect.
"What are you after?" Rindo looked at him carefully.
"Nothing, I just think it’s appropriate to show my respect to the current Student Council President before the school year ends." He paused for a moment and continued.
"If the students choose me, I would be honored to inherit your position."
"The Student Council is not a kingdom that has an heir." But it was clear that the current Student Council President was not happy.
"Of course it isn’t, that’s why I said if the students choose me." Rodrick added, and the sentence sounded completely respectful on the surface.
But the confidence behind it was almost insulting, he was not speaking as someone who might become the next Student Council President.
He was speaking like someone who was only waiting for something to become official that he already considered his.

"Choice? Like the choice everyone else had when they decided not to group with me? Did you really give them a choice? You basically told them either isolate him or I’ll make your lives miserable!" Kain let out a humorless laugh from beside Lian.
The atmosphere of the field became several degrees colder, and Rodrick shifted his gaze toward him.
"I never told anyone not to work with you." No anger appeared on his face.
Kain smiled, but there was no warmth in it.
"Of course, you’re much smarter and... more of a bastard than to directly say something like that."
He took one step forward.

"You just created a system where anyone who worked with me would lose better missions, strong teams, and the support of your group, the group that was the strongest faction in the academy after the Student Council... though now I should say the strongest? Anyway, then you stood aside and let everyone figure out for themselves what choice they had to make."

"I gave the resources that belonged to my group to the members of my group, nobody was required to join me. Nobody was forced to distance themselves from you." Rodrick stayed silent for a few seconds.

"Yeah. You found a nice explanation for it." Kain sneered, he was talking about his own resources, but in reality, by putting pressure on the members of his group, he had forced them to always spend whatever Student Points they had on resources so those resources would not reach him.
He tried to get the resources he wanted from outside the academy, but they were very expensive, and his only hope was his family, who were able to help him a little.
Unfortunately, his family was not as rich as the Vorhelms or that bastard’s family, and he had limited resources.
He needed resources to maximize his stats, not everyone was like Lian and could gain stats by hunting.
In the end, he was forced to find the things he wanted himself through exploration and advancing deeper.
"It’s called a choice." Rodrick kept looking directly into his eyes.
For a moment, no one said anything, and these few sentences showed Rodrick’s true character more than any shouting or threat could.
He did not see himself as a bully, to him, power meant creating conditions.
If people made a decision that benefited him under those conditions, in his mind, it was still their own choice.
Rindo was worried about the possibility of him becoming the next president for exactly this reason.
This boy did not need to openly break a rule, he could make the rules appear to remain in place, while the result was always what he wanted.
Finally, Rodrick took his gaze away from Kain and looked at the three platforms of the Gate.
"Anyway, you won this part."
Several people from Lian’s group raised their eyebrows, and he slightly raised his hand, causing his people to step back a few steps.
"You have three Seals. We have two, the rules are clear, put your Seals in, take your reward, and open the path."
’What the hell is this bastard thinking?’ All of them suddenly frowned more deeply, and the same thought appeared in their minds.

chapters.title: Chapter 445: A Successful Trap...?
paragraphs: ’What the hell is this bastard thinking?’ Everyone’s frowns suddenly became deeper, and the same thought appeared in their minds.
"He backed down way too easily." Seraphina also did not trust this offer much.
Marcus looked around.
"Maybe he wants to look fair in front of everyone. If he starts a fight over the three platforms now, all the participants watching the result will notice."
"Or he is sure he can defeat us after the path opens." Rindo said calmly.
"Or both." Kain looked at Rodrick.
Lian said nothing, he had been watching the behavior of Rodrick’s people for the past few minutes.

Three mages were on the right side of the field, four people were on the left, and two more were standing a little farther back, none of them were acting directly threatening, but the way they were standing was too organized.
The distances between them were almost equal and more importantly, he had felt short flows of Mana in the ground several times.
They were very weak and so small that perhaps a normal person would not notice them, but his senses were too sensitive to such things.
And there was only one conclusion he could make from this, something was being prepared.
And one thing was clear, without opening the Gate, Rodrick could not reach the Crown either, and whatever plan he had, it had to be carried out after the path was activated.
"Put the Seals in." Lian suddenly said.
Everyone turned their eyes toward him.
"Are you sure?" Kain frowned.
"No." The young Vorhelm answered without hesitation.
"That was a very reassuring answer, so why exactly do you want us to put the Seals in?"
"If he has a plan, he can’t complete it before the path opens. We also can’t go anywhere without opening the path, it has to be opened in the end anyway, so let’s see what’s in his head."
Rindo looked at him for a few moments and then at the platforms, it was logical, even if they knew that bastard had a plan, there was nothing they could do, they had to open the path anyway.
"Alright." He finally nodded.
The group moved forward, and Rodrick and his people really stayed behind.
First, the Resistance Seal was placed on the platform on the left.
Clack!
White light ran from the bottom to the top of one of the fifty-meter pillars.
[Resistance Seal registered.]
Then Lian took out the Spirit Seal and placed it on the central platform.
[Spirit Seal registered.]
One platform remained, and Lian turned the Speed Seal between his fingers, for a moment his eyes moved toward Rodrick, he was still standing calmly.
Clack!
The third Seal locked into its place.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The entire Gate lit up, a wave of golden light covered the field, and a huge wind came out from the arch.
[Three Seals registered.]
[Alliance Contribution: 3 of 3.]
[Highest Contribution confirmed.]
[Crown Point reward is being distributed.]
Separate notifications appeared.
[Direct contribution in registering two Seals confirmed.]
[Lian’s reward: 200 Points.]
[Crown Points: 1194.]
The other members of the group also received Points based on their contribution, but no one had time to check the numbers for long.
The golden surface inside the arch exploded, and light shot into the empty space in front of the Gate, and several hundred meters ahead, the first piece of stone appeared in the air.
Then the second.
The third.
Dozens.
Hundreds.
The stones appeared in the empty space at an incredible speed and locked together one after another.
Clack!
Clack!
Clack!
A straight path several kilometers long formed over the sea of black clouds and continued directly toward the surface of the upside-down mountain.
At the end of it, huge stairs lit up on the body of the mountain, thousands of stairs appeared, and the Crown was at the top of them.
For a few seconds, the entire field watched the scene in silence, the path had opened, and they had entered the final stage of the test.
"Now! Execute the plan!" Rodrick suddenly shouted, and all the calmness disappeared from his voice.
Lian’s eyes narrowed.
The same mages who had been spread across different points of the field before almost sat down on one knee at the same time.
Their hands and staffs touched the ground, and Mana exploded, the lines that had been hidden inside the stone until that moment lit up under the group’s feet.
"Watch out!" He shouted a warning.
Frost Dominion.
Cold exploded in an instant, and a huge wall of ice rose in front of the group, and one second later hell was unleashed.
Dozens of Mana attacks hit the wall at the same time.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The entire ice wall exploded in a huge blast, and billions of pieces of ice spread across the field.
Even with Lian’s warning, several people had to throw themselves onto the ground.
But this was only the first layer, and four black walls rose from the ground.
Boom!
Boom!
Boom!
Boom!
They surrounded the group from four sides, and that was not the end, the mages spent their Mana again, and chains came out.
Shapes and symbols appeared around them, and it was clear that this was not a simple skill.
Hundreds of glowing chains shot through the walls and rushed toward the members of the group.
[Seven-Layer Prison Array.]
"They prepared it beforehand!" Rindo shouted angrily and knocked away the blade of one of the chains.
"That bastard was buying time from the beginning!" Kain broke another one with his fist.
Marcus created a shield in front of himself.
"Damn it! That conversation and his backing away were all to complete this Array!"
Everything he had said, all of his actions, and even forcing Darren to bark like a dog were only to buy time and make sure his plan would work.
And it had worked, the path in front of him was now open, and everyone else was trapped in the Array.
"I’m going to kill those bastards!" Ethan did not need any more analysis.
He ran directly toward one of the walls, and on the other side of the field, Rodrick did not stay even for a moment to watch the result.
"Let’s go." His eyes moved toward Elena.
The girl only paused for a moment, turned her head, and through the black walls and Mana explosions, her eyes met Lian’s for a fraction of a second.
The same complicated feeling appeared again, this time there was perhaps even some doubt in it.
But it was only for a moment, then she turned around, and she and her new boyfriend ran toward the central path.
Several of the fastest members of the group also moved with them.
"No, I won’t let—" Kain saw them, he did not want those bastards to get the Crown and take first place in this test.
However, two chains passed beside his head and blocked his path, forcing him to move back and making it impossible for him to follow them.
He clenched his teeth, he wanted to force his way through, but more chains appeared from nowhere.
All the mages in Rodrick’s group had joined together to create this Array and were working together.
Seraphina pulled out her sword, and a slash appeared in the air.
SHRAAAK!
Three chains were cut at the same time, but four more chains took their place.
"This Array isn’t meant to kill us! They only want to hold us here!" Rindo suddenly understood and looked at Rodrick, who was getting farther away every second.
Lian had reached the same conclusion, in fact, he had understood something even more important.
Rodrick had not underestimated them.
If he thought their group was weak, there was no need for several mages, a prepared Array, seven layers of restraints, and a surprise attack.
He could have attacked directly after the Gate opened.
But he didn’t.
He knew exactly how dangerous this group was.
He respected their strength enough to prepare a complete plan to stop them for several minutes before reaching the field.
"... he didn’t even think for a moment that we were weak." The Student Council President also realized this truth.
Many students underestimated them because of their Levels, but Rodrick had not done that.
Kain sent one of Rodrick’s students flying several meters back with his fist.
"Should we be happy that he respects us?! We can’t let him take first place!" In fact, this was even worse from his point of view.

sentences.text: ’What the hell is this bastard thinking?’ Everyone’s frowns suddenly became deeper, and the same thought appeared in their minds.
"He backed down way too easily." Seraphina also did not trust this offer much.
Marcus looked around.
"Maybe he wants to look fair in front of everyone.
If he starts a fight over the three platforms now, all the participants watching the result will notice."
"Or he is sure he can defeat us after the path opens." Rindo said calmly.
"Or both." Kain looked at Rodrick.
Lian said nothing, he had been watching the behavior of Rodrick’s people for the past few minutes.

Three mages were on the right side of the field, four people were on the left, and two more were standing a little farther back, none of them were acting directly threatening, but the way they were standing was too organized.
The distances between them were almost equal and more importantly, he had felt short flows of Mana in the ground several times.
They were very weak and so small that perhaps a normal person would not notice them, but his senses were too sensitive to such things.
And there was only one conclusion he could make from this, something was being prepared.
And one thing was clear, without opening the Gate, Rodrick could not reach the Crown either, and whatever plan he had, it had to be carried out after the path was activated.
"Put the Seals in." Lian suddenly said.
Everyone turned their eyes toward him.
"Are you sure?" Kain frowned.
"No." The young Vorhelm answered without hesitation.
"That was a very reassuring answer, so why exactly do you want us to put the Seals in?"
"If he has a plan, he can’t complete it before the path opens.
We also can’t go anywhere without opening the path, it has to be opened in the end anyway, so let’s see what’s in his head."
Rindo looked at him for a few moments and then at the platforms, it was logical, even if they knew that bastard had a plan, there was nothing they could do, they had to open the path anyway.
"Alright." He finally nodded.
The group moved forward, and Rodrick and his people really stayed behind.
First, the Resistance Seal was placed on the platform on the left.
Clack!
White light ran from the bottom to the top of one of the fifty-meter pillars.
[Resistance Seal registered.]
Then Lian took out the Spirit Seal and placed it on the central platform.
[Spirit Seal registered.]
One platform remained, and Lian turned the Speed Seal between his fingers, for a moment his eyes moved toward Rodrick, he was still standing calmly.
Clack!
The third Seal locked into its place.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The entire Gate lit up, a wave of golden light covered the field, and a huge wind came out from the arch.
[Three Seals registered.]
[Alliance Contribution: 3 of 3.]
[Highest Contribution confirmed.]
[Crown Point reward is being distributed.]
Separate notifications appeared.
[Direct contribution in registering two Seals confirmed.]
[Lian’s reward: 200 Points.]
[Crown Points: 1194.]
The other members of the group also received Points based on their contribution, but no one had time to check the numbers for long.
The golden surface inside the arch exploded, and light shot into the empty space in front of the Gate, and several hundred meters ahead, the first piece of stone appeared in the air.
Then the second.
The third.
Dozens.
Hundreds.
The stones appeared in the empty space at an incredible speed and locked together one after another.
Clack!
Clack!
Clack!
A straight path several kilometers long formed over the sea of black clouds and continued directly toward the surface of the upside-down mountain.
At the end of it, huge stairs lit up on the body of the mountain, thousands of stairs appeared, and the Crown was at the top of them.
For a few seconds, the entire field watched the scene in silence, the path had opened, and they had entered the final stage of the test.
"Now!
Execute the plan!" Rodrick suddenly shouted, and all the calmness disappeared from his voice.
Lian’s eyes narrowed.
The same mages who had been spread across different points of the field before almost sat down on one knee at the same time.
Their hands and staffs touched the ground, and Mana exploded, the lines that had been hidden inside the stone until that moment lit up under the group’s feet.
"Watch out!" He shouted a warning.
Frost Dominion.
Cold exploded in an instant, and a huge wall of ice rose in front of the group, and one second later hell was unleashed.
Dozens of Mana attacks hit the wall at the same time.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The entire ice wall exploded in a huge blast, and billions of pieces of ice spread across the field.
Even with Lian’s warning, several people had to throw themselves onto the ground.
But this was only the first layer, and four black walls rose from the ground.
Boom!
Boom!
Boom!
Boom!
They surrounded the group from four sides, and that was not the end, the mages spent their Mana again, and chains came out.
Shapes and symbols appeared around them, and it was clear that this was not a simple skill.
Hundreds of glowing chains shot through the walls and rushed toward the members of the group.
[Seven-Layer Prison Array.]
"They prepared it beforehand!" Rindo shouted angrily and knocked away the blade of one of the chains.
"That bastard was buying time from the beginning!" Kain broke another one with his fist.
Marcus created a shield in front of himself.
"Damn it!
That conversation and his backing away were all to complete this Array!"
Everything he had said, all of his actions, and even forcing Darren to bark like a dog were only to buy time and make sure his plan would work.
And it had worked, the path in front of him was now open, and everyone else was trapped in the Array.
"I’m going to kill those bastards!" Ethan did not need any more analysis.
He ran directly toward one of the walls, and on the other side of the field, Rodrick did not stay even for a moment to watch the result.
"Let’s go." His eyes moved toward Elena.
The girl only paused for a moment, turned her head, and through the black walls and Mana explosions, her eyes met Lian’s for a fraction of a second.
The same complicated feeling appeared again, this time there was perhaps even some doubt in it.
But it was only for a moment, then she turned around, and she and her new boyfriend ran toward the central path.
Several of the fastest members of the group also moved with them.
"No, I won’t let—" Kain saw them, he did not want those bastards to get the Crown and take first place in this test.
However, two chains passed beside his head and blocked his path, forcing him to move back and making it impossible for him to follow them.
He clenched his teeth, he wanted to force his way through, but more chains appeared from nowhere.
All the mages in Rodrick’s group had joined together to create this Array and were working together.
Seraphina pulled out her sword, and a slash appeared in the air.
SHRAAAK!
Three chains were cut at the same time, but four more chains took their place.
"This Array isn’t meant to kill us!
They only want to hold us here!" Rindo suddenly understood and looked at Rodrick, who was getting farther away every second.
Lian had reached the same conclusion, in fact, he had understood something even more important.
Rodrick had not underestimated them.
If he thought their group was weak, there was no need for several mages, a prepared Array, seven layers of restraints, and a surprise attack.
He could have attacked directly after the Gate opened.
But he didn’t.
He knew exactly how dangerous this group was.
He respected their strength enough to prepare a complete plan to stop them for several minutes before reaching the field.
"... he didn’t even think for a moment that we were weak." The Student Council President also realized this truth.
Many students underestimated them because of their Levels, but Rodrick had not done that.
Kain sent one of Rodrick’s students flying several meters back with his fist.
"Should we be happy that he respects us?!
We can’t let him take first place!" In fact, this was even worse from his point of view.

chapters.title: Chapter 446: Crown Captured
paragraphs: "Should we be happy that he respects us?! We can’t let him take first place!" In fact, this was even worse from his point of view
That bastard was winning even without underestimating them.
The fight exploded across the entire field.

Ethan fought with two people and slammed his elbow directly into one person’s face, while Marcus blocked another attack with his shield and pushed the second attacker back with a kick at the same time.
Selina raised a wave of water against a huge fire, and hot steam exploded across the field.
Liana raised her hand, the Silvercrest Gryphon dived from the sky, and its claws targeted one of the mages responsible for the Array.
The man had to take his hand off the ground and create a shield, and at the same time one of the Array’s lines went out.
"One!" He shouted.
"Separate the mages from the Array! We don’t need to defeat all of them!" Rindo understood immediately.
Seraphina moved and made another slash, splitting one of the Mana pillars in half.
But even with their progress, Rodrick had already created a large distance.
Very large.
For a moment, Lian looked through the chaos toward the central path.
He and Elena were now near the end of the bridge and had reached the mountain.
Rodrick was the first person to step onto the huge stairs of the upside-down mountain.
His breathing had become heavy, not because of tiredness but because of excitement, he had worked for months to build his current position.
Power.
Resources.
Connections.
The trust of the students.
The fear of his opponents.
All of it was for something more than just becoming Student Council President, he did not want to be one of the best of his generation.
He wanted to be the name people said first when they talked about the new generation.
And today was the best opportunity.
He climbed the stairs two at a time, Elena was several meters behind him, and the higher they went, the stronger the wind became.
The Crown was no longer a small point and was almost the size of a real Crown, floating several meters above a stone platform.
He reached the final step.
Only a few meters remained before he could take first place in this test, and a smile appeared on his face.
Everything had gone according to his plan, the only problem was that he had failed to get three Seals, but it did not matter...the person who has the last smile is the winner.
He had allowed them to open the Gate and bought several minutes, trapped them, and now he had arrived first.
Rodrick raised his hand and closed his fingers around the Crown.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
Golden light covered the entire peak...he had obtained the Crown.
Down the mountain, one of the last prison walls broke under the combined attack of Seraphina and Kain.
But the sound of the light explosion made almost everyone look up, the Crown was no longer floating in the air and was in Rodrick’s hand.
"He got it..." Rindo’s face changed.
"Fuck." Marcus let out a heavy breath.
"That bastard really made it!"
Kain pushed one student aside, and when he saw the Crown in Rodrick’s hand, his face tightened with anger.
"Damn it! That bastard really got the Crown!"
Among all of them, only one person showed almost no reaction.
Lian.
He grabbed one of the Mana chains with his armored hand and broke it with force.
Clack!
Then he slowly raised his head and looked at the Crown.
"Don’t worry."
Kain almost violently turned his head toward him.
"Don’t worry?! How can you be so calm?! We just let that bastard pass right in front of us and take the Crown! We’re losing to him!" He asked in disbelief.
The young Vorhelm said nothing and only looked at the Crown for several seconds, then a short memory of the academy hall appeared in his mind.
"So whoever takes the Crown wins?" A student had asked Silas.
"I said the Crown will become available." And Silas had answered.
Nothing more, he had never once said that taking the Crown was the end of the test.
"No, he only became the first person to reach the Crown." The corner of Lian’s lips rose.
"What difference does it make?" Kain looked at him with a deep frown.
"Professor Silas never said that whoever takes the Crown wins." The young Vorhelm reminded him of the point.
Kain was silent for a moment.
Rindo also suddenly looked at him, and Seraphina remembered something, their eyes narrowed slightly.
And at that exact moment, the entire realm became silent, and then the first notification appeared in front of all the participants.
[Crown captured.]
[Crown Holder: Rodrick Ashen.]
On the peak, Rodrick’s smile became deeper, but the next notification appeared.
[Final Stage has begun.]
His smile stopped for a moment.
[Crown Holder registered as the King.]
[The King’s location will be revealed to all participants.]
[Defeating the King: 500 Points.]
[Capturing the Crown from the King: Allowed.]
[Final Stage Victory Condition:]
[Keep the Crown for 30 minutes.]
[Time Remaining: 30:00.]
The red pillar of light that reached from the Crown to the sky could now be seen from almost every part of the realm.
There was no longer any need for anyone to guess where Rodrick was.
The King was standing at the highest point of the upside-down mountain, and the system was practically shouting his location to every participant.
The effect of the notifications was almost immediate.
On the distant islands, groups that had been looking for each other or for extra points from Sub-Tests only moments ago changed their paths.
Some of the stone bridges became filled with groups of five or ten people.
From another path, nearly twenty students were running toward the Central Gate, and even those who had no real chance of taking the Crown now had enough reason to join this chaos.
Five hundred Points.
For many students, even taking part in defeating Rodrick could raise their final rank by several places.
Kain saw this scene and a smile appeared on his face.
"Well then, we should go after him now, right?" He looked impatiently toward the mountain path and cracked his fists. "If we move right now, we can get up there before half the academy arrives and—"
"No." Lian said calmly.
And for a moment, he thought he had heard wrong, he turned his head toward him.
"No?"
The young Vorhelm looked at the timer.
Then he looked back toward the top of the mountain, Rodrick was only a small figure beside the red light of the Crown from this distance.
"Thirty minutes is a long time, anyone who goes up there now is using Rodrick’s people’s Mana and energy without taking anything away from us."
Kain opened his mouth, but Lian continued.
"I’m not going to spend my own energy to tire out my enemy when hundreds of people are volunteering to do it."
There was silence for a few seconds.
"That sounds pretty unfair." Ethan moved his gaze between Lian and the mountain.
"Yeah, that’s why it’s a good idea." Marcus added.
"I never said it was a bad idea."

chapters.title: Chapter 447: A King Under Siege
paragraphs: Rindo said nothing, his gaze stayed on Lian for a few moments and then moved back to Rodrick.
His logic was correct.
If the only goal was to defeat the King, there was no reason for them to be the first group to attack his defensive wall.
All of them had thought that getting the Crown meant the end, but it turned out that it was only a trap, a trap that Rodrick had fallen into.
However, thinking about it more deeply, that boy was one of the few people who might actually be able to keep the Crown, he was strong himself and he also had a group.
Having the other students attack them and make them tired was a good idea.
But before that, there was still one problem, the Array around them had not been completely destroyed.
The black walls were still standing on three sides of the field, and Mana lines were moving between them.
Every few seconds, a glowing chain also came out of one of the walls and forced them to change their position.
Kain angrily moved closer to one of the walls and pulled his fist back.
Boom!
The black stone shook under the punch.
A crack appeared on its surface, but almost immediately the Mana lines on it lit up and the crack started closing.
"Damn it." He clenched his teeth and raised his fist again, he even wanted to use his skills.
"You’re wasting time." Lian said, these walls were not simple and were made from the power of several mages between Level 25 and 35.
Breaking them was not as easy as punching them, especially because the walls were an Array, which made it even harder.
Kain stopped his fist in the air and slowly turned his head toward him.
"If you have a better way, I’d really like to see it."
The young Vorhelm lowered his gaze toward the ground, an Array was different from a normal skill.
A skill usually started from a person’s body, Mana, or ability and followed a clear path toward its target.
But an Array was more like a network.
Several stable points, Mana flows, secondary cores, and a coordinating structure gathered the power of several people into one system.
This allowed a proper Array to create an effect much stronger than the power of a single mage.
But a network had one weakness, if the right node was cut, it did not matter how powerful the other parts were, the network would fall apart.
For most people, finding such a point among dozens of Mana paths was not easy.
But Lian did not need to guess.
[True Sequence.]
His eyes narrowed slightly, and the world in front of him changed, Mana flows appeared inside the ground like glowing veins.
One path came from the eastern wall, the second came from behind, and he easily found three secondary cores and seven stable points of the Array.
And finally, all the lines met at a seemingly empty point, about twelve meters to their left.
The coordinating core.
"Arrays only look scary when you don’t know where their heart is." A short smile appeared on his face.
"Over there where there is nothing." Kain followed his gaze.

"Apparently, and that’s exactly what makes them smart, I guess they are using some kind of skill or artifact to hide the coordinating core... besides, now that I think about it, they are very skilled at setting up Arrays."
"Rodrick may have intentionally forced them to become as skilled as possible at setting up Arrays, and during this time he trained them a lot in different situations inside the Ruined Realm."
He had always thought that bastard was an arrogant idiot, and during their high school years he really was like that, but it was clear that he had changed.
Why? Change did not happen without a reason.
If he had changed like this, something had definitely happened to him or he had experienced something that caused it.
Anyway, this was not something that mattered to him for now, and the young Vorhelm raised his right hand and Mana gathered in his palm.
[Cataclysm Pulse.]
BOOOOOM!
The destructive wave hit the ground, the stone exploded within several meters, and a deep hole opened in the ground.
For a fraction of a second, something like a polygon-shaped crystal could be seen under the stones.
Then... crack!
The crystal broke and its effect was almost immediate, all the Mana lines around the field flashed at the same time.
Once.
Twice.
Then they went out, and the chains moving in the air turned into particles of light.
The black walls shook, deep cracks spread across them, and a few seconds later, they collapsed one after another.
Boom!
Dust covered the entire area.
Kain only looked at the ruins for a few moments, then very slowly turned back toward Lian.
"You could have done this from the beginning?"
"Yeah."
"And you let us fight these pieces of trash for several minutes?"
"You looked entertained." He looked at his friend’s unhappy expression for a few moments and burst into laughter.
Kain opened his mouth, but no words came out, and in the end he closed it.
The Student Council President was the same, the whole group was the same, and they all gave him an empty look, but said nothing.
What could they say?

With the Array destroyed, there was nothing else between them and the central path, only the terrified and shocked mages were still there, and they still did not understand how the Array had been destroyed.
And getting rid of those few mages was not very difficult for Kain with the help of Rindo, Cassian, and Seraphina.
After that, the group moved to a high point near the entrance of the path, a place from where they could see a large part of the bridge, the mountain stairs, and even the higher platforms.
In the distance, the first wave of attackers had arrived.
About thirty students reached the foot of the mountain almost at the same time from three different paths.
The remaining members of Rodrick’s group had also seen them, but what happened next even made Rindo look more serious.
No chaos formed, and no one ran toward the enemy without a purpose.
"First line, forward." Rodrick’s voice came down from the stairs.
Nearly twelve warriors and defenders stepped forward three steps at almost the same time.
They activated their shields, heavy armor, and defensive skills, forming a human wall at the widest part of the path.
"Second line, keep a distance of three meters and no one moves forward without an order.
The mages and long-range attackers spread out behind them.
"Healers inside the third circle, don’t use Mana for surface wounds. Anyone who can still fight does not get immediate healing."
No argument was heard, and the orders were followed.
"He organized them quickly." The Student Council President said quietly.
Kain crossed his arms over his chest.
"They’re Awakened Ones who have followed him for nine months and have hunted and explored the Ruined Realm with him for a long time, what else did you expect?"
"Third group, left side." At the same moment, Rodrick looked down from the high ground, and several people immediately changed their positions.
"Main pressure will come from that side in five seconds. Don’t defend to hold them there, push them toward the center."
Marcus raised an eyebrow.
Four seconds passed and then... five.
A group of seven people came out from behind the rocks on the left and attacked that section at high speed.
But the defenders were already prepared, two shields moved aside, and the attackers thought they had found an opening and entered.
At that moment, three magic attacks from the opposite angle blocked their path.
They were forced to change direction toward the center, and right there, boom!
A heavy wave of Mana hit them, and two people were immediately pulled out by their protective seals.
"He’s good." Rindo stayed silent for a few moments and had to admit that his rival had good observation and battle skills.
This admission was not easy for Rindo, he did not like what Rodrick had built in the academy.
But disagreeing with someone was not a reason to ignore their abilities.
Rodrick was not just a rich person with a large group, he read the battlefield, noticed pressure, and knew his people.
And most importantly, he knew when not to aim for a complete victory.
However, with all of this, his gaze fell on the tall figure of Lian, no matter how good Rodrick was, it did not make him call that monster strong.
But this boy...was not someone whose abilities could be understood with common sense or compared with others.
And that made him curious...when these two faced each other, what would happen?
At the same time, one of the attackers pulled back, and two of Rodrick’s people wanted to chase him.
"Come back, no one moves more than ten meters away from the defensive line, remember, we’re not here for Points, we’re buying time." He said to his people right there.
The two returned without any complaints.
Lian watched in silence, and a very faint smile appeared on his face, at least his final opponent in this test was not going to be an idiot.
The first wave was almost over, and more than half of the attackers had been eliminated or retreated.
But before Rodrick’s people had a chance to rest, the second group arrived.
This time there were more of them.
From the east, nearly twenty people, from the center, another eleven people, and among them were several upper-year students whose presence was clearly different from the first wave.
The first clash pushed the defensive line back two meters.
Boom!

Breaking them was not as easy as punching them, especially because the walls were an Array, which made it even harder.
Kain stopped his fist in the air and slowly turned his head toward him.
"If you have a better way, I’d really like to see it."
The young Vorhelm lowered his gaze toward the ground, an Array was different from a normal skill.
A skill usually started from a person’s body, Mana, or ability and followed a clear path toward its target.
But an Array was more like a network.
Several stable points, Mana flows, secondary cores, and a coordinating structure gathered the power of several people into one system.
This allowed a proper Array to create an effect much stronger than the power of a single mage.
But a network had one weakness, if the right node was cut, it did not matter how powerful the other parts were, the network would fall apart.
For most people, finding such a point among dozens of Mana paths was not easy.
But Lian did not need to guess.
[True Sequence.]
His eyes narrowed slightly, and the world in front of him changed, Mana flows appeared inside the ground like glowing veins.
One path came from the eastern wall, the second came from behind, and he easily found three secondary cores and seven stable points of the Array.
And finally, all the lines met at a seemingly empty point, about twelve meters to their left.
The coordinating core.
"Arrays only look scary when you don’t know where their heart is." A short smile appeared on his face.
"Over there where there is nothing." Kain followed his gaze.

"Apparently, and that’s exactly what makes them smart, I guess they are using some kind of skill or artifact to hide the coordinating core... besides, now that I think about it, they are very skilled at setting up Arrays."
"Rodrick may have intentionally forced them to become as skilled as possible at setting up Arrays, and during this time he trained them a lot in different situations inside the Ruined Realm."
He had always thought that bastard was an arrogant idiot, and during their high school years he really was like that, but it was clear that he had changed.
Why?
Change did not happen without a reason.
If he had changed like this, something had definitely happened to him or he had experienced something that caused it.
Anyway, this was not something that mattered to him for now, and the young Vorhelm raised his right hand and Mana gathered in his palm.
[Cataclysm Pulse.]
BOOOOOM!
The destructive wave hit the ground, the stone exploded within several meters, and a deep hole opened in the ground.
For a fraction of a second, something like a polygon-shaped crystal could be seen under the stones.
Then... crack!
The crystal broke and its effect was almost immediate, all the Mana lines around the field flashed at the same time.
Once.
Twice.
Then they went out, and the chains moving in the air turned into particles of light.
The black walls shook, deep cracks spread across them, and a few seconds later, they collapsed one after another.
Boom!
Dust covered the entire area.
Kain only looked at the ruins for a few moments, then very slowly turned back toward Lian.
"You could have done this from the beginning?"
"Yeah."
"And you let us fight these pieces of trash for several minutes?"
"You looked entertained." He looked at his friend’s unhappy expression for a few moments and burst into laughter.
Kain opened his mouth, but no words came out, and in the end he closed it.
The Student Council President was the same, the whole group was the same, and they all gave him an empty look, but said nothing.
What could they say?

With the Array destroyed, there was nothing else between them and the central path, only the terrified and shocked mages were still there, and they still did not understand how the Array had been destroyed.
And getting rid of those few mages was not very difficult for Kain with the help of Rindo, Cassian, and Seraphina.
After that, the group moved to a high point near the entrance of the path, a place from where they could see a large part of the bridge, the mountain stairs, and even the higher platforms.
In the distance, the first wave of attackers had arrived.
About thirty students reached the foot of the mountain almost at the same time from three different paths.
The remaining members of Rodrick’s group had also seen them, but what happened next even made Rindo look more serious.
No chaos formed, and no one ran toward the enemy without a purpose.
"First line, forward." Rodrick’s voice came down from the stairs.
Nearly twelve warriors and defenders stepped forward three steps at almost the same time.
They activated their shields, heavy armor, and defensive skills, forming a human wall at the widest part of the path.
"Second line, keep a distance of three meters and no one moves forward without an order.
The mages and long-range attackers spread out behind them.
"Healers inside the third circle, don’t use Mana for surface wounds.
Anyone who can still fight does not get immediate healing."
No argument was heard, and the orders were followed.
"He organized them quickly." The Student Council President said quietly.
Kain crossed his arms over his chest.
"They’re Awakened Ones who have followed him for nine months and have hunted and explored the Ruined Realm with him for a long time, what else did you expect?"
"Third group, left side." At the same moment, Rodrick looked down from the high ground, and several people immediately changed their positions.
"Main pressure will come from that side in five seconds.
Don’t defend to hold them there, push them toward the center."
Marcus raised an eyebrow.
Four seconds passed and then... five.
A group of seven people came out from behind the rocks on the left and attacked that section at high speed.
But the defenders were already prepared, two shields moved aside, and the attackers thought they had found an opening and entered.
At that moment, three magic attacks from the opposite angle blocked their path.
They were forced to change direction toward the center, and right there, boom!
A heavy wave of Mana hit them, and two people were immediately pulled out by their protective seals.
"He’s good." Rindo stayed silent for a few moments and had to admit that his rival had good observation and battle skills.
This admission was not easy for Rindo, he did not like what Rodrick had built in the academy.
But disagreeing with someone was not a reason to ignore their abilities.
Rodrick was not just a rich person with a large group, he read the battlefield, noticed pressure, and knew his people.
And most importantly, he knew when not to aim for a complete victory.
However, with all of this, his gaze fell on the tall figure of Lian, no matter how good Rodrick was, it did not make him call that monster strong.
But this boy...was not someone whose abilities could be understood with common sense or compared with others.
And that made him curious...when these two faced each other, what would happen?
At the same time, one of the attackers pulled back, and two of Rodrick’s people wanted to chase him.
"Come back, no one moves more than ten meters away from the defensive line, remember, we’re not here for Points, we’re buying time." He said to his people right there.
The two returned without any complaints.
Lian watched in silence, and a very faint smile appeared on his face, at least his final opponent in this test was not going to be an idiot.
The first wave was almost over, and more than half of the attackers had been eliminated or retreated.
But before Rodrick’s people had a chance to rest, the second group arrived.
This time there were more of them.
From the east, nearly twenty people, from the center, another eleven people, and among them were several upper-year students whose presence was clearly different from the first wave.
The first clash pushed the defensive line back two meters.
Boom!

chapters.title: Chapter 448: The End of Waiting
paragraphs: The first clash pushed the defensive line two meters back.
Boom!
A large warrior with a double-edged hammer broke one of the defenders’ shields, two others passed through the gap..
"Elena, take the east side." Rodrick’s voice came immediately.
Elena, who had been standing a few meters below the platform until that moment, answered him without looking at him.
"Got it." Mana gathered around her fingers.
But unlike the large and flashy attacks of most mages, what she created was thin and precise.

Six tightly formed strands of mana separated from around her hand, the first wrapped around the wrist of the warrior in front, the man wanted to bring his hammer down, but the path of his hand changed by a few centimeters.
That was enough to make the attack land beside the defender’s shield instead of his head.
The second strand caught another attacker’s leg.
The third hit the blade of a sword and changed the angle of the attack, and the fourth went directly toward the mana shield of the next person.
Clack!
The defensive shield shook for a moment.
Elena moved herself and raised her hand, a thin blade of mana formed in front of her palm.
Slash!
It hit the same weak point of the shield and the shield broke, the student’s Protective Seal activated and his body turned into light.
She did not even look at him disappearing.
The fifth and sixth strands moved from both sides and changed the attacks of two other people at the same time so that they hit each other.
Boom!
Both were thrown backward.
"She has gotten much better." Seraphina, who was standing at the bottom of the mountain, watched the fight carefully.
"Elena?" Kain looked at her.
"Yeah."
Elena had a mage class, but she was not one of those normal elemental mages and her talent was completely special and allowed her to make strands from almost anything and use them like deadly whips.

Of course, it was not like she could make strands from nothing, and she had some special conditions, and as far as she knew, she mostly used mana to make the strands and sometimes combined elements with them.
She did not take her eyes off the girl, controlling several paths at the same time, while also fighting at close range herself, was not easy.
Especially when the battlefield was full of dozens of moving targets, Elena had not only become stronger but her control had also become better, much better.
At the top of the mountain, Rodrick only gave the east side a short look.
His girlfriend had closed the gap, so he turned his attention back to the center.
But Elena’s eyes left the enemies for a moment and looked down the mountain, toward the distant height, where Lian and the others were standing.
Her eyes stayed on his figure for a few seconds.
He still was not coming.
She did not know why this bothered her so much.
Maybe she expected Lian to be the first person to attack Rodrick without thinking.
Maybe she wanted to see his new power.
Or maybe...
No.
She looked away. This was not the time to think about these things.
The second wave had not been broken and had actually turned into a third wave.
More groups from the distant islands had reached the mountain and now the stairs had turned into battlefields in several places.
The light from the skills lit up the sky every few seconds.
Arrows.
Flames.
Summons.
Rocks breaking off from the mountain wall and hitting students, and the sound of Protective Seals activating continued almost without stopping.
For the first time, Rodrick’s group started to retreat, although it was a planned retreat.
The first line moved five meters higher and the second line took its position again, the healers pulled two seriously injured people back.
And Rodrick was still standing at the center of all these movements, until three people broke through the defensive line and all three were above Level 30.
The first was a tall warrior with a round shield and a short sword, the second was a fast spear user and the third was a man with heavy gloves who was going directly toward the Crown.
One of Rodrick’s guards wanted to step forward.
"Stay back." But he said.
The man stopped and he himself came down, the first shield warrior made the first attack and his sword came from the right.
Rodrick only took half a step forward, his hand hit the attacker’s wrist and changed the direction of the sword, at the same time his other fist hit the center of the shield directly.
Boom!
The shield hit its owner’s chest and the man was thrown three meters back, the spear came from behind on the left but he did not even turn his head.
His body turned and his hand grabbed the body of the spear and moved it downward, causing the spearhead to sink into the stone.
Clack!
Rodrick’s knee hit the spear user’s stomach and the air left the man’s lungs.
But the third person had arrived and his heavy fist came directly toward his head and this time he was forced to raise both forearms.
Boom!
The stone under his feet cracked and he took two steps back.
The attacker smiled and thought that they might have a chance to get the Crown.
"Not bad." But Rodrick also gave a very short smile.
The man punched again but instead of defending, his target moved forward, the attack passed beside his cheek and his own fist hit directly between the attacker’s ribs.
Crack!
The man bent over but at the same time the second punch hit his chin and his head was forced upward and the third punch also landed.
Boom!
It hit the center of his chest and at the same time his Protective Seal lit up and the man’s body disappeared into particles of light.
Rodrick did not even stop to watch the result and turned around.
"Close the center’s distance. Two people take Alden’s place, second healer come forward."
As if those few seconds of close combat had never happened.
"Should we go now?" Kain asked.
"No." Lian answered lazily.
"Really?"
"Yeah."
"God."
At the top of the mountain, the number of Rodrick’s people had decreased.
About eight members of his main group had been eliminated and several others were injured.
The mages’ mana was also no longer as much as at the beginning of the stage, the big attacks had become less common and the healers were acting more carefully.
But the structure was still maintained and more importantly, the Crown was still in his hands.
Lian had no reason to hurry because of this, every minute that passed, all the other participants were doing something that he would eventually have to do himself.
Wear them down.
"Now?" Kain asked again.
"No."
"I don’t even know why I keep asking."
At the top of the mountain, a large explosion destroyed part of the stairs.
Three students were thrown downward at the same time, but their Protective Seals activated before they fell.
Rodrick was also no longer completely unharmed and a long cut could be seen on his left forearm, the upper part of his armor was torn and blood was running down from the corner of his eyebrow.
But his eyes were still the same, cold, focused and controlled, even tiredness had not been able to remove his commanding attitude.
Elena also had a small wound on her cheek and one of her sleeves was burned, but the eastern side was still under her control.
Five more students attacked and the girl sent the strands made of mana between them.
One of the attackers jumped upward and the second came forward from below and the third tried to pass through her blind spot.
She did not move back and two strands moved, the path of the first one changed in the air and the second attack hit the stone.
Then the girl suddenly moved forward herself and with a direct palm strike, she threw the third attacker toward the edge of the stairs.
His Protective Seal activated.
A moment later, Elena looked down again, Lian was still there and this made a very slight frown appear between her eyebrows this time.
What was he waiting for? Why was he not attacking himself?
Kain said nothing else and only looked at Lian, hoping that maybe his time had finally come.
"Not yet." But he said without turning his head.
"fuck you."
Liana laughed and even the corner of Rindo’s lips rose slightly, none of them knew what they were waiting for, but if the Special Area had taught them one thing, it was to trust this man.
But the young Vorhelm really had not been waiting just to annoy Kain.
The situation at the top of the mountain had become exactly what he wanted, Rodrick’s group was still dangerous but more tired, fewer in number, with less mana, and the healers were more exhausted.
And dozens of other students who were also injured enough that they could no longer be a complete threat to Lian.
He was not going to hurry for the Crown, in fact he had not even decided to take the Crown, getting it would only be an extra reward.
There were five hundred points for defeating the King.
And more importantly, there was Rodrick himself, he had known for a long time that sooner or later he would have to settle this rivalry between them.
It was better for it to be today.
A place where no family, teacher or outside pressure could come between them.
Lian separated himself from the stone wall he had been leaning against.
Kain looked at him.
"Is it finally time?"
"Yeah, now almost everyone is tired enough, so now its our time"
